1.m: It is based on sacred tradition.

1.s: āmnāyaḥ punar mantrāś ca brāhmaṇāni ca
1.d: आम्नायः पुनर् मन्त्राश् च ब्राह्मणानि च
1.m: Sacred tradition, moreover, consists of mantras and Brāhmaṇas.

1.s: tad yathābrāhmaṇaṃ vidhir evaṃ karmaliṅgā mantrāḥ
1.d: तद् यथाब्राह्मणं विधिर् एवं कर्मलिङ्गा मन्त्राः
1.m: As the Brāhmaṇa directs, such is the rule; in that manner mantras indicate the ritual action.
Likewise mantras follow the indication of the Brāhmaṇa.
In the absence of that, [one follows] authoritative transmission,
because Brāhmaṇas have been lost.
Facing east, he acts in a low voice.
Ending toward the east or north for the gods;
ending toward the south or west for the ancestors.
at least three times for the gods,
Clockwise movement is the practice for the gods;
The gods receive offerings with the utterance of svāhā and the utterance of vaṣaṭ;
the ancestors receive offerings with the utterance of svadhā and obeisance.
Sacrificial grass cut near the root is for the ancestors;

1.s: pra yacha parśum iti darbhāhārāya dātraṃ prayachati
1.d: प्र यछ पर्शुम् इति दर्भाहाराय दात्रं प्रयछति
1.m: With "Hand forth the sickle" [12.3.31a], he gives a sickle to the grass-gatherer.

1.s: oṣadhīr dāntu parvan iti upari parvaṇāṃ lūtvā tūṣṇīm āhṛtya uttarato agner upasādayati
1.d: ओषधीर् दान्तु पर्वन् इति उपरि पर्वणां लूत्वा तूष्णीम् आहृत्य उत्तरतो अग्नेर् उपसादयति
1.m: With "Let them cut the plants at the node" [12.3.31b], having cut them above the nodes, having brought them silently, he sets them down north of the fire.
He should not turn his back to the fire.
He should not step between parts of the sacrifice.
Bending his right knee, he makes an offering.

1.s: yā pūrvā paurṇamāsī sānumatir yā uttarā sā rākā
1.d: या पूर्वा पौर्णमासी सानुमतिर् या उत्तरा सा राका
1.m: The preceding full moon day is Anumati; the succeeding one is Rākā.

1.s: yā pūrvāmāvāsyā sā sinīvālī yā uttarā sā kuhūḥ
1.d: या पूर्वामावास्या सा सिनीवाली या उत्तरा सा कुहूः
1.m: The preceding new moon day is Sinīvālī; the succeeding one is Kuhū.
Saying, "Today is the day of preparation," he eats food suitable for one about to fast,
avoiding honey, salt, meat, and māṣa beans.

1.s: mamāgne varcaḥ iti samidha ādhāya vratam upaiti
1.d: ममाग्ने वर्चः इति समिध आधाय व्रतम् उपैति
1.m: Having placed firewood sticks on the fire with "My splendor, O Agni" [5.3.1], he undertakes the vow,
or with "Thee by vow, O lord of vows" [7.74.4].

1.s: prātarhute agnau karmaṇe vāṃ veṣāya vāṃ sukṛtāya vām iti pāṇī prakṣālyāpareṇāgner darbhān āstīrya teṣūttaram ānaḍuhaṃ rohitaṃ carma prāggrīvam uttaraloma prastīrya pavitre kurute
1.d: प्रातर्हुते अग्नौ कर्मणे वां वेषाय वां सुकृताय वाम् इति पाणी प्रक्षाल्यापरेणाग्नेर् दर्भान् आस्तीर्य तेषूत्तरम् आनडुहं रोहितं चर्म प्राग्ग्रीवम् उत्तरलोम प्रस्तीर्य पवित्रे कुरुते
1.m: When the morning offering has been made into the fire, having washed both hands with "For work [I take] you two, for energy you two, for good deed you two", having strewn darbha grass to the west of the fire, having spread out upon it an ox hide, red, with the neck facing east and the hair upward, he makes two strainers.

1.s: darbhau aprachinnāntau prakṣālyānulomam anumārṣṭi viṣṇor manasā pūte sthaḥ iti
1.d: दर्भौ अप्रछिन्नान्तौ प्रक्षाल्यानुलोमम् अनुमार्ष्टि विष्णोर् मनसा पूते स्थः इति
1.m: Having washed two darbha grass blades with unbroken tips, he wipes them downward with "You two are purified by the thought of Viṣṇu".

2.s: tvaṃ bhūmim aty eṣy ojasā tvaṃ vedyāṃ sīdasi cārur adhvare | tvāṃ pavitram ṛṣayo bharantas tvaṃ punīhi duritāny asmat || iti pavitre antardhāya havir nirvapati devasya tvā savituḥ prasave aśvinor bāhubhyāṃ pūṣṇo hastābhyāṃ juṣṭaṃ nirvapāmi iti
2.d: त्वं भूमिम् अत्य् एष्य् ओजसा त्वं वेद्यां सीदसि चारुर् अध्वरे । त्वां पवित्रम् ऋषयो भरन्तस् त्वं पुनीहि दुरितान्य् अस्मत् ॥ इति पवित्रे अन्तर्धाय हविर् निर्वपति देवस्य त्वा सवितुः प्रसवे अश्विनोर् बाहुभ्यां पूष्णो हस्ताभ्यां जुष्टं निर्वपामि इति
2.m: Interposing the two strainers with "Thou traversest the earth with might; thou sittest pleasing on the altar at the rite. The seers, bringing thee as a strainer, do thou cleanse away evils from us!", he pours out the sacrificial oblation with "At the instigation of divine Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins, with the hands of Pūṣan, I pour out what is agreeable to [the deity]".
Likewise [adding] "to Agni and Soma" [on the full moon day];
[adding] "to Indra and Agni" on the new moon day.

2.s: niruptaṃ pavitrābhyāṃ prokṣati amuṣmai tvā juṣṭam yathādevatam
2.d: निरुप्तं पवित्राभ्यां प्रोक्षति अमुष्मै त्वा जुष्टम् यथादेवतम्
2.m: He besprinkles what has been poured out with the two strainers, with "Agreeable to N.N. [thee]", according to the deity.

2.s: ulūkhalamusalaṃ śūrpaṃ prakṣālitaṃ carmaṇi ādhāya vrīhīn ulūkhala opyāvaghnaṃs trir haviṣkṛtā vācaṃ visṛjati haviṣkṛd ā dravehi iti
2.d: उलूखलमुसलं शूर्पं प्रक्षालितं चर्मणि आधाय व्रीहीन् उलूखल ओप्यावघ्नंस् त्रिर् हविष्कृता वाचं विसृजति हविष्कृद् आ द्रवेहि इति
2.m: Having placed a washed mortar, pestle, and winnowing basket on the hide, having poured the paddy into the mortar, pounding, he utters the call to the oblation-preparer three times: "O oblation-preparer, run hither, come!"

2.s: avahatya suphalīkṛtān kṛtvā triḥ prakṣālya taṇḍulān agne varur yajñiyas tvādhi arukṣat iti carum adhidadhāti
2.d: अवहत्य सुफलीकृतान् कृत्वा त्रिः प्रक्षाल्य तण्डुलान् अग्ने वरुर् यज्ञियस् त्वाधि अरुक्षत् इति चरुम् अधिदधाति
2.m: Having pounded [the grains], having husked them thoroughly, having washed the rice grains three times, he sets on the boiled oblation with "O Agni, the sacrificial vessel has climbed upon thee" [11.1.16].
With "Clean, purified" [11.1.17], he pours in water.
With "Purified by sacred prayer" [11.1.18], [he pours in] the rice grains.

2.s: pari tvāgne puraṃ vayam iti triḥ paryagni karoti
2.d: परि त्वाग्ने पुरं वयम् इति त्रिः पर्यग्नि करोति
2.m: With "Around thee, O Agni, we a rampart" [7.71.1], he carries fire around three times.
With the stirring stick, he stirs clockwise three times.
From then on, according to wish.
He sets down the kindling wood north of the fire;
With "Agreeable to Agni I besprinkle thee", [he besprinkles] the kindling wood;

2.s: darbhamuṣṭim abhyukṣya paścād agneḥ prāgagraṃ nidadhāti ūrṇamradaṃ prathasva svāsasthaṃ devebhyaḥ iti
2.d: दर्भमुष्टिम् अभ्युक्ष्य पश्चाद् अग्नेः प्रागग्रं निदधाति ऊर्णम्रदं प्रथस्व स्वासस्थं देवेभ्यः इति
2.m: Having sprinkled a handful of darbha grass, he places it west of the fire with the tips toward the east, with "Spread wide, soft as wool, a good seat for the gods".

2.s: darbhāṇām apādāya ṛṣīṇāṃ prastaro asi iti dakṣiṇato agner brahmāsanaṃ nidadhāti
2.d: दर्भाणाम् अपादाय ऋषीणां प्रस्तरो असि इति दक्षिणतो अग्नेर् ब्रह्मासनं निदधाति
2.m: Taking from the darbha grasses, with "Thou art the ritual grass bunch of the seers" [16.2.6], he sets down the seat of the Brahman priest south of the fire.

2.s: purastād agner āstīrya teṣāṃ mūlāni apareṣāṃ prāntair avachādayan parisarpati dakṣiṇenāgnim ā paścārdhāt
2.d: पुरस्ताद् अग्नेर् आस्तीर्य तेषां मूलानि अपरेषां प्रान्तैर् अवछादयन् परिसर्पति दक्षिणेनाग्निम् आ पश्चार्धात्
2.m: Having strewn [darbha grass] in front of the fire, covering their roots with the tips of the subsequent ones, he moves around south of the fire as far as the western half.
He gives the order: 'Strew around!'

2.s: devasya tvā savituḥ prasave aśvinor bāhubhyāṃ pūṣṇo hastābhyāṃ prasūtaḥ praśiṣā paristṛṇāmi iti
2.d: देवस्य त्वा सवितुः प्रसवे अश्विनोर् बाहुभ्यां पूष्णो हस्ताभ्यां प्रसूतः प्रशिषा परिस्तृणामि इति
2.m: With: 'At the instigation of god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins, with the hands of Pūṣan, impelled by the command, I strew around.'
In this manner to the north, making an odd number of layers.
Where they meet, he makes that [end] overlap from the south.

2.s: stīrṇaṃ prokṣati haviṣāṃ tvā juṣṭaṃ prokṣāmi iti
2.d: स्तीर्णं प्रोक्षति हविषां त्वा जुष्टं प्रोक्षामि इति
2.m: He besprinkles the strewn grass with: 'Welcome to the sacrificial oblations, I besprinkle you.'
What is strewn should not be put to use unbesprinkled.
Nor a part of the sacrifice unbesprinkled.
Upon it he places the [utensils] that have been washed and air-dried:

2.s: vilīnapūtam ājyaṃ gṛhītvādhiśritya paryagni kṛtvā udag udvāsya paścād agner upasādya udagagrābhyāṃ pavitrābhyām utpunāti
2.d: विलीनपूतम् आज्यं गृहीत्वाधिश्रित्य पर्यग्नि कृत्वा उदग् उद्वास्य पश्चाद् अग्नेर् उपसाद्य उदगग्राभ्यां पवित्राभ्याम् उत्पुनाति
2.m: Having taken ghee that is melted and strained, placed it on the fire, carried fire around [it], removed it toward the north, set it down to the west of the fire, he purifies it by straining with two strainers pointing toward the north:
'You are purified by the thought of Viṣṇu.'
'May god Savitṛ purify you.'

2.s: achidreṇa tvā pavitreṇa śatadhāreṇa sahasradhāreṇa supvot punāmi iti tṛtīyam
2.d: अछिद्रेण त्वा पवित्रेण शतधारेण सहस्रधारेण सुप्वोत् पुनामि इति तृतीयम्
2.m: A third time with: 'With an unbroken strainer of a hundred streams, of a thousand streams, well-cleansed, I purify you.'

2.s: śṛtaṃ havir abhighārayati madhvā samañjan ghṛtavat karātha iti
2.d: शृतं हविर् अभिघारयति मध्वा समञ्जन् घृतवत् कराथ इति
2.m: He bastes the cooked sacrificial oblation with: 'Anointing it with honey, you shall make it full of ghee.'

2.s: abhighārya udañcam udvāsayati ud vāsayāgneḥ śṛtam akarma havyam ā sīda pṛṣṭham amṛtasya dhāma iti
2.d: अभिघार्य उदञ्चम् उद्वासयति उद् वासयाग्नेः शृतम् अकर्म हव्यम् आ सीद पृष्ठम् अमृतस्य धाम इति
2.m: Having basted it, he takes it off toward the north with: 'Remove from the fire; we have made the cooked oblation! Sit on the back, the abode of immortality!'
Having placed it west of the ghee and decorated it, he purifies it by straining in the same manner.
With: 'Stand up...' [he looks at] what belongs to Indra.

2.s: agnir bhūyām iti tisṛbhir upasamādadhāti asmai kṣatrāṇi etam idhmam iti vā
2.d: अग्निर् भूयाम् इति तिसृभिर् उपसमादधाति अस्मै क्षत्राणि एतम् इध्मम् इति वा
2.m: He adds fuel with three [verses], beginning: 'May I become Agni...', or with: 'To him realms...', [or] 'This kindling wood...'

3.s: yunajmi tvā brahmaṇā daivyena havyāyāsmai voḍheva jātavedaḥ | indhānās tvā suprajasaḥ suvīrā jyog jīvema balihṛto vayaṃ te iti
3.d: युनज्मि त्वा ब्रह्मणा दैव्येन हव्यायास्मै वोढेव जातवेदः । इन्धानास् त्वा सुप्रजसः सुवीरा ज्योग् जीवेम बलिहृतो वयं ते इति
3.m: With: 'I yoke you with divine prayer to carry this oblation, O Jātavedas. Kindling you, rich in offspring, rich in heroes, may we live long, bringing you tribute offerings.'

3.s: dakṣiṇato jāṅmāyanam udapātram upasādyābhimantrayate tathodapātraṃ dhāraya yathāgre brahmaṇaspatiḥ | satyadharmā adīdharad devasya savituḥ save iti
3.d: दक्षिणतो जाङ्मायनम् उदपात्रम् उपसाद्याभिमन्त्रयते तथोदपात्रं धारय यथाग्रे ब्रह्मणस्पतिः । सत्यधर्मा अदीधरद् देवस्य सवितुः सवे इति
3.m: Having set down to the south the water vessel [called] Jāṅmāyana, he addresses it with a mantra: 'Hold the water vessel thus, as Bṛhaspati held it in the beginning, true to the cosmic order, at the instigation of god Savitṛ.'

3.s: atha udakam āsiñcati iheta devīr amṛtaṃ vasānā hiraṇyavarṇā anavadyarūpāḥ | āpaḥ samudro varuṇaś ca rājā saṃpātabhāgān haviṣo juṣantām || indrapraśiṣṭā varuṇaprasūtā apaḥ samudrād divam ud vahantu | indrapraśiṣṭā varuṇaprasūtā divas pṛthivyā śriyam ud vahantu iti
3.d: अथ उदकम् आसिञ्चति इहेत देवीर् अमृतं वसाना हिरण्यवर्णा अनवद्यरूपाः । आपः समुद्रो वरुणश् च राजा संपातभागान् हविषो जुषन्ताम् ॥ इन्द्रप्रशिष्टा वरुणप्रसूता अपः समुद्राद् दिवम् उद् वहन्तु । इन्द्रप्रशिष्टा वरुणप्रसूता दिवस् पृथिव्या श्रियम् उद् वहन्तु इति
3.m: Then he pours water into it with: 'Hither, O goddesses, clad in immortality, golden-hued, of irreproachable form! May the waters, the ocean, and king Varuṇa enjoy the residue portions of the sacrificial oblation. Commanded by Indra, impelled by Varuṇa, may the waters convey [blessings] from the ocean to heaven; commanded by Indra, impelled by Varuṇa, may they convey prosperity from heaven to earth.'

3.s: ṛtaṃ tvā satyena pariṣiñcāmi jātavedaḥ iti saha havirbhiḥ paryukṣya jīvābhir ācamya utthāya vedaprapadbhiḥ prapadyate o;m prapadye bhūḥ prapadye bhuvaḥ prapadye svaḥ prapadye janat prapadye iti
3.d: ऋतं त्वा सत्येन परिषिञ्चामि जातवेदः इति सह हविर्भिः पर्युक्ष्य जीवाभिर् आचम्य उत्थाय वेदप्रपद्भिः प्रपद्यते ओ;म् प्रपद्ये भूः प्रपद्ये भुवः प्रपद्ये स्वः प्रपद्ये जनत् प्रपद्ये इति
3.m: Having sprinkled around [the fire] along with the sacrificial oblations with: 'I sprinkle you around with cosmic truth, O order, Jātavedas,' having sipped water with the Jīvā verses [and] stood up, he takes refuge with the Veda-refuge formulas: 'Om, I take refuge in Earth; I take refuge in the Atmosphere; I take refuge in Heaven; I take refuge in the Created.'

3.s: prapadya paścāt stīrṇasya darbhān āstīrya ahe daidhiṣavyod atas tiṣṭhāny asya sadane sīda yo 'smat pākataraḥ iti brahmāsanam anvīkṣate
3.d: प्रपद्य पश्चात् स्तीर्णस्य दर्भान् आस्तीर्य अहे दैधिषव्योद् अतस् तिष्ठान्य् अस्य सदने सीद यो ऽस्मत् पाकतरः इति ब्रह्मासनम् अन्वीक्षते
3.m: Having taken refuge, having spread darbha grass west of what was strewn, he looks at the seat of the Brahman priest with: 'O Daidhiṣavya, stand up from here! Sit on the seat of another who is more inexperienced than we!'

3.s: nirastaḥ parāgvasuḥ saha pāpmanā nirastaḥ so 'stu yo 'smān dveṣṭi yaṃ ca vayaṃ dviṣmaḥ iti dakṣiṇā tṛṇaṃ nirasyati
3.d: निरस्तः पराग्वसुः सह पाप्मना निरस्तः सो ऽस्तु यो ऽस्मान् द्वेष्टि यं च वयं द्विष्मः इति दक्षिणा तृणं निरस्यति
3.m: With: 'Parāgvasu is cast out along with evil; cast out be he who hates us and whom we hate,' he tosses a grass blade to the south.

3.s: tad anvālabhya japati idam aham arvāgvasoḥ sadane sīdāmi ṛtasya sadane sīdāmi satyasya sadane sīdāmi iṣṭasya sadane sīdāmi pūrtasya sadane sīdāmi māmṛṣad deva barhiḥ svāsasthaṃ tvādhyāsadeyam ūrṇamradam anabhiśokam
3.d: तद् अन्वालभ्य जपति इदम् अहम् अर्वाग्वसोः सदने सीदामि ऋतस्य सदने सीदामि सत्यस्य सदने सीदामि इष्टस्य सदने सीदामि पूर्तस्य सदने सीदामि मामृषद् देव बर्हिः स्वासस्थं त्वाध्यासदेयम् ऊर्णम्रदम् अनभिशोकम्
3.m: Touching that [seat], he recites in a low voice: 'Here I sit on the seat of Arvāgvasu; I sit on the seat of the cosmic order; I sit on the seat of truth; I sit on the seat of the sacrifice; I sit on the seat of good works. May the god not harm me; O sacrificial grass, may I sit upon you, who provide a good seat, soft as wool, bringing no sorrow.'

3.s: vimṛgvarīṃ ity upaviśyāsanīyaṃ brahmajapaṃ japati bṛhaspatir brahmā brahmasadana āsiṣyate bṛhaspate yajñaṃ gopāya yad ud udvata un nivataḥ śakeyam iti
3.d: विमृग्वरीं इत्य् उपविश्यासनीयं ब्रह्मजपं जपति बृहस्पतिर् ब्रह्मा ब्रह्मसदन आसिष्यते बृहस्पते यज्ञं गोपाय यद् उद् उद्वत उन् निवतः शकेयम् इति
3.m: Having sat down with: 'The purifying one...', he recites the Brahman priest's mutterings pertaining to the seat: 'Bṛhaspati the Brahman will sit on the Brahman's seat,' 'O Bṛhaspati, protect the sacrifice,' [and] 'That I may be able to ascend the heights, the depths...'

3.s: darbhaiḥ sruvaṃ nirmṛjya niṣṭaptaṃ rakṣo niṣṭaptā arātayaḥ pratyuṣṭaṃ rakṣaḥ pratyuṣṭā arātayaḥ iti pratapya mūle sruvaṃ gṛhītvā japati viṣṇor hasto asi dakṣiṇaḥ pūṣṇā datto bṛhaspateḥ | taṃ tvāhaṃ sruvam ā dade devānāṃ havyavāhanam || ayaṃ sruvo vi dadhāti homān śatākṣarachandasā jāgatena | sarvā yajñasya samanakti viṣṭhā bārhaspatyā iṣṭiḥ śarmaṇā daivyena iti
3.d: दर्भैः स्रुवं निर्मृज्य निष्टप्तं रक्षो निष्टप्ता अरातयः प्रत्युष्टं रक्षः प्रत्युष्टा अरातयः इति प्रतप्य मूले स्रुवं गृहीत्वा जपति विष्णोर् हस्तो असि दक्षिणः पूष्णा दत्तो बृहस्पतेः । तं त्वाहं स्रुवम् आ ददे देवानां हव्यवाहनम् ॥ अयं स्रुवो वि दधाति होमान् शताक्षरछन्दसा जागतेन । सर्वा यज्ञस्य समनक्ति विष्ठा बार्हस्पत्या इष्टिः शर्मणा दैव्येन इति
3.m: Having wiped the dipping spoon with darbha grass, heated it with: 'Burnt is the demon, burnt are the enemies; scorched is the demon, scorched are the enemies,' [and] seized the dipping spoon at its base, he recites in a low voice: 'You are the right hand of Viṣṇu, given by Pūṣan to Bṛhaspati; as such, I take hold of you, the dipping spoon, the bearer of oblations for the gods. / This dipping spoon ordains the offerings with a hundred-syllabled meter, with the Jagatī; it anoints all the stages of the sacrifice, an offering to Bṛhaspati with divine protection.'

3.s: oṃ bhūḥ śaṃ bhūtyai tvā gṛhṇe bhūtaye iti prathamaṃ grahaṃ gṛhṇāti
3.d: ओं भूः शं भूत्यै त्वा गृह्णे भूतये इति प्रथमं ग्रहं गृह्णाति
3.m: With: 'Om, earth! For good fortune, I take you for prosperity,' he takes the first portion.

3.s: oṃ bhuvaḥ śaṃ puṣṭyai tvā gṛhṇe puṣṭaye iti dvitīyam
3.d: ओं भुवः शं पुष्ट्यै त्वा गृह्णे पुष्टये इति द्वितीयम्
3.m: With: 'Om, atmosphere! For good fortune, I take you for nourishment,' the second.

3.s: oṃ svaḥ śaṃ tvā gṛhṇe sahasrapoṣāya iti tṛtīyam
3.d: ओं स्वः शं त्वा गृह्णे सहस्रपोषाय इति तृतीयम्
3.m: With: 'Om, heaven! For good fortune, I take you for thousandfold increase,' the third.

3.s: oṃ jagat śaṃ tvā gṛhṇe aparimitapoṣāya iti caturtham
3.d: ओं जगत् शं त्वा गृह्णे अपरिमितपोषाय इति चतुर्थम्
3.m: With: 'Om, world! For good fortune, I take you for boundless increase,' the fourth.

3.s: rājakarmābhicārikeṣu amuṣya tvā prāṇāya gṛhṇe apānāya vyānāya samānāya udānāya iti pañcamam
3.d: राजकर्माभिचारिकेषु अमुष्य त्वा प्राणाय गृह्णे अपानाय व्यानाय समानाय उदानाय इति पञ्चमम्
3.m: In rites for kings and rites of sorcery, a fifth with: 'For the in-breath of so-and-so I take you, for the out-breath, for the diffused breath, for the equalised breath, for the upward breath.'

3.s: agnāv agniḥ hṛdā pūtam purastād yuktaḥ yajñasya cakṣuḥ iti juhoti
3.d: अग्नाव् अग्निः हृदा पूतम् पुरस्ताद् युक्तः यज्ञस्य चक्षुः इति जुहोति
3.m: He offers with: 'Fire in fire, purified by the heart...', 'Yoked in the east...', [and] 'Eye of the sacrifice...'
West of the fire, in the middle region, in the same place [he offers] the preliminary oblations.
To the south of the fire, into the water vessel, he leads the residue of the ghee oblations.
The preliminary oblation, the ghee portion, the concluding oblation: [this is] the full performance of pacified rites.

4.s: vṛṣṇe bṛhate svarvide agnaye śulkaṃ harāmi tviṣīmate | sa na sthirān balavataḥ kṛṇotu jyok ca no jīvātave dadhāti || agnaye svāhā iti uttarapūrvārdhe āgneyam ājyabhāgaṃ juhoti
4.d: वृष्णे बृहते स्वर्विदे अग्नये शुल्कं हरामि त्विषीमते । स न स्थिरान् बलवतः कृणोतु ज्योक् च नो जीवातवे दधाति ॥ अग्नये स्वाहा इति उत्तरपूर्वार्धे आग्नेयम् आज्यभागं जुहोति
4.m: In the north-eastern half, he offers the ghee portion to Agni with: 'To the bull, the great, the finder of light, to fiery Agni, I bring tribute; may he make us firm and strong, and long may he establish our life! To Agni, svāhā!'

4.s: dakṣiṇapūrvārdhe somāya tvaṃ soma divyo nṛcakṣāḥ sugā;m asmabhyaṃ patho anu khyaḥ | abhi no gotraṃ viduṣa iva neṣo 'chā no vācam uśatīṃ jigāsi || somāya svāhā iti
4.d: दक्षिणपूर्वार्धे सोमाय त्वं सोम दिव्यो नृचक्षाः सुगा;म् अस्मभ्यं पथो अनु ख्यः । अभि नो गोत्रं विदुष इव नेषो ऽछा नो वाचम् उशतीं जिगासि ॥ सोमाय स्वाहा इति
4.m: In the south-eastern half, to Soma with: 'You, O divine Soma, who look upon men, have revealed easy paths for us; lead us to a cattle-pen like a wise guide; you attain our eager speech. To Soma, svāhā!'

4.s: upastīryājyaṃ saṃhatābhyām aṅgulibhyāṃ dvir haviṣo avadyati madhyāt pūrvārdhāt ca
4.d: उपस्तीर्याज्यं संहताभ्याम् अङ्गुलिभ्यां द्विर् हविषो अवद्यति मध्यात् पूर्वार्धात् च
4.m: Having spread an underlayer of ghee, with his fingers joined, he cuts off [portions] twice from the sacrificial oblation: from the middle and from the eastern half.
Having basted what has been cut off with ghee, he bastes the sacrificial oblation in return twice.
From wherever he cuts off, [he bastes] that in succession.
In this way are all the cut-off portions [treated],
except for that belonging to [Agni] Sviṣṭakṛt.

4.s: ud enam uttaraṃ naya iti purastāddhomasaṃhatāṃ pūrvām
4.d: उद् एनम् उत्तरं नय इति पुरस्ताद्धोमसंहतां पूर्वाम्
4.m: With "Lead him up higher" [AVŚ 6.5.1], [he offers the first oblation] contiguous to the preliminary oblation, to the east.
In this way he offers each subsequent [oblation] contiguous to the preceding one.
The oblations are made verse by verse, ending with svāhā.

4.s: yām uttarām agner ājyabhāgasya juhoti rakṣodevatyā sā yāṃ dakṣiṇataḥ somasya pitṛdevatyā sā
4.d: याम् उत्तराम् अग्नेर् आज्यभागस्य जुहोति रक्षोदेवत्या सा यां दक्षिणतः सोमस्य पितृदेवत्या सा
4.m: The one which he offers to the north of Agni's ghee portion belongs to the Rakṣases; that [which he offers] to the south of Soma's belongs to the ancestors.

4.s: tasmād antarā hotavyā devaloke eva hūyante yāṃ hutvā pūrvām aparāṃ juhoti sāpakramantī sa pāpīyān yajamāno bhavati
4.d: तस्माद् अन्तरा होतव्या देवलोके एव हूयन्ते यां हुत्वा पूर्वाम् अपरां जुहोति सापक्रमन्ती स पापीयान् यजमानो भवति
4.m:
Therefore, they should be offered between the two; thus they are offered in the realm of the gods alone.

The one who, having offered the first, offers the next one away from it—that [oblation] steps back; that sacrificer becomes worse off.

4.s: yāṃ parāṃparāṃ saṃhatāṃ juhoti sābhikramantī sa vasīyān yajamāno bhavati
4.d: यां परांपरां संहतां जुहोति साभिक्रमन्ती स वसीयान् यजमानो भवति
4.m: The one who offers each subsequent one contiguous [to the previous]—that [oblation] advances; that sacrificer becomes more prosperous.

4.s: yām anagnau juhoti sāndhā tayā cakṣur yajamānasya mīyate so andhaṃbhāvuko yajamāno bhavati
4.d: याम् अनग्नौ जुहोति सान्धा तया चक्षुर् यजमानस्य मीयते सो अन्धंभावुको यजमानो भवति
4.m: The one which he offers where there is no fire is blind; by it the sacrificer's eyesight is destroyed; that sacrificer becomes blind.

4.s: yāṃ dhūme juhoti sā tamasi hūyate so arocako yajamāno bhavati
4.d: यां धूमे जुहोति सा तमसि हूयते सो अरोचको यजमानो भवति
4.m: The one which he offers in smoke is offered in darkness; that sacrificer loses his appetite.

4.s: yāṃ jyotiṣmati juhoti tayā brahmavarcasī bhavati tasmāt jyotiṣmati hotavyam
4.d: यां ज्योतिष्मति जुहोति तया ब्रह्मवर्चसी भवति तस्मात् ज्योतिष्मति होतव्यम्
4.m: The one which he offers in the flame makes him full of spiritual luster; therefore, one should offer in the flame.

4.s: evam asmai kṣatram agnīṣomau iti agniṣomīyasya
4.d: एवम् अस्मै क्षत्रम् अग्नीषोमौ इति अग्निषोमीयस्य
4.m: In the same manner, [he offers the portions] of the oblation to Agni and Soma with "To him dominion, Agni and Soma" [AVŚ 6.54.2],

5.s: agnīṣomā savedasā sahūtī vanataṃ giraḥ | sa devatrā babhūvathuḥ || yuvam etāni divi rocanāny agniś ca soma sakratū adhattam | yuvaṃ sindhū;mr abhiśaster avadyād agnīṣomāv amuñcataṃ gṛbhītān || agnīśomā ya āhutiṃ yo vāṃ dāśād dhaviśkṛtim | sa prajayā suvīryaṃ viśvam āyur vyaśnavat |
5.d: अग्नीषोमा सवेदसा सहूती वनतं गिरः । स देवत्रा बभूवथुः ॥ युवम् एतानि दिवि रोचनान्य् अग्निश् च सोम सक्रतू अधत्तम् । युवं सिन्धू;म्र् अभिशस्तेर् अवद्याद् अग्नीषोमाव् अमुञ्चतं गृभीतान् ॥ अग्नीशोमा य आहुतिं यो वां दाशाद् धविश्कृतिम् । स प्रजया सुवीर्यं विश्वम् आयुर् व्यश्नवत् ।
5.m: "O Agni and Soma, sharing possessions, invocations together, accept our songs; / you have become among the gods. // You, Agni and Soma, of shared purpose, set these lights in the sky; / you freed the rivers from the curse, from being held captive, O Agni and Soma. // O Agni and Soma, whoever offers oblation to you, who brings sacrificial worship, / may he attain with his offspring heroes' strength and a full span of life."

5.s: indrāgnī rocanā divaḥ pari vājeṣu bhūṣathaḥ | tad vāṃ ceti pra vīryam || śnathad vṛtram uta sanoti vājam indrā yo agnī sahurī saparyāt | irajyantā vasavyasya bhūreḥ sahastamā sahasā vājayantā || indrāgnī asmān rakṣatāṃ yau prajānāṃ prajāvatī | sa prajayā suvīryaṃ viśvam āyur vyaśnavat || gomad dhiraṇyavad vasu yad vām aśvāvad īmahe | indrāgnī vanemahi || svāhā iti
5.d: इन्द्राग्नी रोचना दिवः परि वाजेषु भूषथः । तद् वां चेति प्र वीर्यम् ॥ श्नथद् वृत्रम् उत सनोति वाजम् इन्द्रा यो अग्नी सहुरी सपर्यात् । इरज्यन्ता वसव्यस्य भूरेः सहस्तमा सहसा वाजयन्ता ॥ इन्द्राग्नी अस्मान् रक्षतां यौ प्रजानां प्रजावती । स प्रजया सुवीर्यं विश्वम् आयुर् व्यश्नवत् ॥ गोमद् धिरण्यवद् वसु यद् वाम् अश्वावद् ईमहे । इन्द्राग्नी वनेमहि ॥ स्वाहा इति
5.m: "Indra and Agni, you adorn the lights of heaven along with the prizes; / that heroic power of yours is recognized." / "He will slay Vṛtra and win the prize, who serves Indra and Agni, the victorious ones, / the rulers over abundant wealth, mightiest, invigorating through their might." / "May Indra and Agni protect us, who are rich in offspring for the creatures; / may he attain with his offspring heroes' strength and a full span of life." / "Cattle-rich, gold-rich wealth, with horses, which we ask of you, / may we obtain, O Indra and Agni!" with "Svāhā!"
[These verses are used] for the sacrificial oblation to Indra and Agni on the new moon day.

5.s: prāk sviṣṭakṛtaḥ pārvaṇahomau samṛddhihomāḥ kāmyahomāś ca
5.d: प्राक् स्विष्टकृतः पार्वणहोमौ समृद्धिहोमाः काम्यहोमाश् च
5.m: Prior to the Sviṣṭakṛt [offering], there are the two joint-day oblations, the prosperity oblations, and the wish-granting oblations.
With "Full from behind" [AVŚ 7.80.1] on the full moon day;

5.s: yat te devā akṛṇvan bhāgadheyam ity amāvāsyāyām
5.d: यत् ते देवा अकृण्वन् भागधेयम् इत्य् अमावास्यायाम्
5.m: with "What portion the gods made for you" [AVŚ 7.79.1] on the new moon day.

5.s: ākūtyai tvā svāhā | kāmāya tvā svāhā | samṛdhe tvā svāhā | ākūtyai tvā kāmāya tvā samṛdhe tvā svāhā | ṛcā stomaṃ samardhaya gāyatreṇa rathantaraṃ | bṛhad gāyatravartani || svāhā
5.d: आकूत्यै त्वा स्वाहा । कामाय त्वा स्वाहा । समृधे त्वा स्वाहा । आकूत्यै त्वा कामाय त्वा समृधे त्वा स्वाहा । ऋचा स्तोमं समर्धय गायत्रेण रथन्तरं । बृहद् गायत्रवर्तनि ॥ स्वाहा
5.m: "To Intention, svāhā! To Desire, svāhā! To Prosperity, svāhā! To Intention, to Desire, to Prosperity, svāhā!" / "Make the chant prosper through the verse, the Rathantara through the Gāyatra meter, / the Bṛhat having the course of the Gāyatra, svāhā!"

5.s: pṛthivyām agnaye samanaman iti saṃnatibhiś ca prajāpate na tvad etāny anyaḥ iti ca
5.d: पृथिव्याम् अग्नये समनमन् इति संनतिभिश् च प्रजापते न त्वद् एतान्य् अन्यः इति च
5.m: And with the bowings: "Upon earth they bowed down to Agni" [AVŚ 4.39.1-8], and "O Prajāpati, none other than you [encompasses all these things]" [AVŚ 7.80.3].

5.s: upastīryājyaṃ sarveṣām uttarataḥ sakṛtsakṛd avadāya dvir avattam abhighārayati
5.d: उपस्तीर्याज्यं सर्वेषाम् उत्तरतः सकृत्सकृद् अवदाय द्विर् अवत्तम् अभिघारयति
5.m: Having spread ghee as a base, having cut off once from the northern part of all [oblations], he bastes the cut-off portion twice with ghee,

5.s: ā devānām api panthām aganma yac chaknavāma tad anupravoḍhum | agnir vidvān sa yajāt sa id dhotā so 'dhvarān sa ṛtūn kalpayāti || agnaye sviṣṭakṛte svāhā ity uttarapūrvārdhe avayutaṃ hutvā sarvaprāyaścittīyān homān juhoti
5.d: आ देवानाम् अपि पन्थाम् अगन्म यच् छक्नवाम तद् अनुप्रवोढुम् । अग्निर् विद्वान् स यजात् स इद् धोता सो ऽध्वरान् स ऋतून् कल्पयाति ॥ अग्नये स्विष्टकृते स्वाहा इत्य् उत्तरपूर्वार्धे अवयुतं हुत्वा सर्वप्रायश्चित्तीयान् होमान् जुहोति
5.m: Having offered [the portion] separated in the northeast with "We have reached the path of the gods, so far as we can follow it; / Agni, knowing, shall sacrifice, he alone is the Hotṛ; he shall arrange the rites, he the seasons," [and] "To Agni Sviṣṭakṛt, svāhā!", he offers the all-expiatory oblations:

5.s: svāheṣṭebhyaḥ svāhā | vaṣaḍ aniṣṭebhyaḥ svāhā | bheṣajaṃ sviṣṭyai svāhā | niṣkṛtir duriṣṭyai svāhā | daivībhyas tanūbhyaḥ svāhā | ayāś cāgne 'sy anabhiśastiś ca satyam it tvam ayā asi | ayāsā manasā kṛto 'yās san havyam ūhiṣe | ā no dhehi bheṣajam || svāhā iti | oṃ svāhā bhūḥ svāhā bhuvaḥ svāhā svaḥ svāhoṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ svāhā iti
5.d: स्वाहेष्टेभ्यः स्वाहा । वषड् अनिष्टेभ्यः स्वाहा । भेषजं स्विष्ट्यै स्वाहा । निष्कृतिर् दुरिष्ट्यै स्वाहा । दैवीभ्यस् तनूभ्यः स्वाहा । अयाश् चाग्ने ऽस्य् अनभिशस्तिश् च सत्यम् इत् त्वम् अया असि । अयासा मनसा कृतो ऽयास् सन् हव्यम् ऊहिषे । आ नो धेहि भेषजम् ॥ स्वाहा इति । ओं स्वाहा भूः स्वाहा भुवः स्वाहा स्वः स्वाहों भूर् भुवः स्वः स्वाहा इति
5.m: "To the sacrificed, svāhā! To the un-sacrificed, vaṣaṭ, svāhā! Medicine for good sacrifice, svāhā! Expiation for ill sacrifice, svāhā! To the divine bodies, svāhā!" / "You are Ayās, O Agni, and free from curse; truly you are Ayās; / made Ayās with an Ayās-mind, being Ayās you have carried the oblation; / bestow medicine upon us, svāhā!" / "Oṃ svāhā, bhūḥ svāhā, bhuvaḥ svāhā, svaḥ svāhā, oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ svāhā!"

6.s: yan me skannaṃ manaso jātavedo yad vāskandad dhaviṣo yatrayatra | utpruṣo vipruṣaḥ saṃ juhomi satyāḥ santu yajamānasya kāmāḥ || svāhā iti
6.d: यन् मे स्कन्नं मनसो जातवेदो यद् वास्कन्दद् धविषो यत्रयत्र । उत्प्रुषो विप्रुषः सं जुहोमि सत्याः सन्तु यजमानस्य कामाः ॥ स्वाहा इति
6.m: With: "Whatever of my oblation has spilled from the mind, O Jātavedas, or whatever spilled from the oblation anywhere, / I offer up the spurting and spraying drops; may the desires of the sacrificer come true, svāhā!"

6.s: yan me skannaṃ yad asmṛti iti ca skannāsmṛtihomau
6.d: यन् मे स्कन्नं यद् अस्मृति इति च स्कन्नास्मृतिहोमौ
6.m: With "Whatever of mine has spilled" and "What through forgetfulness" [AVŚ 7.106.1], there are the two oblations for what has spilled and for what was forgotten.

6.s: yad adya tvā prayati iti saṣthitahomāḥ
6.d: यद् अद्य त्वा प्रयति इति सष्थितहोमाः
6.m: With "If today at your setting forth" [AVŚ 7.97.1-8], there are the oblations for what has been completed.

6.s: manasas pate iti uttamaṃ caturgṛhītena
6.d: मनसस् पते इति उत्तमं चतुर्गृहीतेन
6.m: With "O Lord of the mind" [AVŚ 7.97.8], [he offers] the last [oblation] with four ladlefuls [of ghee].

6.s: barhir ājyaśeṣe anakti
6.d: बर्हिर् आज्यशेषे अनक्ति
6.m: He anoints the sacrificial grass with the residue of the ghee:

6.s: pṛthivyai tvā iti mūlam antarikṣāya tvā iti madhyaṃ dive tvā iti agram evaṃ triḥ
6.d: पृथिव्यै त्वा इति मूलम् अन्तरिक्षाय त्वा इति मध्यं दिवे त्वा इति अग्रम् एवं त्रिः
6.m: the root with "To the earth, you [I anoint]", the middle with "To the intermediate space, you [I anoint]", the tip with "To heaven, you [I anoint]"—in this way three times.

6.s: saṃ barhir aktam ity anupraharati yathādevatam
6.d: सं बर्हिर् अक्तम् इत्य् अनुप्रहरति यथादेवतम्
6.m: He throws [it] in following [the oblations] according to its deity, with "The sacrificial grass, anointed" [AVŚ 7.98.1].

6.s: sruvam agnau dhārayati
6.d: स्रुवम् अग्नौ धारयति
6.m: He holds the dipping spoon over the fire.

6.s: yad ājyadhānyāṃ tat saṃsrāvayati saṃsrāvabhāgās taviṣā bṛhantaḥ prastareṣṭhā barhiṣadaś ca devāḥ | imaṃ yajñam abhi viśve gṛṇantaḥ svāhā devā amṛtā mādayantām || iti
6.d: यद् आज्यधान्यां तत् संस्रावयति संस्रावभागास् तविषा बृहन्तः प्रस्तरेष्ठा बर्हिषदश् च देवाः । इमं यज्ञम् अभि विश्वे गृणन्तः स्वाहा देवा अमृता मादयन्ताम् ॥ इति
6.m: Whatever is in the ghee vessel, he causes to flow together into [the fire] with "Sharing in the confluent flow, mighty, great, standing on the prastara and sitting on the sacrificial grass, the gods, / all rejoicing at this sacrifice, svāhā, may the immortal gods delight!"

6.s: sruvo 'si ghṛtād aniśitaḥ sapatnakṣayaṇo divi ṣīda | antarikṣe sīda pṛthivyāṃ sīdottaro 'haṃ bhūyāsam adhare matsapatnāḥ iti sruvaṃ prāgdaṇḍaṃ nidadhāti
6.d: स्रुवो ऽसि घृताद् अनिशितः सपत्नक्षयणो दिवि षीद । अन्तरिक्षे सीद पृथिव्यां सीदोत्तरो ऽहं भूयासम् अधरे मत्सपत्नाः इति स्रुवं प्राग्दण्डं निदधाति
6.m: He sets down the dipping spoon with its handle pointing east, with "You are the dipping spoon, unblunted by ghee, destroying rivals; sit in heaven, / sit in the intermediate space, sit on earth; may I be superior, lower be my rivals!"

6.s: vi muñcāmi brahmaṇā jātavedasam agniṃ hotāram ajaraṃ rathaspṛtam | sarvā devānāṃ janimāni vidvān yathābhāgaṃ vahatu havyam agniḥ || agnaye svāhā iti samidham ādadhāti
6.d: वि मुञ्चामि ब्रह्मणा जातवेदसम् अग्निं होतारम् अजरं रथस्पृतम् । सर्वा देवानां जनिमानि विद्वान् यथाभागं वहतु हव्यम् अग्निः ॥ अग्नये स्वाहा इति समिधम् आदधाति
6.m: With "I release Jātavedas with the sacred word, Agni the Hotṛ, unaging, chariot-rescuing; / knowing all the births of the gods, let Agni carry the oblation according to each one's share; / to Agni, svāhā!" he places a firewood stick [on the fire].

6.s: edho 'si iti dvitīyāṃ samid asi iti tṛtīyam
6.d: एधो ऽसि इति द्वितीयां समिद् असि इति तृतीयम्

6.s: tejo 'si iti mukhaṃ vimārṣṭi
6.d: तेजो ऽसि इति मुखं विमार्ष्टि

6.s: dakṣiṇenāgniṃ trīn viṣṇukramān kramate viṣṇoḥ kramo 'si iti dakṣiṇena pādenānusaṃharati savyam
6.d: दक्षिणेनाग्निं त्रीन् विष्णुक्रमान् क्रमते विष्णोः क्रमो ऽसि इति दक्षिणेन पादेनानुसंहरति सव्यम्
6.m: To the south of the fire he strides the three Viṣṇu strides with "Viṣṇu's stride are you" [AVŚ 10.5.25-27]; with the right foot he draws up the left.

6.s: sūryasyāvṛtam ity abhidakṣiṇam āvartate
6.d: सूर्यस्यावृतम् इत्य् अभिदक्षिणम् आवर्तते
6.m: With "The sun's turn" [AVŚ 10.5.37], he turns around clockwise.

6.s: aganma svaḥ ity ādityam īkṣate
6.d: अगन्म स्वः इत्य् आदित्यम् ईक्षते
6.m: With "We have gone to heaven" [AVŚ 16.9.3-4], he looks at the sun.

6.s: indrasya vacasā vayaṃ mitrasya varuṇasya ca | brahmaṇā sthāpitaṃ pātraṃ punar utthāpayāmasi || ity apareṇāgnim udapātraṃ parihṛtyottareṇāgnim āpo hi ṣṭhā mayobhuvaḥ iti mārjayitvā barhiṣi patnyāñjalau ninayati samudraṃ vaḥ pra hiṇomi iti idaṃ janāsaḥ ? iti vā
6.d: इन्द्रस्य वचसा वयं मित्रस्य वरुणस्य च । ब्रह्मणा स्थापितं पात्रं पुनर् उत्थापयामसि ॥ इत्य् अपरेणाग्निम् उदपात्रं परिहृत्योत्तरेणाग्निम् आपो हि ष्ठा मयोभुवः इति मार्जयित्वा बर्हिषि पत्न्याञ्जलौ निनयति समुद्रं वः प्र हिणोमि इति इदं जनासः ? इति वा
6.m: With the mantra, 'By Indra's word we, and by Mitra's and Varuṇa's, raise up again the vessel placed by the Brahman,' having carried the water vessel around to the west of the fire, having sprinkled [himself] to the north of the fire with 'Waters indeed are ye, wholesome,' he pours [it] out upon the sacrificial grass into the joined hands of the wife with 'I send you forth to the sea,' or with 'This, O people.'

6.s: vīrapatny ahaṃ bhūyāsam iti mukhaṃ vimārṣṭi
6.d: वीरपत्न्य् अहं भूयासम् इति मुखं विमार्ष्टि
6.m: With 'May I be the wife of a hero,' she wipes her face.

6.s: vratāni vratapataye iti samidham ādadhāti
6.d: व्रतानि व्रतपतये इति समिधम् आदधाति
6.m:
With 'Vows to the lord of vows,' he places a firewood stick [on the fire].

Having sprinkled around with 'Truth with order,' he removes the remnants of the sacrificial oblation towards the north.

6.s: satyaṃ tvartena iti pariṣicya udañci havirucchiṣṭāny udvāsayati
6.d: सत्यं त्वर्तेन इति परिषिच्य उदञ्चि हविरुच्छिष्टान्य् उद्वासयति

6.s: pūrṇapātraṃ dakṣiṇā
6.d: पूर्णपात्रं दक्षिणा

6.s: nādakṣiṇaṃ haviḥ kurvīta yaḥ kurute kṛtyām ātmanaḥ kurute iti brāhmaṇam
6.d: नादक्षिणं हविः कुर्वीत यः कुरुते कृत्याम् आत्मनः कुरुते इति ब्राह्मणम्
6.m: 'One should not make a sacrificial oblation devoid of a fee; whoever makes [it so] makes sorcery against himself'—thus says the Brāhmaṇa.

6.s: anvāhāryaṃ brāhmaṇān bhojayati
6.d: अन्वाहार्यं ब्राह्मणान् भोजयति
6.m: He feeds Brahmins with the anvāhārya cooked rice.

6.s: yad vai yajñasyānanvitaṃ bhavati tad anvāhāryeṇānvāhriyate
6.d: यद् वै यज्ञस्यानन्वितं भवति तद् अन्वाहार्येणान्वाह्रियते
6.m: 'Whatever is deficient in the sacrifice, that is supplemented by the anvāhārya.

6.s: etad anvāhāryasyānvāhāryatvam
6.d: एतद् अन्वाहार्यस्यान्वाहार्यत्वम्
6.m: This is the nature of the anvāhārya to supplement.

6.s: īḍyā vā anye devāḥ saparyeṇyā anye | devā īḍyā devā brāhmaṇāḥ saparyeṇyāḥ
6.d: ईड्या वा अन्ये देवाः सपर्येण्या अन्ये । देवा ईड्या देवा ब्राह्मणाः सपर्येण्याः
6.m: Some gods indeed are to be praised; others are to be served. The gods are to be praised; the Brahmin gods are to be served.

6.s: yajñena eva īḍyān prīṇāti anvāhāryeṇa saparyeṇyān
6.d: यज्ञेन एव ईड्यान् प्रीणाति अन्वाहार्येण सपर्येण्यान्
6.m: By the sacrifice one pleases those to be praised; by the anvāhārya those to be served.

6.s: te asya ubhe prītā yajñe bhavantīti
6.d: ते अस्य उभे प्रीता यज्ञे भवन्तीति
6.m: Both become pleased in his sacrifice'—[thus it is said].

6.s: imau darśapūrṇamāsau vyākhyātau
6.d: इमौ दर्शपूर्णमासौ व्याख्यातौ
6.m: These new and full moon sacrifices are explained.

6.s: darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ pākayajñāḥ
6.d: दर्शपूर्णमासाभ्यां पाकयज्ञाः
6.m: By the new and full moon sacrifices, the domestic sacrifices [are explained].

6.s: kumbhīpākād eva vyuddhāraṃ juhuyāt
6.d: कुम्भीपाकाद् एव व्युद्धारं जुहुयात्
6.m: He should offer portions taken out directly from the pot-cooked dish.

6.s: adhiśrayaṇa paryagnikaraṇa abhighāraṇa udvāsana alaṃkaraṇa utpavanaiḥ saṃskṛtya
6.d: अधिश्रयण पर्यग्निकरण अभिघारण उद्वासन अलंकरण उत्पवनैः संस्कृत्य
6.m: Having prepared [it] by placing on the fire, carrying fire around, basting with ghee, removing from the fire, garnishing, and purifying by straining.

6.s: athāpi ślokau bhavataḥ ājyabhāgāntaṃ prāktantram ūrdhvaṃ sviṣṭakṛtā saha | havīṃṣi yajña āvāpo yathā tantrasya tantavaḥ || pākayajñān samāsādya ekājyān ekabarhiṣaḥ | ekasviṣṭakṛtaḥ kuryāt nānāpi sati daivate iti |
6.d: अथापि श्लोकौ भवतः आज्यभागान्तं प्राक्तन्त्रम् ऊर्ध्वं स्विष्टकृता सह । हवींषि यज्ञ आवापो यथा तन्त्रस्य तन्तवः ॥ पाकयज्ञान् समासाद्य एकाज्यान् एकबर्हिषः । एकस्विष्टकृतः कुर्यात् नानापि सति दैवते इति ।
6.m: And moreover, there are two verses: 'Ending with the ghee portions is the introductory framework; what follows is together with the Sviṣṭakṛt; the sacrificial oblations inserted into the sacrifice are like the threads of a web.' / 'Having brought together the domestic sacrifices, one should make them have a single ghee [offering], a single sacrificial grass [bed], and a single Sviṣṭakṛt, even when the deities are various.'

6.s: etena evāmāvāsyo vyākhyātaḥ
6.d: एतेन एवामावास्यो व्याख्यातः
6.m: By this very [procedure] the new moon sacrifice is explained.

6.s: aindrāgno atra dvitīyo bhavati
6.d: ऐन्द्राग्नो अत्र द्वितीयो भवति
6.m: Here the second [cake] belongs to Indra-Agni.

6.s: tayor vyatikrame tvam agne vratapā asi kāmas tad agre iti śāntāḥ
6.d: तयोर् व्यतिक्रमे त्वम् अग्ने व्रतपा असि कामस् तद् अग्रे इति शान्ताः
6.m: In case of an omission of those two, the pacifying [formulas] are: 'Thou, O Agni, art the keeper of vows,' and 'Desire was in the beginning.'

7.m: He eats [the remnant]; in the absence of a specific instruction, a pot-cooked rice dish [is used].
In rites for prosperity, [milk] from a cow with a calf of identical colour [is used].
He casts in rice, barley, and sesame.
He consumes milk-rice, sacrificial cakes, and ritual fluids.
He gives a mash beverage and boiled rice.
At an injunction of water, one should understand the water vessel.
He procures ritual equipment from the east [or] from the north.
From trees out of reach of a cow.
The performance of rites in the wilderness is towards the east or towards the north.

7.s: uttarata udakānte prayujya karmāṇy apāṃ sūktair āplutya pradakṣiṇam āvṛtya apa upaspṛśyānavekṣamāṇā grāmam udāvrajanti
7.d: उत्तरत उदकान्ते प्रयुज्य कर्माण्य् अपां सूक्तैर् आप्लुत्य प्रदक्षिणम् आवृत्य अप उपस्पृश्यानवेक्षमाणा ग्रामम् उदाव्रजन्ति
7.m: Having performed rites towards the north at the edge of the water, having bathed with the water hymns, having turned clockwise, having touched water, they return up to the village without looking back.
Things to be fed, bound on, bathed with, ridden, or eaten receive residues of oblations.
All are to be consecrated with mantras.

7.s: strīvyādhitāv āplutāvasiktau śirastaḥ prakramyā prapadāt pramārṣṭi
7.d: स्त्रीव्याधिताव् आप्लुतावसिक्तौ शिरस्तः प्रक्रम्या प्रपदात् प्रमार्ष्टि
7.m: A woman and a sick person, bathed and washed, he wipes down starting from the head down to the tip of the feet.
Having first made [the recipient] step forward, he gives [the object].
Having steeped [amulets] in curd and honey on three [days] beginning with the thirteenth [tithi], he binds them on.
Consecration with mantras and oblations are performed while [the beneficiary] is touching from behind.
The preparation of sacrificial oblations takes place behind the fire on an ox hide.
He also makes [them] sip water from the bathing and pouring waters.
He eats of [substances] possessing residues of oblations, or anoints himself.
He directs the smoke of things to be placed upon [the fire].

8.s: purastāddhomavatsu niśākarmasu pūrvāhṇe yajñopavītī śālāniveśamaṃ samūhayaty upavatsyadbhaktam aśitvā snāto ahatavasanaḥ prayuṅkte
8.d: पुरस्ताद्धोमवत्सु निशाकर्मसु पूर्वाह्णे यज्ञोपवीती शालानिवेशमं समूहयत्य् उपवत्स्यद्भक्तम् अशित्वा स्नातो अहतवसनः प्रयुङ्क्ते
8.m: In night rites that have preliminary oblations, wearing the sacred thread over the left shoulder in the forenoon, he sweeps the entrance of the house; having eaten the meal of one about to fast, bathed, and wearing unwashed clothes, he performs [the rite].
He presents directional tribute offerings to those to whom offerings are made.
Everywhere the base [utensil used] is the sacrificial fee for the performer.
Immediately contiguous [rites/items] are identical and joined.

8.s: pra yacha parśum iti darbhalavanaṃ prayachati
8.d: प्र यछ पर्शुम् इति दर्भलवनं प्रयछति
8.m: With 'Reach forth the sickle,' he hands over the sickle for cutting darbha grass.
With the mantra 'yat tvā śikvaḥ' [AV 10.6.3], he washes [it].
With the mantra 'yat-yat kṛṣṇaḥ' [AV 12.3.13], he performs what is stated in the mantra.

8.s: palāśa udumbara jambu kāmpīla srag vaṅgha śirīṣa sraktya varaṇa bilva jaṅgiḍa kuṭaka garhya galāvala vetasa śimbala sipuna syandana araṇikā aśmayokta tunyu pūtudāravaḥ śāntāḥ
8.d: पलाश उदुम्बर जम्बु काम्पील स्रग् वङ्घ शिरीष स्रक्त्य वरण बिल्व जङ्गिड कुटक गर्ह्य गलावल वेतस शिम्बल सिपुन स्यन्दन अरणिका अश्मयोक्त तुन्यु पूतुदारवः शान्ताः
8.m: Palāśa, udumbara, jambu, kāmpīla, sragvaṅgha, śirīṣa, sraktya, varaṇa, bilva, jaṅgiḍa, kuṭaka, garhya, galāvala, vetasa, śimbala, sipuna, syandana, araṇikā, aśmayokta, tunyu, and pūtudāru are pacified [trees].

8.s: citi prāyaścitti śamī śamakā savaṃśā śāmyavākā talāśa palāśa vāśā śiṃśapā śimbala sipuna darbha apāmārga ākṛtiloṣṭa valmīkavapā dūrvāprānta vrīhi yavāḥ śāntāḥ
8.d: चिति प्रायश्चित्ति शमी शमका सवंशा शाम्यवाका तलाश पलाश वाशा शिंशपा शिम्बल सिपुन दर्भ अपामार्ग आकृतिलोष्ट वल्मीकवपा दूर्वाप्रान्त व्रीहि यवाः शान्ताः
8.m: Citi, prāyaścitti, śamī, śamakā, savaṃśā, śāmyavākā, talāśa, palāśa, vāśā, śiṃśapā, śimbala, sipuna, darbha, apāmārga, an clod of prescribed shape, earth from a termite mound, tips of dūrvā grass, rice, and barley are pacified [plants and substances].

8.s: pramanda uśīra śalalī upadhāna śakadhūmā jarantaḥ
8.d: प्रमन्द उशीर शलली उपधान शकधूमा जरन्तः
8.m: Pramanda, uśīra, porcupine quill, upadhāna, and dried cowdung are old [calmative materials].
Lead, river-lead, iron filings, and a chameleon's head are calming [substances].
Curds, ghee, honey, and water are the ritual fluids.

8.s: vrīhi yavā godhūma upavāka tila priyaṅgu śyāmākā iti miśradhānyāni
8.d: व्रीहि यवा गोधूम उपवाक तिल प्रियङ्गु श्यामाका इति मिश्रधान्यानि
8.m: Rice, barley, wheat, upavāka, sesame, panic-seed, and millet are mixed grains.
He should append the concluding formulas according to the purpose.

8.s: ihaiva dhruvām eha yātu yamo mṛtyuḥ satyaṃ bṛhat ity anuvāko vāstoṣpatīyāni
8.d: इहैव ध्रुवाम् एह यातु यमो मृत्युः सत्यं बृहत् इत्य् अनुवाको वास्तोष्पतीयानि
8.m: The hymns 'ihaiva dhruvām' [AV 3.12], 'eha yātu' [AV 6.73], 'yamo mṛtyuḥ' [AV 6.93], and the section 'satyaṃ bṛhat' [AV 12.1] are the ones relating to the lord of the homestead.

8.s: divyo gandharvaḥ imaṃ me agne yau te mātā iti mātṛnāmāni
8.d: दिव्यो गन्धर्वः इमं मे अग्ने यौ ते माता इति मातृनामानि
8.m: 'divyo gandharvaḥ' [AV 2.2], 'imaṃ me agne' [AV 6.111], and 'yau te mātā' [AV 8.6] are the maternal demon hymns.

8.s: stuvānam idaṃ haviḥ nissālām arāyakṣayaṇam śaṃ no devī pṛśniparṇī ā paśyati tānt satyaujāḥ tvayā pūrvam purastād yuktaḥ rakṣohaṇam iti anuvākaś cātanāni
8.d: स्तुवानम् इदं हविः निस्सालाम् अरायक्षयणम् शं नो देवी पृश्निपर्णी आ पश्यति तान्त् सत्यौजाः त्वया पूर्वम् पुरस्ताद् युक्तः रक्षोहणम् इति अनुवाकश् चातनानि
8.m: 'stuvānam' [AV 1.7], 'idaṃ haviḥ' [AV 1.8], 'nissālām' [AV 2.14], 'arāyakṣayaṇam' [AV 2.18.3], 'śaṃ no devī pṛśniparṇī' [AV 2.25], 'ā paśyati' [AV 4.20], 'tānt satyaujāḥ' [AV 4.36], 'tvayā pūrvam' [AV 4.37], 'purastād yuktaḥ' [AV 5.29], and the section 'rakṣohaṇam' [AV 8.3–4] are the expulsion hymns.

9.s: ambayo yanti śaṃbhumayobhū hiraṇyavarṇāḥ nissālām ye agnayaḥ brahma jajñānam ity ekā uta devāḥ mṛgārasūktāny uttamaṃ varjayitvā apa naḥ śośucad agham punantu mā sasruṣīḥ himavataḥ prasravanti vāyoḥ pūtaḥ pavitreṇa śaṃ ca no mayaś ca naḥ anaḍudbhyas tvaṃ prathamaṃ mahyam āpaḥ vaiśvānaro raśmibhiḥ yamo mṛtyuḥ viśvajit saṃjñānam naḥ yady antarikṣe punar maitv indriyam śivā naḥ śaṃ no vāto vātu agniṃ brūmo vanaspatīn iti
9.d: अम्बयो यन्ति शंभुमयोभू हिरण्यवर्णाः निस्सालाम् ये अग्नयः ब्रह्म जज्ञानम् इत्य् एका उत देवाः मृगारसूक्तान्य् उत्तमं वर्जयित्वा अप नः शोशुचद् अघम् पुनन्तु मा सस्रुषीः हिमवतः प्रस्रवन्ति वायोः पूतः पवित्रेण शं च नो मयश् च नः अनडुद्भ्यस् त्वं प्रथमं मह्यम् आपः वैश्वानरो रश्मिभिः यमो मृत्युः विश्वजित् संज्ञानम् नः यद्य् अन्तरिक्षे पुनर् मैत्व् इन्द्रियम् शिवा नः शं नो वातो वातु अग्निं ब्रूमो वनस्पतीन् इति
9.m: 'ambayo yanti' [AV 1.4], 'śaṃbhumayobhū' [AV 1.5–6], 'hiraṇyavarṇāḥ' [AV 1.33], 'nissālām' [AV 2.14], 'ye agnayaḥ' [AV 3.21.1–7], the single stanza 'brahma jajñānam' [AV 4.1.1], 'uta devāḥ' [AV 4.13], the Mṛgāra hymns except the last [AV 4.23–29], 'apa naḥ śośucad agham' [AV 4.33], 'punantu mā' [AV 6.19], 'sasruṣīḥ' [AV 6.23], 'himavataḥ prasravanti' [AV 6.24], 'vāyoḥ pūtaḥ pavitreṇa' [AV 6.51], 'śaṃ ca no mayaś ca naḥ' [AV 6.57.3], 'anaḍudbhyas tvaṃ prathamaṃ' [AV 6.59], 'mahyam āpaḥ' [AV 6.61], 'vaiśvānaro raśmibhiḥ' [AV 6.62], 'yamo mṛtyuḥ' [AV 6.93], 'viśvajit' [AV 6.107], 'saṃjñānaṃ naḥ' [AV 7.52], 'yady antarikṣe' [AV 7.66], 'punar maitv indriyam' [AV 7.67], 'śivā naḥ' [AV 7.68.3], 'śaṃ no vāto vātu' [AV 7.69], and 'agniṃ brūmo vanaspatīn' [AV 11.6]—
With 'pṛthivyai śrotrāya' [AV 6.10], he pours [the water] back three times.

9.s: ambayo yanti śaṃbhumayobhū hiraṇyavarṇāḥ śaṃtatīyaṃ ca yady antarikṣe punar maitv indriyam śivā naḥ śaṃ no vāto vātu agniṃ brūmo vanaspatīn iti
9.d: अम्बयो यन्ति शंभुमयोभू हिरण्यवर्णाः शंततीयं च यद्य् अन्तरिक्षे पुनर् मैत्व् इन्द्रियम् शिवा नः शं नो वातो वातु अग्निं ब्रूमो वनस्पतीन् इति
9.m: 'ambayo yanti' [AV 1.4], 'śaṃbhumayobhū' [AV 1.5–6], 'hiraṇyavarṇāḥ' [AV 1.33], and the Śaṃtatīya hymn [AV 4.13], 'yady antarikṣe' [AV 7.66], 'punar maitv indriyam' [AV 7.67], 'śivā naḥ' [AV 7.68.3], 'śaṃ no vāto vātu' [AV 7.69], and 'agniṃ brūmo vanaspatīn' [AV 11.6]—
With 'pṛthivyai śrotrāya' [AV 6.10], he pours [the water] back three times.

9.s: ubhayataḥ sāvitry ubhayataḥ śaṃ no devī
9.d: उभयतः सावित्र्य् उभयतः शं नो देवी
9.m: On both sides is the Sāvitrī verse, on both sides is 'śaṃ no devī' [AV 1.6].
Wearing unwashed clothes, he prepares pacifying water in a bronze bowl.

9.s: atisṛṣṭo apāṃ vṛṣabhaḥ ity apo atisṛjya sarvā imā āpa oṣadhaya iti pṛṣṭvā sarvā ity ākhyāta oṃ bṛhaspatiprasūtaḥ karavāṇīty anujñāpya oṃ savitṛprasūtaḥ kurutāṃ bhavān ity anujñātaḥ kurvīta
9.d: अतिसृष्टो अपां वृषभः इत्य् अपो अतिसृज्य सर्वा इमा आप ओषधय इति पृष्ट्वा सर्वा इत्य् आख्यात ओं बृहस्पतिप्रसूतः करवाणीत्य् अनुज्ञाप्य ओं सवितृप्रसूतः कुरुतां भवान् इत्य् अनुज्ञातः कुर्वीत
9.m: Having dispatched the water with 'atisṛṣṭo apāṃ vṛṣabhaḥ' [AV 16.1.1], having asked: 'Are all these water and plants?', once declared 'all', having obtained authorization saying 'Om, impelled by Bṛhaspati I shall act', he should perform it when authorized: 'Om, impelled by Savitṛ may you act'.

9.s: pūrvayā kurvīteti gārgya pārthaśravasa bhāgāli kāṅkāyana uparibabhrava kauśika jāṭikāyana kaurupathayaḥ
9.d: पूर्वया कुर्वीतेति गार्ग्य पार्थश्रवस भागालि काङ्कायन उपरिबभ्रव कौशिक जाटिकायन कौरुपथयः
9.m: 'He should perform it with the former [set],' say Gārgya, Pārthaśravasa, Bhāgāli, Kāṅkāyana, Uparibabhru, Kauśika, Jāṭikāyana, and the Kaurupathis.

9.s: anyatarayā kurvīteti yuvā kauśiko yuvā kauśikaḥ
9.d: अन्यतरया कुर्वीतेति युवा कौशिको युवा कौशिकः
9.m: 'He should perform it with either of the two,' says the younger Kauśika, the younger Kauśika.

10.m:
[10].1) Rituals for generating intellect for the former [hymn].
[10].2) He ties on the tongues of a parrot, a starling, and a kṛśa bird.
[10].3) He causes him to eat them.
[10].4) He puts [firewood sticks] of udumbara, palāśa, and karkandhu on [the fire].
[10].5) He pours [grains into the fire].
[10].6) He consumes [them].
[10].7) He gives the alms food to the instructor.
[10].8) He whispers into the ear of the sleeping [boy].
[10].9) Approaching him, he mutters [the mantra].
[10].10) Parched grains mixed with ghee are offered entirely.
[10].11) Having offered them mixed with sesame, he eats them.
[10].12) Having driven a speckled staff into the ground to the east of the fire, he consecrates the parched grains upon a black antelope skin to the west of the fire.
[10].13) Having reached the end of the hymn, he hands them over.
[10].14) He offers once.
[10].15) He gives the staff, the parched grains, and the antelope skin.
[10].16) With the hymn 'ahaṃ rudrebhir' [AV 4.30], he feeds [the newborn] with a particle of gold before grasping the breast: two kiṃstyanābhi peppers, one white-flowered and one green-flowered.
[10].17) On the lap of the mother of the [child] beginning to speak, he applies the residues of oblations to the child's palate.
[10].18) He feeds [him] curds and honey.
[10].19) He makes the initiated boy recite [it]; this is a rite that brings a hundred years of life.
[10].20) With 'tvaṃ no medhe' [AV 6.108] and 'dyauś ca ma' [AV 12.1.35], he consumes [the food].
[10].21) He stands worshiping the sun.
[10].22) With 'yad agne tapasā' [AV 7.61], he consumes [food] on the full moon day of Mārgaśīrṣa.
[10].23) He stands worshiping the fire.
[10].24) With 'prātar agniṃ' [AV 3.16], 'girāv aragarāṭeṣu' [AV 6.69], and 'divaspṛthivyāḥ' [AV 6.125.2], having risen, he wipes his face.

10.s: purastād agneḥ kalmāṣam daṇḍaṃ nihatya paścād agneḥ kṛṣṇājine dhānā anumantrayate
10.d: पुरस्ताद् अग्नेः कल्माषम् दण्डं निहत्य पश्चाद् अग्नेः कृष्णाजिने धाना अनुमन्त्रयते

10.s: ahaṃ rudrebhir iti śuklapuṣpaharitapuṣpe kiṃstyanābhipippalyau jātarūpaśakalena prāk stanagrahāt prāśayati
10.d: अहं रुद्रेभिर् इति शुक्लपुष्पहरितपुष्पे किंस्त्यनाभिपिप्पल्यौ जातरूपशकलेन प्राक् स्तनग्रहात् प्राशयति

10.s: prathamapravadasya mātur upasthe tālūni saṃpātān ānayati
10.d: प्रथमप्रवदस्य मातुर् उपस्थे तालूनि संपातान् आनयति

10.s: tvaṃ no medhe dyauś ca ma iti bhakṣayati
10.d: त्वं नो मेधे द्यौश् च म इति भक्षयति

10.s: yad agne tapasā ity āgrahāyaṇyāṃ bhakṣayati
10.d: यद् अग्ने तपसा इत्य् आग्रहायण्यां भक्षयति

10.s: prātar agniṃ girāv aragarāṭeṣu divaspṛthivyāḥ iti saṃhāya mukhaṃ vimārṣṭi
10.d: प्रातर् अग्निं गिराव् अरगराटेषु दिवस्पृथिव्याः इति संहाय मुखं विमार्ष्टि

11.m:
[11.1] The rites for the success of a vedic student [are performed] with the preceding [hymn].
[11.2] The [rites beginning with] the udumbara wood, and so forth [are employed].
[11.3] He lays down the bedding [taken] from the lodging of the vedic student.
[11.4] He offers into an anthill fat, honey, śyāmāka grain, reed tops, and ghee.
[11.5] Having thrown the [earth from] anthills into the remainder of the ghee, having entered the village, [he offers them] wholly burnt.
[11.6] He gives to the vedic students food [consisting of] parched grains mixed with sesame.
[11.7] These are rites for the success of a village.
[11.8] A modification: wood-shavings from the base of a post [and] coverings of assembly halls [are used].
[11.9] [He gives] food to the villagers;
[11.10] surā liquor to the drinkers of surā.
[11.11] The rites beginning with the udumbara wood and ending with eating are for all kinds of success.
[11.12] He produces fire thrice.
[11.13] He reveres [the fire].
[11.14] He eats blood mixed with ritual fluid from the left palm [and] the heart.
[11.15] The pṛśnimantha beverage [is used].
[11.16] Having bound in a coarse garment what is scraped from the tongue, the coverings of the eyes, the brain, [and] the heart, he steeps it in wash-water for three nights.
[11.17] He makes powders [thereof].
[11.18] Having poured them into a beverage of mixed grains, he consumes it mixed with curds and honey.
[11.19] With the mantras "In this [person] wealth..." (AV 1.9), "What they bound..." (AV 1.35), [and] "Nine vital breaths..." (AV 5.28), he ties on a pair of scented kṛṣṇala berries.
[11.20] Having made a human limb [from the milk] of a cow with a calf of identical color imbued with residue of oblations for twelve nights, he eats it without looking toward [it].

11.s: ājyaśeṣe pipīlikodvāpān opya grāmam etya sarvahutān
11.d: आज्यशेषे पिपीलिकोद्वापान् ओप्य ग्रामम् एत्य सर्वहुतान्

11.s: jihvāyā utsādyam akṣyoḥ paristaraṇaṃ mastṛhaṇaṃ hṛdayaṃ dūrśa upanahya tisro rātrīḥ palpūlane vāsayati
11.d: जिह्वाया उत्साद्यम् अक्ष्योः परिस्तरणं मस्तृहणं हृदयं दूर्श उपनह्य तिस्रो रात्रीः पल्पूलने वासयति

11.s: asmin vasu yad ābadhnan nava prāṇān iti yugmakṛṣṇalaṃ vāsitaṃ badhnāti
11.d: अस्मिन् वसु यद् आबध्नन् नव प्राणान् इति युग्मकृष्णलं वासितं बध्नाति

11.s: sārūpavatsaṃ puruṣagātraṃ dvādaśarātraṃ saṃpātavantaṃ kṛtvānabhimukhan aśnāti
11.d: सारूपवत्सं पुरुषगात्रं द्वादशरात्रं संपातवन्तं कृत्वानभिमुखन् अश्नाति

12.s: kathaṃ mahe iti mādānakaśṛtaṃ kṣīraudanam aśnāti
12.d: कथं महे इति मादानकशृतं क्षीरौदनम् अश्नाति
12.m:
[12.1] With the mantra "How to the great..." (AV 5.11), he eats boiled milk-rice cooked over mādānaka wood.
[12.2] In a drinking vessel, having put rice and barley into the milk of a cow having a calf of identical color, having thickened it, [and] having poured honey, he makes [him] eat.
[12.3] With the mantra "To earth, to hearing..." (AV 6.10), he makes oblations.
[12.4] With the mantra "The calf of the Virāj..." (AV 13.1.33), [rites] ending with the beverage [are performed].
[12.5] With the mantras "Sharing a heart..." (AV 3.30), "Right well then..." (AV 5.1.5), "Agree together..." (AV 6.64), "Let it come here..." (AV 6.73), "Let [your minds] be united..." (AV 6.74), "Let your minds..." (AV 6.94), [and] "Agreement for us..." (AV 7.52), rites for concord [are performed].
[12.6] Having carried a water jar imbued with residue of oblations around the village, he pours it out in the middle.
[12.7] Likewise a jar of surā.
[12.8] He makes [them] eat oyster-meat [or] pieces of flesh of a three-year-old heifer.
[12.9] He makes cooked food, surā, and a water-booth imbued with residue of oblations.
[12.10] The rites for splendor [are performed] with the preceding [and] with the hymn "My splendor, O Agni..." (AV 5.3).
[12.11] The three rites beginning with the udumbara wood [are performed].
[12.12] He consecrates the right thigh of a maiden.
[12.13] He offers the omentum.
[12.14] He reveres the fire.
[12.15] With the mantras "In the morning Agni..." (AV 3.16), "On the mountain, on the aragarāṭas..." (AV 6.69), [and] "From heaven, from earth..." (AV 6.125.2), he makes [him] eat curds and honey,
[12.16] mixed with kīlāla beverage for a kṣatriya, and pure kīlāla for the others.

12.s: camase sarūpavatsāyā dugdhe vrīhiyavāvavadhāya mūrchayitvā madhv āsicyāśyati
12.d: चमसे सरूपवत्साया दुग्धे व्रीहियवाववधाय मूर्छयित्वा मध्व् आसिच्याश्यति

12.s: sahṛdayaṃ tad ū ṣu saṃ jānīdhvam eha yātu saṃ vaḥ pṛcyantāṃ saṃ vo manāṃsi saṃjñānaṃ naḥ iti sāṃmanasyāni
12.d: सहृदयं तद् ऊ षु सं जानीध्वम् एह यातु सं वः पृच्यन्तां सं वो मनांसि संज्ञानं नः इति सांमनस्यानि

12.s: udakūlijaṃ saṃpātavantaṃ grāmaṃ parihṛtya madhye ninayati
12.d: उदकूलिजं संपातवन्तं ग्रामं परिहृत्य मध्ये निनयति

12.s: prātar agniṃ girāv aragarāṭeṣu divaspṛthivyāḥ iti dadhimadhv āśayati
12.d: प्रातर् अग्निं गिराव् अरगराटेषु दिवस्पृथिव्याः इति दधिमध्व् आशयति

13.m:
[13.1] With the hymn "The elephant's splendor..." (AV 3.22), [he addresses] an elephant.
[13.2] He binds on an ivory amulet,
[13.3] having smeared the hairs with lac [and] having covered them with gold.
[13.4] With the mantras "In the lion, in the tiger..." (AV 6.38) and "Fame is the havis..." (AV 6.39), [he binds on] navel-hairs of a snātaka, a lion, a tiger, a goat, a black bull, and a king,
[13.5] [and] splinters of ten pacified trees.
[13.6] In both [rites], with the mantras "In the morning Agni..." (AV 3.16), "On the mountain, on the aragarāṭas..." (AV 6.69), [and] "From heaven, from earth..." (AV 6.125.2), he eats seven vital parts mixed in a cooked pot-offering.
[13.7] "It is inauspicious for a brāhmaṇa who should eat blood," says Gārgya.
[13.8] The hair-amulet has been explained.
[13.9] He bathes [him] with all [the mantras].
[13.10] He pours water down [over him].
[13.11] Having sprinkled a four-finger-long blade of grass with a drop of dirt-remover [and] having stirred it up,
[13.12] with the words: "Leprosy in a dog, gray hair in a goat, fever in grass, consumption in him who hates us and whom we hate," he throws away the blade of grass to the south, [and] adorns [the patient] with verses mentioning fragrance.

13.s: siṃhe vyāghre yaśo havir iti snātakasiṃhavyāghrabastakṛṣṇavṛṣabharājñāṃ nabhilomāni
13.d: सिंहे व्याघ्रे यशो हविर् इति स्नातकसिंहव्याघ्रबस्तकृष्णवृषभराज्ञां नभिलोमानि

13.s: etayoḥ prātar agniṃ girāv aragarāṭeṣu divaspṛthivyāḥ iti sapta marmāṇi sthālīpāke pṛktāny aśnāti
13.d: एतयोः प्रातर् अग्निं गिराव् अरगराटेषु दिवस्पृथिव्याः इति सप्त मर्माणि स्थालीपाके पृक्तान्य् अश्नाति

13.s: akuśalaṃ yo brāhmaṇo lohitam aśnīyād iti gārgyaḥ
13.d: अकुशलं यो ब्राह्मणो लोहितम् अश्नीयाद् इति गार्ग्यः

13.s: śuni kilāsam aje palitaṃ tṛṇe jvaro yo asmān dveṣṭi yaṃ ca vayaṃ dviṣmas tasmin rājayakṣma iti dakṣiṇā tṛṇaṃ nirasyati gandhapravādābhir alaṃ kurute
13.d: शुनि किलासम् अजे पलितं तृणे ज्वरो यो अस्मान् द्वेष्टि यं च वयं द्विष्मस् तस्मिन् राजयक्ष्म इति दक्षिणा तृणं निरस्यति गन्धप्रवादाभिर् अलं कुरुते

14.m:
[14.1] The rites for frightening elephants [are performed] with the preceding [hymn].
[14.2] He rolls [a wheel] toward [the elephants] with a chariot-wheel imbued with residue of oblations.
[14.3] He approaches on a conveyance,
[14.4] with musical instruments,
[14.5] having thrown pebbles into a leather bag and a bladder,
[14.6] with a goad, disguised as naked.
[14.7] With the hymns "We know the reed's..." (AV 1.2), "May they not find us..." (AV 1.19), "Splitting not..." (AV 1.20), "Granting well-being..." (AV 1.21), "Down the fury..." (AV 6.65), "Handless..." (AV 6.66), "Around the paths..." (AV 6.67), "Overpowering..." (AV 6.97), "Indra shall conquer..." (AV 6.98), [and] "Unto you, O Indra..." (AV 6.99), the battle rites [are performed].
[14.8] He offers groats mixed with ghee.
[14.9] In the bow-kindling, he places a bow as a firewood stick.
[14.10] Likewise in the arrow-kindling [an arrow].
[14.11] Having wiped off the bow imbued with residue of oblations, he hands it over.
[14.12] The arrow-encircling rites [are performed] with the first [hymn].
[14.13] He ties on roots of grass [from] a mallet, bow-notches, and bowstring loops.
[14.14] The rites for driving away [the enemy] [are performed] with the hymn "Far off yonder..." (AV 1.26).
[14.15] He pours in chaff, husks, chaff-shavings, and shavings.
[14.16] He recites [the hymn].
[14.17] With the hymns "Agni our enemies..." (AV 3.1) and "Agni our messenger..." (AV 3.2), the bewitching rites [are performed].
[14.18] Having supported [the vessel] with cooked rice, he offers the chaff with a mortar.
[14.19] Likewise millet grains.
[14.20] He winnows out [the grains] with twenty-one pebbles.
[14.21] He sacrifices to Apvā.
[14.22] With the hymn "Sharpened..." (AV 3.19), he releases a white-footed [female animal] imbued with residue of oblations.
[14.23] He should harness [her] when they are eager to fight.
[14.24] With the two hymns "This one, O Indra..." (AV 4.22 and 4.23), [rites] ending with the presentation [are performed] for the two yoked [horses].
[14.25] He reveres [the fire] with the two hymns connected to the directions (AV 3.26 and 3.27) and "Homage to the god-missiles..." (AV 6.13).
[14.26] With the hymns "Through you, O Manyu..." (AV 4.31) and "Whichever, O Manyu..." (AV 4.32), the rites of wrath [are performed].
[14.27] Looking upon both armies, he mutters [the hymns].
[14.28] He scatters loops of hemp and muñja grass, adorned with ingiḍa, imbued with residue of oblations, and accompanied by recitation, along the paths of the army.
[14.29] Likewise unbaked vessels.
[14.30] Having besprinkled grasses with ingiḍa [oil], he sets them on fire with Āṅgirasa fire.
[14.31] That [army] which the smoke envelopes, they conquer.

14.s: vidmā śarasya mā no vidan adārasṛd svastidā ava manyur nirhastaḥ pari vartmāny abhibhūr indro jayāti abhi tvendra iti sāṃgrāmikāni
14.d: विद्मा शरस्य मा नो विदन् अदारसृद् स्वस्तिदा अव मन्युर् निर्हस्तः परि वर्त्मान्य् अभिभूर् इन्द्रो जयाति अभि त्वेन्द्र इति सांग्रामिकानि

14.s: agnir naḥ śatrūn agnir no dūtaḥ iti mohanāni
14.d: अग्निर् नः शत्रून् अग्निर् नो दूतः इति मोहनानि

14.s: tvayā manyo yas te manyo iti saṃrambhaṇāni
14.d: त्वया मन्यो यस् ते मन्यो इति संरम्भणानि

14.s: bhāṅgamauñjān pāśan iṅgiḍālaṃkṛtān saṃpātavato anūktān senākrameṣu vapati
14.d: भाङ्गमौञ्जान् पाशन् इङ्गिडालंकृतान् संपातवतो अनूक्तान् सेनाक्रमेषु वपति

15.s: ṛdhaṅ mantras tad id āsa ity āśvatthyāṃ pātryāṃ trivṛti gomayaparicaye hastipṛṣṭhe puruṣaśirasi vāmitrāñ juhvad abhiprakramya nivapati
15.d: ऋधङ् मन्त्रस् तद् इद् आस इत्य् आश्वत्थ्यां पात्र्यां त्रिवृति गोमयपरिचये हस्तिपृष्ठे पुरुषशिरसि वामित्राञ् जुह्वद् अभिप्रक्रम्य निवपति
15.m:
[15].1) With the mantras "ṛdhaṅ mantras" [AV 5.1] and "tad id āsa" [AV 5.2], in a vessel of aśvattha wood, in a threefold heap of cow dung, upon the back of an elephant, or on a human skull, stepping forward while offering the enemies [symbolically], he pours out.
[15].2) Kings prepare an altar from [earth] turned up by a boar.
[15].3) Upon it, [rites] up to the principal oblations [are performed].
[15].4) Having established the fire on the cremation ground of one killed by a single arrow, he offers through the hole of a chariot wheel with a long-handled dipping spoon.
[15].5) Having heard what is to be harnessed, he should harness [it].
[15].6) He recites: "yadi cin nu tvā" [AV 5.2.4] and "namo devavadhebhyo" [AV 6.13].
[15].7) For a vaiśya, [the rites are carried out] up to the principal oblations.
[15].8) With "tvayā vayam" [AV 5.2.5], [he acts] for the armed village leader.
[15].9) With "ni tad dadhiṣe" [AV 5.2.6], he causes the king to look at the water vessel two by two.
[15].10) Whom he does not see, [that one] should not fight.
[15].11) With "ni tad dadhiṣe" [AV 5.2.6], "vanaspate" [AV 12.3.33], "ayā viṣṭhā" [AV 7.3], "agna indraś" [AV 7.110], and "diśas catasro" [AV 8.8.22], he mounts the king together with his charioteer onto a new chariot.
[15].12) With "brahma jajñānam" [AV 5.6], [takes place] the prognosis of life.
[15].13) Having placed three sinew-cords upon the burning coals:
[15].14) When they shrink upwards, there is good fortune.
[15].15) In a battle rite, he assigns these [cords]: in the middle is death; the other two are the armies.
[15].16) Death passes by those about to be defeated; those about to conquer pass by death.
[15].17) When they curl up at the tips, the leaders are slain; in the middles, the middle-ranking; at the ends, the common soldiers.
[15].18) In the same manner [are read] reed stalks.

15.s: ekeṣvā hatasyādahane upasamādhāya dīrghadaṇḍeṇa sruveṇa rathcakrasya khena samayā juhoti
15.d: एकेष्वा हतस्यादहने उपसमाधाय दीर्घदण्डेण स्रुवेण रथ्चक्रस्य खेन समया जुहोति

15.s: yadi cin nu tvā namo devavadhebhyo ity anvāha
15.d: यदि चिन् नु त्वा नमो देववधेभ्यो इत्य् अन्वाह

15.s: ni tad dadhiṣe iti rājñodapātraṃ dvaudvau avekṣayet
15.d: नि तद् दधिषे इति राज्ञोदपात्रं द्वौद्वौ अवेक्षयेत्

15.s: ni tad dadhiṣe vanaspate ayā viṣṭhā agna indraś diśas catasro iti navaṃ rathaṃ rājānaṃ sasārathim āsthāpayati
15.d: नि तद् दधिषे वनस्पते अया विष्ठा अग्न इन्द्रश् दिशस् चतस्रो इति नवं रथं राजानं ससारथिम् आस्थापयति

15.s: sāṃgrāmikam etā vyādiśati madhye mṛtyur itare sene
15.d: सांग्रामिकम् एता व्यादिशति मध्ये मृत्युर् इतरे सेने

15.s: agreṣūtkucatsu mukhyā hanyante madhyeṣu madhyā anteṣu avare
15.d: अग्रेषूत्कुचत्सु मुख्या हन्यन्ते मध्येषु मध्या अन्तेषु अवरे

16.s: uccair ghoṣo upa śvāsaya iti sarvavāditrāṇi prakṣālya tagara uśīreṇa saṃdhāvya saṃpātavanti trir āhatya prayachati
16.d: उच्चैर् घोषो उप श्वासय इति सर्ववादित्राणि प्रक्षाल्य तगर उशीरेण संधाव्य संपातवन्ति त्रिर् आहत्य प्रयछति
16.m:
[16].1) With "uccair ghoṣo" [AV 5.20] and "upa śvāsaya" [AV 6.126], having washed all musical instruments and rubbed them with tagara and uśīra, having bestowed the residue of oblations upon them, striking them three times, he hands them over.
[16].2) With "vihṛdayam" [AV 5.21], sacrificing higher up, turning the dipping spoon upward,
[16].3) Having sewn a soma shoot into a deer-skin, he ties it onto the kṣatriya.
[16].4) With "pari vartmāni" [AV 6.67] and "indro jayāti" [AV 6.98], the king marches around the army three times.
[16].5) The soma shoot of the previous rite has been explained.
[16].6) With "saṃdānaṃ vo" [AV 6.103] and "ādānena" [AV 6.104], bindings and tying-ups [are performed] with fetters.
[16].7) With "marmāṇi te" [AV 7.118], he arms the kṣatriya in armor.
[16].8) There is the appending of the hymns for safety.
[16].9) With "indro manthatu" [AV 8.8]:
[16].10) Having placed a putrid rope with "pūtirajjur" [AV 8.8.2ab],
[16].11) He churns fire from aśvattha and bādhaka woods.
[16].12) With "dhūmam" [AV 8.8.2cd], he consecrates the smoke.
[16].13) With "agnim" [AV 8.8.2cd], [he consecrates] the fire.
[16].14) In that wild fire, he places enemy-destroying [sticks] of aśvattha, bādhaka, tājadbhaṅga, āhva, khadira, and śara.
[16].15) The traps have been explained:
[16].16) Traps of aśvattha, nets of hemp,
[16].17) Staffs of bādhaka wood.
[16].18) With "svāhaibhyo" [AV 8.8.24cd], he offers for friends.
[16].19) With "durāhāmībhya" [AV 8.8.24cd], using his left hand, [he offers] iṅgiḍa oil on the bādhaka [stick] for the enemies.
[16].20) Having driven in a branch of red aśvattha north of the fire and wound it with dark-blue and red threads, he drives [the enemies] south with "nīlalohitenāmūn" [AV 8.8.24e].
[16].21) With "ye bāhav" [AV 11.9] and "ut tiṣṭhata" [AV 11.10], he gives instructions according to the characteristic marks [in the text].
[16].22) For the purpose of the oblation, there is speckled ghee.
[16].23) The strewing rites end with the principal oblations.
[16].24) Through the strewings, [the hymns of] Triṣandhi, the forms of the thunderbolt, and the forms of Arbudi [are employed].
[16].25) He ties a white-footed [insect] that has received the residue of oblations with a darbha cord to the chariot staff for the kṣatriya.
[16].26) He casts a second one.
[16].27) With "asmin vasu" [AV 1.9], [the rite is for] the restoration to a realm.
[16].28) He feeds [a cow] having a calf of identical color [with mash] cooked from awnless rice with kāmpīla growing from incisions.
[16].29) With "abhīvartena" [AV 1.29], having bound an amulet of chariot-rim wood wrapped with iron, lead, red metal, silver, and copper, with a golden navel and perfumed, strung on a cord, placed upon sacrificial grass, having received the residue of oblations, he fastens the points verse by verse with the two verses containing "abhīvarta" at the end.
[16].30) With "acikradat" [AV 3.3] and "ā tvā gan" [AV 3.4], toward the direction of the realm from which he has been expelled, he pours out a puroḍāśa shaped like a bed onto darbha grass in water.
[16].31) Then, having covered the hearth of the fire with a clod of earth from there, he eats rice cooked in milk.
[16].32) Whence the clod of earth [comes], thence [come] the ritual materials.
[16].33) When the puroḍāśa of three [portions] has been eaten in the morning, they summon [him].

16.s: vihṛdayam ity uccaistarāṃ hutvā sruvam udvartayan
16.d: विहृदयम् इत्य् उच्चैस्तरां हुत्वा स्रुवम् उद्वर्तयन्

16.s: pari vartmāni indro jayāti iti rājā triḥ senāṃ pariyāti
16.d: परि वर्त्मानि इन्द्रो जयाति इति राजा त्रिः सेनां परियाति

16.s: saṃdānaṃ vo ādānena iti pāśair ādānasaṃdānāni
16.d: संदानं वो आदानेन इति पाशैर् आदानसंदानानि

16.s: tasminn araṇye sapatnakṣayaṇīr ādadhāty aśvattha badhaka tājadbhaṅga āhva khadira śarāṇām
16.d: तस्मिन्न् अरण्ये सपत्नक्षयणीर् आदधात्य् अश्वत्थ बधक ताजद्भङ्ग आह्व खदिर शराणाम्

16.s: durāhāmībhya iti savyena iṅgiḍam amitrebhyo bādhake
16.d: दुराहामीभ्य इति सव्येन इङ्गिडम् अमित्रेभ्यो बाधके

16.s: uttarato agner lohitāśvatthasya śākhāṃ nihatya nīlalohitābhyāṃ sūtrābhyāṃ paritatya nīlalohitenāmūn iti dakṣiṇā prahāpayati
16.d: उत्तरतो अग्नेर् लोहिताश्वत्थस्य शाखां निहत्य नीललोहिताभ्यां सूत्राभ्यां परितत्य नीललोहितेनामून् इति दक्षिणा प्रहापयति

16.s: ye bāhav ut tiṣṭhata iti yathāliṅgaṃ saṃpreṣyati
16.d: ये बाहव् उत् तिष्ठत इति यथालिङ्गं संप्रेष्यति

16.s: śitipadīṃ saṃpātavatīṃ darbharajjvā kṣatriyāya upasaṅgadaṇḍe badhnāti
16.d: शितिपदीं संपातवतीं दर्भरज्ज्वा क्षत्रियाय उपसङ्गदण्डे बध्नाति

16.s: ānuśūkānāṃ vrīhīṇām āvraskajaiḥ kāmpīlaiḥ śṛtaṃ sārūpavatsam āśayati
16.d: आनुशूकानां व्रीहीणाम् आव्रस्कजैः काम्पीलैः शृतं सारूपवत्सम् आशयति

16.s: abhīvartena iti rathanemimaṇim ayaḥsīsaloharajatatāmraveṣṭitaṃ hemanābhiṃ vāsitaṃ baddhvā sūtrotaṃ barhiṣi kṛtvā saṃpātavantaṃ pratyṛcaṃ bhṛṣṭīr abhīvarttottamābhyām ācṛtati
16.d: अभीवर्तेन इति रथनेमिमणिम् अयःसीसलोहरजतताम्रवेष्टितं हेमनाभिं वासितं बद्ध्वा सूत्रोतं बर्हिषि कृत्वा संपातवन्तं प्रत्यृचं भृष्टीर् अभीवर्त्तोत्तमाभ्याम् आचृतति

16.s: acikradat ā tvā gan iti yasmād rāṣṭrād avaruddhas tasyāśāyāṃ śayanavidhaṃ puroḍāśaṃ darbheṣūdake ninayati
16.d: अचिक्रदत् आ त्वा गन् इति यस्माद् राष्ट्राद् अवरुद्धस् तस्याशायां शयनविधं पुरोडाशं दर्भेषूदके निनयति

16.s: tato loṣṭena jyotir āyatanaṃ saṃstīrya kṣīraudanam aśnāti
16.d: ततो लोष्टेन ज्योतिर् आयतनं संस्तीर्य क्षीरौदनम् अश्नाति

17.s: bhūto bhūteṣu iti rājānam abhiṣekṣyan mahānade śāntyudakaṃ karoty ādiṣṭānām
17.d: भूतो भूतेषु इति राजानम् अभिषेक्ष्यन् महानदे शान्त्युदकं करोत्य् आदिष्टानाम्
17.m:
[17].1) With 'Existing among beings...' [AV 4.8], when about to consecrate the king, he prepares pacifying water from a great river [using the plants] that have been specified.
[17].2) Having cooked the boiled oblation, he consecrates him as he stands on darbha grass south of the enclosed [hearth].
[17].3) He has him step onto an ox hide [placed on] a couch.
[17].4) They two pour together [the contents of their] water vessels.
[17].5) They exchange garments.
[17].6) The Brahman priest should say: 'Together indeed is our good deed, together our bad deed.'
[17].7) [The king replies:] 'Whoever performs a bad deed, his is the bad deed; our good deed is together.'
[17].8) He feeds him.
[17].9) Having mounted a horse, he makes him advance in the northeast direction.
[17].10) A thousand [cows] and the best village are the sacrificial fee.
[17].11) The rites up to the exchanging of garments are explained by the single-king rite.
[17].12) He consecrates him on darbha grass upon a couch.
[17].13) On a higher [couch] he has him step onto a tiger skin.
[17].14) Four royal sons, couch-bearers, grasping the bed by its separate legs, carry it into the assembly hall.
[17].15) A servant washes his feet.
[17].16) A Mahāśūdra sprinkles [them] with water.
[17].17) He sorts out the dice that have attained the kṛta throw up to the third time.
[17].18) A Vaiśya approaches him with all his possessions, [saying]: 'Release [it], O long-lived one!'
[17].19) [The king says:] 'I release for the Brāhmaṇa; I release for the Kṣatriya; I release for the Vaiśya. Let righteousness be practiced in my country!'
[17].20) He receives [it].
[17].21) He feeds him.
[17].22) Having mounted a horse, he makes him advance in the northeast direction.
[17].23) He goes up to the assembly hall.
[17].24) He feeds the Brāhmaṇas with honey mixture.
[17].25) He makes him consume the ritual fluids.
[17].26) He approaches the buffaloes.
[17].27) 'They should offer a cow,' say Gārgya and Pārthaśravas; 'not [so],' says Bhāgali.
[17].28) With 'Increase this Kṣatriya for me, O Indra...' [AV 4.22], he addresses the Kṣatriya every morning.
[17].29) The pouring together and exchanging of garments have been stated.
[17].30) With 'Savitṛ of impulses...' [AV 5.24], one about to abide in the domestic priesthood, having placed firewood sticks of the vaiśvalopa tree [on the fire],
[17].31) should initiate the Kṣatriya with 'Indra [gave] the royal power...' [AV 7.84.2].
[17].32) Regarding this they say: 'One should not make a Kṣatriya recite the Sāvitrī verse.'
[17].33) How indeed could he initiate him if he did not make him recite it?
[17].34) He should indeed make him recite it; he should indeed make him recite it.

17.s: sthālīpākaṃ śrapayitvā dakṣiṇataḥ parigṛhyāyā darbheṣu tiṣṭhantam abhiṣiñcati
17.d: स्थालीपाकं श्रपयित्वा दक्षिणतः परिगृह्याया दर्भेषु तिष्ठन्तम् अभिषिञ्चति

17.s: sahaiva nau sukṛtaṃ saha duṣkṛtam iti brahmā brūyāt
17.d: सहैव नौ सुकृतं सह दुष्कृतम् इति ब्रह्मा ब्रूयात्

17.s: yo duṣkṛtaṃ karavat tasya duṣkṛtaṃ sukṛtaṃ nau saheti
17.d: यो दुष्कृतं करवत् तस्य दुष्कृतं सुकृतं नौ सहेति

17.s: catvāro rājaputrās tālpāḥ pṛthakpādeṣu śayanaṃ parāmṛśya sabhāṃ prāpayanti
17.d: चत्वारो राजपुत्रास् ताल्पाः पृथक्पादेषु शयनं परामृश्य सभां प्रापयन्ति

17.s: utsṛjāmi brāhmaṇāya utsṛjāmi kṣatriyāya utsṛjāmi vaiśyāya dharmo me janapade caryatām iti
17.d: उत्सृजामि ब्राह्मणाय उत्सृजामि क्षत्रियाय उत्सृजामि वैश्याय धर्मो मे जनपदे चर्यताम् इति

17.s: kuryur gām iti gārgyapārthaśravasau neti bhāgaliḥ
17.d: कुर्युर् गाम् इति गार्ग्यपार्थश्रवसौ नेति भागलिः

17.s: imam indra vardhaya kṣatriyaṃ me iti kṣatriyaṃ prātaḥ prātar abhimantrayate
17.d: इमम् इन्द्र वर्धय क्षत्रियं मे इति क्षत्रियं प्रातः प्रातर् अभिमन्त्रयते

17.s: savitā prasavānām iti paurohitye vatsyan vaiśvalopīḥ samidha ādhāya
17.d: सविता प्रसवानाम् इति पौरोहित्ये वत्स्यन् वैश्वलोपीः समिध आधाय

17.s: tad āhur na kṣatriyaṃ sāvitrīṃ vācayed iti
17.d: तद् आहुर् न क्षत्रियं सावित्रीं वाचयेद् इति

17.s: kathaṃ nu tam upanayīta yan na vācayed
17.d: कथं नु तम् उपनयीत यन् न वाचयेद्

18.s: pūrvasya pūrvasyāṃ paurṇamāsyām astamita udakānte kṛṣṇacailaparihito nirṛtikarmāṇi prayuṅkte
18.d: पूर्वस्य पूर्वस्यां पौर्णमास्याम् अस्तमित उदकान्ते कृष्णचैलपरिहितो निरृतिकर्माणि प्रयुङ्क्ते
18.m:
[18].1) On the full moon day of the previous [month], at sunset, at the water's edge, clad in a black cloth, he performs the rites to Nirṛti.
[18].2) He should bury an earthen vessel at an eddy turning to the right in a navigable river.
[18].3) He pours water over it with the water hymns.
[18].4) He abandons the black [cloth] in the water.
[18].5) Having put on unwashed clothes and sandals, he departs from the lethal [place].
[18].6) Having stayed away from home, he performs the ritual of prosperity for that [person] on the next [full moon day].
[18].7) Having smeared the earthen vessel, fastened it in the water, and added fire therein, he makes it have residue of oblations.
[18].8) He eats.
[18].9) Having placed [it on the water], he floats the black [cloth] away.
[18].10) Having put on old sandals, holding an old umbrella with the left hand, and having ignited hall-grass with the right hand, he casts it down upon old vīriṇa grass.
[18].11) Turning round without looking back, he makes a single offering.
[18].12) He throws down the left [umbrella] and the sandals.
[18].13) Having added fire upon old vīriṇa grass, with 'This is your source...' [AV 3.20], he scatters rice grains mixed with pebbles from an old granary [into the fire].
[18].14) With 'Bring to us...' [AV 5.7], parched grains [are scattered].
[18].15) With both [granaries] fitted together, [he scatters] the third [offering].
[18].16) Having tied a stamp to the left leg of a black bird, and a sacrificial cake to the stamp, with 'Fly forth from here...' [AV 7.115], he makes it fly away without turning back.
[18].17) Having joined blue [thread], covered it with red, wrapped it with white, having approached the turban with a hook by the second [verse], he casts it face down into the water along with the hook using the left hand.
[18].18) Covered by the third [verse], wrapped round by the fourth [verse].
[18].19) The Citrā rite of the previous [topic].
[18].20) He eats food cooked in a vessel, having green sacrificial grass.
[18].21) He lays down [firewood sticks] smeared [with ghee], measuring a span.
[18].22) At the confluence of two navigable rivers, behind the fire, within a furrow marked on the ground, he consumes the sweet drink directly with his mouth.
[18].23) He consumes the vow of brilliance for three nights.
[18].24) He consumes only that.
[18].25) With 'By the two who are beneficial and comforting...' [AV 1.5 + 1.6], 'Brahman born first...' [AV 4.1.1], 'Of this lovely...' [AV 9.9], 'He who is Rohita...' [AV 13.1.25], 'Upward his banners...' [AV 13.2.1], 'Chief am I...' [AV 16.3.1], and 'The overcoming one...' [AV 17.1.1-5], he eats milk-rice with waters.
[18].26) The rites conclude with the stirred drink.
[18].27) When about to go abroad, he should offer oblations with the second [verse].
[18].28) Then upon returning,
[18].29) then upon returning.
[18].30) Then when making a request,
[18].31) then when making a request.
[18].32) There are four layers of palāśa sticks.
[18].33) There are four of upolava-darbha grass.
[18].34) Having placed that kindling wood of at least eight [sticks], interwoven, on the sacrificial fire of a sattra, he should make oblations over it with ghee.
[18].35) He should hold in the smoke.
[18].36) He should consume the residue.
[18].37) And if he should not find that, then having made a place like a sacrificial enclosure at the site of a sattra,
[18].38) they call [this] rite 'the ocean'.

18.s: śāpeṭam ālipyāpsu nibadhya tasminn upasamādhāya saṃpātavantaṃ karoti
18.d: शापेटम् आलिप्याप्सु निबध्य तस्मिन्न् उपसमाधाय संपातवन्तं करोति

18.s: upamucya jaradupānahau savyena jarat chattraṃ dakṣiṇena śālātṛṇāṇy ādīpya jīrṇaṃ vīriṇam abhinyasyati
18.d: उपमुच्य जरदुपानहौ सव्येन जरत् छत्त्रं दक्षिणेन शालातृणाण्य् आदीप्य जीर्णं वीरिणम् अभिन्यस्यति

18.s: jīrṇe vīriṇa upasamādhāya ayaṃ te yonir iti jaratkoṣṭhād vrīhīñ śarkarāmiśrān āvapati
18.d: जीर्णे वीरिण उपसमाधाय अयं ते योनिर् इति जरत्कोष्ठाद् व्रीहीञ् शर्करामिश्रान् आवपति

18.s: kṛṣṇaśakuneḥ savyajaṅghāyām aṅkam anubadhyāṅke puroḍāśaṃ pra patetaḥ iti anāvṛtaṃ prapādayati
18.d: कृष्णशकुनेः सव्यजङ्घायाम् अङ्कम् अनुबध्याङ्के पुरोडाशं प्र पतेतः इति अनावृतं प्रपादयति

18.s: nīlaṃ saṃdhāya lohitam āchādya śuklaṃ pariṇahya dvitīyayā uṣṇīṣam aṅkena upasādya savyena sahāṅkenāvāṅ apsu apavidhyati
18.d: नीलं संधाय लोहितम् आछाद्य शुक्लं परिणह्य द्वितीयया उष्णीषम् अङ्केन उपसाद्य सव्येन सहाङ्केनावाङ् अप्सु अपविध्यति

18.s: nāvyayoḥ sāṃvaidye paścād agner bhūmiparilekhe kīlālaṃ mukhenāśnāti
18.d: नाव्ययोः सांवैद्ये पश्चाद् अग्नेर् भूमिपरिलेखे कीलालं मुखेनाश्नाति

18.s: śaṃbhumayobhubhyāṃ brahma jajñānam asya vāmasya yo rohito ud asya ketavo mūrdhāhaṃ viṣāsahim iti salilaiḥ kṣīraudanam aśnāti
18.d: शंभुमयोभुभ्यां ब्रह्म जज्ञानम् अस्य वामस्य यो रोहितो उद् अस्य केतवो मूर्धाहं विषासहिम् इति सलिलैः क्षीरौदनम् अश्नाति

18.s: taṃ vyatiṣaktam aṣṭāvaram idhmaṃ sāttrike agnau ādhāyājyenābhijuhuyāt
18.d: तं व्यतिषक्तम् अष्टावरम् इध्मं सात्त्रिके अग्नौ आधायाज्येनाभिजुहुयात्

18.s: tam u cen na vinded atha sattrasyāyatane yajñāyatanam iva kṛtvā
18.d: तम् उ चेन् न विन्देद् अथ सत्त्रस्यायतने यज्ञायतनम् इव कृत्वा

19.s: ambayo yanty śaṃbhumayobhubhyāṃ brahma jajñānam ā gāvo ekā ca me iti gā lavaṇaṃ pāyayaty upatāpinīḥ
19.d: अम्बयो यन्त्य् शंभुमयोभुभ्यां ब्रह्म जज्ञानम् आ गावो एका च मे इति गा लवणं पाययत्य् उपतापिनीः
19.m:
[19.1] With "The mothers go..." (AV 1.4.1), with the two hymns "Beneficent, delight-bringing..." (AV 1.5 + 1.6), "The Brahman born..." (AV 4.1), "Hither, the cows..." (AV 4.21.1), and "And my one..." (AV 5.15.1), he makes sick cows drink salt water.
[19.2] [Also those] desiring offspring.
[19.3] He closes off a watering place.
[19.4] With "Let them flow together..." (AV 1.15.1), two people bring water from navigable streams, pouring it in from all sides.
[19.5] Therein he eats mixed grain cooked [in milk or water].
[19.6] Or a stirred beverage mixed with curd and honey.
[19.7] From whichever person he desires prosperity, having obtained rice, ghee, and milk from him, he eats rice-milk.
