[19.8] If that is not obtainable, having obtained fresh cow dung and dried it, he eats [food] cooked on a three-layered heap of cow dung.
[19.9] With "O Śerabhaka..." (AV 2.24.1), the rite relating to the ocean in the waters has been explained.
[19.10] Having mixed uncrushed barley grains with a portion of milk from a red goat, he eats.
[19.11] So much he approaches.
[19.12] Untying the knots of grass, he steps away.
[19.13] Going back up from the waters, he washes over them with the water vessel, and wipes his face.
[19.14] "Hither let the cattle come..." (AV 2.26.1), "Together with your cattle pen..." (AV 3.24.1), "Having progeny..." (AV 4.21.7 / 7.75), and "Prajāpati..." (AV 6.11.3) are the rites of the cowpen.
[19.15] He eats colostrum of a cow that has calved for the first time, mixed with phlegm.
[19.16] He gives away a cow.
[19.17] He pours out the water vessel.
[19.18] Having swept [the dung] together, stepping on half of it with the left [foot], he tosses it out with the right.
[19.19] While a cow has a calf of identical appearance, having placed balls of dung into bdellium and salt, he buries them behind the fire.
[19.20] In the morning he eats [milk] from three [cows].
[19.21] When transformed, it is accomplished.
[19.22] With "This one has arrived..." (AV 3.5.1), "This amulet..." (AV 8.5.1), "This is my varaṇa..." (AV 10.3.1), and "Of the hostile..." (AV 10.6.1), he fastens [amulets] mentioned in the mantras, after they have been perfumed.
[19.23] Having run four [amulets] of the last [hymn] along a cord together with a piece of gold and bent them, he tosses them around in three parts.
[19.24] Having added fuel with "This firewood..." (AV 10.6.35),
[19.25] having plucked out the perfumed [amulet] with "Him this, the deities..." (AV 10.6.29), he fastens it with "With the splendour of the sacred word..." (AV 10.6.30).
[19.26] With "You are supreme..." (AV 6.15.1), [an amulet] mentioned in the mantra.
[19.27] With "Imperishable are your..." (AV 6.142.3), a barley amulet.
[19.28] With the entire hymn "First she shone forth..." (AV 3.10), he offers the omentum of the Aṣṭakā cow three times.
[19.29] From the cut portions of the cooked mess of grain [he offers].
[19.30] Having offered those offered together mixed with ghee, he lies down behind the fire, restraining his speech.
[19.31] Reciting [names] of the great beings, he rises.

19.s: saṃ saṃ sravantu iti nāvyābhyām udakam āharataḥ sarvata upāsecam
19.d: सं सं स्रवन्तु इति नाव्याभ्याम् उदकम् आहरतः सर्वत उपासेचम्

19.s: yasya śriyaṃ kāmayate tato vrīhi ājyapaya āhārya kṣīraudanam aśnāti
19.d: यस्य श्रियं कामयते ततो व्रीहि आज्यपय आहार्य क्षीरौदनम् अश्नाति

19.s: tadalābhe haritagomayam āhārya śoṣayitvā trivṛti gomayaparicaye śṛtam aśnāti
19.d: तदलाभे हरितगोमयम् आहार्य शोषयित्वा त्रिवृति गोमयपरिचये शृतम् अश्नाति

19.s: śerabhaka iti sāmudram apsu karma vyākhyātam
19.d: शेरभक इति सामुद्रम् अप्सु कर्म व्याख्यातम्

19.s: tān udāvrajann udapātrasya udapātreṇābhiplāvayati mukhaṃ vimārṣṭi
19.d: तान् उदाव्रजन्न् उदपात्रस्य उदपात्रेणाभिप्लावयति मुखं विमार्ष्टि

19.s: eha yantu paśavo saṃ vo goṣṭhena prajāvatīḥ prajāpatir iti goṣṭhakarmāṇi
19.d: एह यन्तु पशवो सं वो गोष्ठेन प्रजावतीः प्रजापतिर् इति गोष्ठकर्माणि

19.s: sārūpavatse śakṛtpiṇḍān guggululavaṇe pratinīya paścād agner nikhanati
19.d: सारूपवत्से शकृत्पिण्डान् गुग्गुलुलवणे प्रतिनीय पश्चाद् अग्नेर् निखनति

19.s: āyam agan ayaṃ pratisaro ayaṃ me varaṇo arātīyor iti mantroktān vāsitān badhnāti
19.d: आयम् अगन् अयं प्रतिसरो अयं मे वरणो अरातीयोर् इति मन्त्रोक्तान् वासितान् बध्नाति

19.s: uttamasya caturo jātarūpaśakalenānusūtraṃ gamayitvāvabhujya traidhaṃ paryasyati
19.d: उत्तमस्य चतुरो जातरूपशकलेनानुसूत्रं गमयित्वावभुज्य त्रैधं पर्यस्यति

19.s: tam imaṃ devatā iti vāsitam ullupya brahmaṇā tejasā iti badhnāti
19.d: तम् इमं देवता इति वासितम् उल्लुप्य ब्रह्मणा तेजसा इति बध्नाति

19.s: prathamā ha vyuvāsa sā ity aṣṭakyāyā vapāṃ sarveṇa sūktena trir juhoti
19.d: प्रथमा ह व्युवास सा इत्य् अष्टक्याया वपां सर्वेण सूक्तेन त्रिर् जुहोति

19.s: sahahutān ājyamiśrān hutvā paścād agner vāgyataḥ saṃviśati
19.d: सहहुतान् आज्यमिश्रान् हुत्वा पश्चाद् अग्नेर् वाग्यतः संविशति

20.m:
[20.1] With "They yoke the plows..." (AV 3.17.1), he stretches out the yoke and plow.
[20.2] He yokes the right draft ox first.
[20.3] With "Come, O Pūrṇaka...", the left one.
[20.4] The plowmen [yoke] the other ones.
[20.5] With "Let the Aśvins shape the plowshare, let Bṛhaspati assist, so that there may be abundant grain, free from consumption, with abundant men", he drags the plowshare across.
[20.6] With "You are full of food; in the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, in your sacrificial session, let it succeed for me...", he measures off.
[20.7] Striking back with cakes [of flour] with "Struck away are the obstacles...", he plows.
[20.8] Having gone to the end of the hymn, he hands [it] over.
[20.9] Speaking auspicious words, they cause three furrows to run eastward.
[20.10] Having turned around with "O furrow, we revere you..." (AV 3.17.8), he sacrifices to Indra with a sacrificial cake at the northern end of the furrow.
[20.11] To the Aśvins with a cooked mess of grain.
[20.12] They lead residues of oblations into the furrow.
[20.13] The subsequent ones into the water vessel.
[20.14] Having put down [portions] of the young sprout oblations,
[20.15] he anoints everything.
[20.16] When he brings the residues of oblations, the wife asks him who is holding a clod of earth from there: "Have you plowed?"
[20.17] "We have plowed."
[20.18] "What have you brought?"
[20.19] "Acquisition, prosperity, nourishment, offspring, cattle, food, food-eating."
[20.20] On the north side, he scatters it into the middle [furrow].
[20.21] Having anointed the northern plowshare, he sets it down for yoking in the morning.
[20.22] Having spread darbha grass at the heads of the furrows, he sets down three cups each of plakṣa and udumbara [wood].
[20.23] Those containing fluid on the southern [furrow], those containing young sprouts on the middle, those containing the sacrificial cake on the northern.
[20.24] Having bent the darbha grasses back, he pours them together.
[20.25] While a cow has a calf of identical appearance, having placed balls of dung into bdellium and salt, he eats.
[20.26] [This is] the rite for success with draft oxen.

20.s: aśvinā phālaṃ kalpayatām upāvatu bṛhaspatiḥ | yathāsad bahudhānyam ayakṣmaṃ bahupūruṣam iti phālam atikarṣati
20.d: अश्विना फालं कल्पयताम् उपावतु बृहस्पतिः । यथासद् बहुधान्यम् अयक्ष्मं बहुपूरुषम् इति फालम् अतिकर्षति

20.s: irāvān asi dhārtarāṣṭre tava me sattre rādhyatām iti pratimimīte
20.d: इरावान् असि धार्तराष्ट्रे तव मे सत्त्रे राध्यताम् इति प्रतिमिमीते

20.s: apahatāḥ pratiṣṭhāḥ ity apūpaiḥ pratihatya kṛṣati
20.d: अपहताः प्रतिष्ठाः इत्य् अपूपैः प्रतिहत्य कृषति

20.s: tisraḥ sītāḥ prācīr gamayanti kalyāṇīr vāco vadantaḥ
20.d: तिस्रः सीताः प्राचीर् गमयन्ति कल्याणीर् वाचो वदन्तः

20.s: sīte vandāmahe tvā ity āvartayitvā uttarasmin sītānte puroḍāśena indraṃ yajate
20.d: सीते वन्दामहे त्वा इत्य् आवर्तयित्वा उत्तरस्मिन् सीतान्ते पुरोडाशेन इन्द्रं यजते

20.s: yatra saṃpātān ānayati tato loṣṭaṃ dhārayantaṃ patnī pṛchaty akṛkṣata iti
20.d: यत्र संपातान् आनयति ततो लोष्टं धारयन्तं पत्नी पृछत्य् अकृक्षत इति

20.s: vittiṃ bhūtiṃ puṣṭiṃ prajāṃ paśūn annam annādyam iti
20.d: वित्तिं भूतिं पुष्टिं प्रजां पशून् अन्नम् अन्नाद्यम् इति

20.s: sītāśiraḥsu darbhān āstīrya plakṣa udumbarasya trīṃs trīṃś camasān nidadhāti
20.d: सीताशिरःसु दर्भान् आस्तीर्य प्लक्ष उदुम्बरस्य त्रींस् त्रींश् चमसान् निदधाति

20.s: rasavato dakṣiṇe śaṣpavato madhyame puroḍāśavata uttare
20.d: रसवतो दक्षिणे शष्पवतो मध्यमे पुरोडाशवत उत्तरे

21.m:
[21].1) With "Rich in milk..." [AVŚ 3.24], [the rite is] for producing abundance.
[21].2) Having wrapped the tips of three kūdī twigs along with a heap of grains sown, clods made of stone, and earth from an ant-hill with pacified fruits in a middle palāśa leaf using darbha grass, he places them in the grain-bins of the heap.
[21].3) In the evening they eat.
[21].4) They pour back the remainder,
[21].5) up until the meal-dispensing.
[21].6) He addresses them with mantras.
[21].7) With "This is our lord of the sky..." [AVŚ 6.79], having besprinkled a stone in the bin, he pours in [grains] and causes them to be poured in along with the kāśī according to the verse.
[21].8) With "The cows have come..." [AVŚ 4.21], he rises up to meet the incoming cows.
[21].9) In the rainy season, he offers thrice to Indra from the first stream [of milk].
[21].10) With "Abounding in offspring...", he addresses them as they set out.
[21].11) On a twelve-threaded tether having the residue of oblations, for [the cows] having the designations of white cows, he performs what is stated in the mantra: "This fodder... the calf here..." [AVŚ 4.38.7cd].
[21].12) With "What [fire] for your burning..." [AVŚ 5.1.3], [the rite is] for securing garment-prosperity.
[21].13) He puts on three [twigs] made of kūdī, wrapped in spider-webs, smeared consecutively.
[21].14) Wrapped at the very ends in reed-grass and muñja-grass, smeared with honey, having cast them around in the chaff,
[21].15) with "And the son..." [AVŚ 5.1.8], he causes the eldest son to settle down.
[21].16) Residing in a measured shelter, he brings about prosperity.
[21].17) With "Half with half..." [AVŚ 5.1.9], with wet hands, without recognizing [the difference], he hands it over.
[21].18) Having separated the eastern part with a pacified branch,
[21].19) he fastens it toward the fire.
[21].20) On that new moon day, he lays on three [sticks] measuring a span.
[21].21) With "In you the resolve..." [AVŚ 5.2.3], [the rite is] for consuming ritual fluids.
[21].22) He performs rites with ritual fluids.
[21].23) With "Praise the height..." [AVŚ 5.2.7], at sunset on a new moon day dedicated to Prajāpati, holding a lamp above a top of an ant-hill covered with darbha grass, he offers thrice.
[21].24) Having brought the residues of rice grains and poured ritual fluids over them, he eats.
[21].25) In this manner on a full moon day, with those steeped in ghee.

21.s: śāntaphalaśilākṛtiloṣṭavalmīkarāśivāpaṃ trīṇi kūdīprāntāni madhyamapalāśe darbheṇa pariveṣṭya rāśipalyeṣu karoti
21.d: शान्तफलशिलाकृतिलोष्टवल्मीकराशिवापं त्रीणि कूदीप्रान्तानि मध्यमपलाशे दर्भेण परिवेष्ट्य राशिपल्येषु करोति

21.s: ayaṃ no nabhasas patiḥ iti palye aśmānaṃ saṃprokṣyānvṛcaṃ kāśī opyāvāpayati
21.d: अयं नो नभसस् पतिः इति पल्ये अश्मानं संप्रोक्ष्यान्वृचं काशी ओप्यावापयति

21.s: ā gāvo iti gā āyatīḥ pratyuttiṣṭhati
21.d: आ गावो इति गा आयतीः प्रत्युत्तिष्ठति

21.s: karkīpravādānāṃ dvādaśadāmnyāṃ saṃpātavatyām ayaṃ ghāso iha vatsām iti mantroktam
21.d: कर्कीप्रवादानां द्वादशदाम्न्यां संपातवत्याम् अयं घासो इह वत्साम् इति मन्त्रोक्तम्

21.s: tisraḥ kūdīmayīr ūrṇanābhikulāya parihitā anvaktā ādadhāti
21.d: तिस्रः कूदीमयीर् ऊर्णनाभिकुलाय परिहिता अन्वक्ता आदधाति

21.s: uta putraḥ iti jyeṣṭhaṃ putram avasāyayati
21.d: उत पुत्रः इति ज्येष्ठं पुत्रम् अवसाययति

21.s: ardham ardhena ity ārdrapāṇir asaṃjñātvā prayachati
21.d: अर्धम् अर्धेन इत्य् आर्द्रपाणिर् असंज्ञात्वा प्रयछति

21.s: stuṣva varṣman iti prājāpatyāmāvāsyāyām astamite valmīkaśirasi darbhāvastīrṇe adhyadhi dīpaṃ dhārayaṃs trir juhoti
21.d: स्तुष्व वर्ष्मन् इति प्राजापत्यामावास्यायाम् अस्तमिते वल्मीकशिरसि दर्भावस्तीर्णे अध्यधि दीपं धारयंस् त्रिर् जुहोति

22.s: ṛdhaṅmantro tad id āsa iti maiśradhānyaṃ bhṛṣṭapiṣṭaṃ lohitālaṃkṛtaṃ rasamiśram aśnāti
22.d: ऋधङ्मन्त्रो तद् इद् आस इति मैश्रधान्यं भृष्टपिष्टं लोहितालंकृतं रसमिश्रम् अश्नाति
22.m:
[22].1) With "The effective mantra..." [AVŚ 5.1] and "That indeed was..." [AVŚ 5.2], he eats mixed grains, roasted and ground, adorned with blood, mixed with ritual fluids;
[22].2) or unroasted, to the north of the fire of plakṣa and udumbara wood, in three wooden cups, [saying] in the forenoon: "With the splendor of the forenoon, I have eaten the beginning of the food";
[22].3) at midday, [saying]: "With the splendor of midday, I have eaten the middle of the food";
[22].4) in the afternoon, [saying]: "With the splendor of the afternoon, I have eaten all of the food."
[22].5) [He takes] the blood with two fingers from a menstruating woman.
[22].6) On whichever field he desires, [he places] the sweet beverage mixed with curd and honey.
[22].7) Having abstained from a woman for a year, having collected semen in a pearl-oyster shell mixed with rice grains, [it is distributed among] seven villages.
[22].8) On the twelfth day and on the new moon day, he becomes a milk-consumer; on the new moon day, he eats curd and honey; having poured into his urine water, curd, honey, and washing water,
[22].9) with: "The flesh-devouring fire has entered the channel, child-portion, with the deceit of the Aṅgirases. O you two divine ones, rejoicing, rich in ghee, enter this [man] for the enjoyment of food, svāhā!";
[22].10) at night, he deposits first-fruits rice grains mixed with honey, from one having menses, until the ripening of the barley.
[22].11) In the same manner having sown both types of barley together,
[22].12) he eats [the food] cooked upon a three-layered collection of cow dung.
[22].13) "It is successful," says Kāṅkāyana.
[22].14) With "My splendor, O Agni..." [AVŚ 5.3], having strewn around the sacrificial fires with darbha, pūtīka, and bhāṅgā plants, he eats in the place of the gārhapatya fire [food] cooked on the gārhapatya fire that has residues of oblations on all [fires].
[22].15) In the same manner on the eastern [fire], having collected [the fire] into the two western ones.
[22].16) In this manner, [the rule regarding] ritual fluids in the droṇakalaśa has been stated.

22.s: abhṛṣṭaṃ plakṣa udumbarasya uttarato agnes triṣu camaseṣu pūrvāhṇasya tejasāgram annasya prāśiṣam iti pūrvāhṇe
22.d: अभृष्टं प्लक्ष उदुम्बरस्य उत्तरतो अग्नेस् त्रिषु चमसेषु पूर्वाह्णस्य तेजसाग्रम् अन्नस्य प्राशिषम् इति पूर्वाह्णे

22.s: madhyandinasya tejasā madhyam annasya prāśi.am iti madhyandine
22.d: मध्यन्दिनस्य तेजसा मध्यम् अन्नस्य प्राशि।अम् इति मध्यन्दिने

22.s: aparāhṇasya tejasā sarvam annasya prāśiṣam ity aparāhṇe
22.d: अपराह्णस्य तेजसा सर्वम् अन्नस्य प्राशिषम् इत्य् अपराह्णे

22.s: yat kṣetraṃ kāmayate tasmin kīlālaṃ dadhimadhumiśram
22.d: यत् क्षेत्रं कामयते तस्मिन् कीलालं दधिमधुमिश्रम्

22.s: saṃvatsaraṃ striyam anupetya śuktyāṃ reta ānīya taṇḍulamiśraṃ saptagrāmam
22.d: संवत्सरं स्त्रियम् अनुपेत्य शुक्त्यां रेत आनीय तण्डुलमिश्रं सप्तग्रामम्

22.s: dvādaśīm amāvāsyā iti kṣīrabhakṣo bhavaty amāvāsyāyāṃ dadhimadhubhakṣas tasya mūtre udakadadhimadhupalpūlanāni āsicya
22.d: द्वादशीम् अमावास्या इति क्षीरभक्षो भवत्य् अमावास्यायां दधिमधुभक्षस् तस्य मूत्रे उदकदधिमधुपल्पूलनानि आसिच्य

22.s: kravyādaṃ nāḍī pra viveśāgniṃ prajābhāṅgirato māyayaitau | āvāṃ devī juṣāṇe ghṛtācī imam annādyāya pra viśataṃ svāhā iti
22.d: क्रव्यादं नाडी प्र विवेशाग्निं प्रजाभाङ्गिरतो माययैतौ । आवां देवी जुषाणे घृताची इमम् अन्नाद्याय प्र विशतं स्वाहा इति

22.s: niśāyām āgrayaṇataṇḍulān udakyān madhumiśrān nidadhāty ā yavānāṃ paṅkteḥ
22.d: निशायाम् आग्रयणतण्डुलान् उदक्यान् मधुमिश्रान् निदधात्य् आ यवानां पङ्क्तेः

22.s: mamāgne varco iti sāttrikān agnīn darbhapūtīkabhāṅgābhiḥ paristīrya gārhapatyaśṛtaṃ sarveṣu saṃpātavantaṃ gārhapatyadeśe aśnāti
22.d: ममाग्ने वर्चो इति सात्त्रिकान् अग्नीन् दर्भपूतीकभाङ्गाभिः परिस्तीर्य गार्हपत्यशृतं सर्वेषु संपातवन्तं गार्हपत्यदेशे अश्नाति

23.s: yajūṃṣi yajñe iti navaśālāyāṃ sarpir madhumiśram aśnāti
23.d: यजूंषि यज्ञे इति नवशालायां सर्पिर् मधुमिश्रम् अश्नाति
23.m:
[23].1) With "The sacrificial formulas in the sacrifice..." [AVŚ 5.26], he eats [or: offers] ghee mixed with honey in a new house.
[23].2) With "Sing at night..." [AVŚ 6.1], [he makes] the second [offering].
[23].3) With the two [verses following], [he makes] the third.
[23].4) With [a verse] to Anumati, [he makes] the fourth.
[23].5) Having besprinkled the house with two fingers and seated himself at the mistress of the house's seat, he pours out the water vessel.
[23].6) With "Right here be..." [AVŚ 7.60.7], he releases his speech.
[23].7) With "Upright his..." [AVŚ 5.27], he makes an oblation over a height-amulet made of udumbara wood, resembling a stirring stick.
[23].8) Having cooked an uncounted number of pastries according to seven traditions,
[23].9) with "Tvaṣṭṛ for me...", in the morning, while receiving his share of food, he eats.
[23].10) He ties on a bowstring-amulet.
[23].11) Having wiped a staff that has the residue of oblations, he carries it.
[23].12) With "Vāyu them..." [AVŚ 6.141], in the night of the Citrā constellation of the two yoked [stars], he makes ritual equipment endowed with the residue of oblations.
[23].13) On the following day, with "Vāyu them..." [AVŚ 6.141], he circumambulates the cows with a branch and a stream of water.
[23].14) Having placed a piece of wood from the first-born [tree], with a knife of udumbara wood, he performs what is stated in the mantra with "With blood..." [AVŚ 6.141.2].
[23].15) With "As they have done..." [AVŚ 6.141.3], having wiped away the blood with a stalk of reed, he eats it mixed with ritual fluids.
[23].16) Everything is made of udumbara wood.
[23].17) With "Whose is this..." [AVŚ 6.33], is the union of the yoke-ties.

23.s: śālām aṅgulibhyāṃ saṃprokṣya gṛhapatnyāsāda upaviśya udapātraṃ ninayati
23.d: शालाम् अङ्गुलिभ्यां संप्रोक्ष्य गृहपत्न्यासाद उपविश्य उदपात्रं निनयति

23.s: ūrdhvā asya iti vārṣmaṇam audumbaraṃ manthapratirūpam abhijuhoti
23.d: ऊर्ध्वा अस्य इति वार्ष्मणम् औदुम्बरं मन्थप्रतिरूपम् अभिजुहोति

23.s: tvaṣṭā me iti prātar vibhakṣyamāṇo aśnāti
23.d: त्वष्टा मे इति प्रातर् विभक्ष्यमाणो अश्नाति

23.s: vāyur enāḥ iti yuktayoś citrākarma niśāyāṃ saṃbhārān saṃpātavataḥ karoti
23.d: वायुर् एनाः इति युक्तयोश् चित्राकर्म निशायां संभारान् संपातवतः करोति

23.s: aparedyur vāyur enāḥ iti śākhayā udakadhārayā gāḥ parikrāmati
23.d: अपरेद्युर् वायुर् एनाः इति शाखया उदकधारया गाः परिक्रामति

23.s: prathamajasya śakalam avadhāya audumbareṇāsinā lohitena iti mantroktam
23.d: प्रथमजस्य शकलम् अवधाय औदुम्बरेणासिना लोहितेन इति मन्त्रोक्तम्

23.s: yathā cakrur itīkṣukāśakāṇḍyā lohitaṃ nirmṛjya rasamiśram aśnāti
23.d: यथा चक्रुर् इतीक्षुकाशकाण्ड्या लोहितं निर्मृज्य रसमिश्रम् अश्नाति

24.m: [24].1) With the verse "Raise yourself up [6.142]", the bringing forth of the seed takes place. / [24].2) Having turned up [the soil] with the plowshare in fertile cultivated land, he pours out [and] sows barley grains mixed with ghee along the furrow, verse by verse. / [24].3) With "Unto that [7.14]", in an extensive open space, in a forest, upon high ground, in an enclosed pavilion having an eastern and a western door, he brings down the residues of oblations into water. / [24].4) He sorts out stalks of soma upon a black antelope skin. / [24].5) He consumes [the portion] possessing residues of oblations with [curds or water] mixed with soma. / [24].6) When [the fire is] blazing, [the offering is] accomplished. / [24].7) With "That, O Savitṛ [7.15]", he ties the tether of a cow that has calved once. / [24].8) With "Let them sprinkle me together [7.33]", [he offers] mixed grain in all kinds of water. / [24].9) With "The divine eagle [7.39]", he sacrifices to Indra with the omentum of a staff-bearing bull. / [24].10) Having covered the cowshed with the hide along with its head and feet still attached, he feeds the brahmins with what is made into cut portions. / [24].11) Having returned from a journey and taken firewood sticks, he mutters in view of the house: "Bearing vigour [7.60]". / [24].12) Having supported the eaves of the house with his right hand and holding the firewood sticks with the left, he mutters. / [24].13) Having stepped past and placed the firewood sticks [on the fire], he grasps the two posts and worships them, saying: "O auspicious ones, possessing offspring, gentle, may I, the master of the house, live long with you!" / [24].14) [He performs] what is stated in the mantra: "What I speak [12.1.58]". / [24].15) Sitting down at the seat of the house-mistress, he pours down the water vessel. / [24].16) About to go abroad on a journey, he looks on with: "Remain right here [7.60.7]". / [24].17) With "From rich pasture [7.73.11]", he stations the cattle in rich pasture. / [24].18) Having drawn water into his folded palms with dūrvā grass-tips, he worships the new moon with the verses addressed to the new moon. / [24].19) With "Indra's belly [7.111]" [and] "The thousandfold [9.4]", he sets free a bull treated with the residues of oblations, / [24].20) [reciting:] "For the bearing of seed I release you; for the bearing of vitality I release you; for herd-hood I release you; for flock-hood I release you; for thousandfold thriving I release you; for boundless thriving I release you!" / [24].21) With "This youth of yours [9.4.24]", having turned away the old [bull], he releases the new one and besprinkles it. / [24].22) One desirous of prosperity sacrifices to Indra with a bull according to the subsequent [rule]. / [24].23) One desirous of wealth [sacrifices] with a white [bull] on the full moon day. / [24].24) With "Truth, great [12.1]", [he performs the rite] on the Āgrahāyaṇī day. / [24].25) Behind the fire, on darbha grass, in a pit, [he makes] a completely burnt offering. / [24].26) He consumes the second [portion] possessing the residues of oblations. / [24].27) With the seven [verses] of the third [section, beginning with] "Aditi" [and] "O Mother Earth [12.1.63]", he offers three times. / [24].28) Having spread a mat of darbha grass behind the fire, he sits down with "The cleansing one [… ]". / [24].29) With "Those auspicious [forms] of yours [9.2.25]", he lies down. / [24].30) With "As lying down [… ]", he turns over. / [24].31) With nine [verses], with the tenth beginning "Auspicious [12.1.59]", [and] with "Up with life [3.31.10]", he stands up. / [24].32) With "Upwards we [7.53.7]", he strides forth. / [24].33) Having stepped outside toward the east or north with three steps using "Rising up [12.1.28]", he looks around with: "As far as your [12.1.33]". / [24].34) And from an elevated spot. / [24].35) In front of the fire, he sprinkles the yoked plow with a water vessel possessing the residues of oblations. / [24].36) This is the conclusion of the yoking rites. / [24].37) He offers with: "On which are the sadas and the havirdhāna [12.1.38–40]", thinking: 'A suitor will come to me.' / [24].38) He worships with: "On which is food [12.1.42]". / [24].39) One desirous of gold [binds on] an amulet with: "Bearing treasure [12.1.44–45]". / [24].40) Having thus found [wealth]. / [24].41) With "On which black [12.1.52]", he sips water from [a pool] made by rain and brings it over his head. / [24].42) With "When you the dappled mare in the chariot [13.1.21–26]", the sky is the dappled mare, the sun is the ruddy one. / [24].43) He gives a dappled cow [as dakṣiṇā]. / [24].44) A rice-mess cooked in milk from a dappled [cow] is offered as a completely burnt oblation. / [24].45) This is the laying down and worship for rites of prosperity. / [24].46) One desirous of all desires [performs this rite] with waters; one desirous of all desires with waters.

24.s: ājyamiśrān yavān urvarāyāṃ kṛṣṭe phālena uduhyānvṛcaṃ kāśīn ninayati nivapati
24.d: आज्यमिश्रान् यवान् उर्वरायां कृष्टे फालेन उदुह्यान्वृचं काशीन् निनयति निवपति

24.s: abhi tyam iti mahāvakāśe araṇya unnate vimite prāgdvārapratyagdvāreṣv apsu saṃpātān ānayati
24.d: अभि त्यम् इति महावकाशे अरण्य उन्नते विमिते प्राग्द्वारप्रत्यग्द्वारेष्व् अप्सु संपातान् आनयति

24.s: saṃ mā siñcantu iti sarvodake maiśradhānyam
24.d: सं मा सिञ्चन्तु इति सर्वोदके मैश्रधान्यम्

24.s: divyaṃ suparṇaṃ ity ṛṣabhadaṇḍino vapayā indraṃ yajate
24.d: दिव्यं सुपर्णं इत्य् ऋषभदण्डिनो वपया इन्द्रं यजते

24.s: proṣya samidha ādāya ūrjaṃ bibhrad iti gṛhasaṃkāśe japati
24.d: प्रोष्य समिध आदाय ऊर्जं बिभ्रद् इति गृहसंकाशे जपति

24.s: savyena samidho dakṣiṇena śālāvalīkaṃ saṃstabhya japati
24.d: सव्येन समिधो दक्षिणेन शालावलीकं संस्तभ्य जपति

24.s: ativrajya samidha ādhāya sumaṅgali prajāvati suśīme ahaṃ vāṃ gṛhapatir jīvyāsam iti sthūṇe gṛhṇāty upatiṣṭhate
24.d: अतिव्रज्य समिध आधाय सुमङ्गलि प्रजावति सुशीमे अहं वां गृहपतिर् जीव्यासम् इति स्थूणे गृह्णात्य् उपतिष्ठते

24.s: dūrvāgrair añjalau apa ānīya darśaṃ dārśībhir upatiṣṭhate
24.d: दूर्वाग्रैर् अञ्जलौ अप आनीय दर्शं दार्शीभिर् उपतिष्ठते

24.s: indrasya kukṣir sāhasras ity ṛṣabhaṃ saṃpātavantam atisṛjati
24.d: इन्द्रस्य कुक्षिर् साहस्रस् इत्य् ऋषभं संपातवन्तम् अतिसृजति

24.s: retodhāyai tvātisṛjāmi vayodhāyai tvātisṛjāmi yūthatvāyai tvātisṛjāmi gaṇatvāyai tvātisṛjāmi sahasrapoṣāyai tvātisṛjāmy aparimitapos.āyai tvātisṛjāmi
24.d: रेतोधायै त्वातिसृजामि वयोधायै त्वातिसृजामि यूथत्वायै त्वातिसृजामि गणत्वायै त्वातिसृजामि सहस्रपोषायै त्वातिसृजाम्य् अपरिमितपोस्।आयै त्वातिसृजामि

24.s: etaṃ vo yuvānaṃ iti purāṇaṃ pravṛtya navam utsṛjate saṃprokṣati
24.d: एतं वो युवानं इति पुराणं प्रवृत्य नवम् उत्सृजते संप्रोक्षति

24.s: tṛtīyasyāditiḥ saptabhir bhūme mātar iti trir juhoti
24.d: तृतीयस्यादितिः सप्तभिर् भूमे मातर् इति त्रिर् जुहोति

24.s: paścād agner darbheṣu kaśipu āstīrya vimṛgvarīṃ ity upaviśati
24.d: पश्चाद् अग्नेर् दर्भेषु कशिपु आस्तीर्य विमृग्वरीं इत्य् उपविशति

24.s: navabhiḥ śantivā iti daśamyā ud āyuṣā ity upottiṣṭhati
24.d: नवभिः शन्तिवा इति दशम्या उद् आयुषा इत्य् उपोत्तिष्ठति

24.s: udīrāṇā iti trīṇi padāni prāṅ vā udaṅ vā bāhyena upaniṣkramya yāvat te iti vīkṣate
24.d: उदीराणा इति त्रीणि पदानि प्राङ् वा उदङ् वा बाह्येन उपनिष्क्रम्य यावत् ते इति वीक्षते

24.s: purastād agneḥ sīraṃ yuktam udapātreṇa saṃpātavatāvasiñcati
24.d: पुरस्ताद् अग्नेः सीरं युक्तम् उदपात्रेण संपातवतावसिञ्चति

24.s: yasyāṃ sadohavirdhāne iti juhoti varo ma āgamiṣyatīti
24.d: यस्यां सदोहविर्धाने इति जुहोति वरो म आगमिष्यतीति

24.s: yasyāṃ kṛṣṇam iti vārṣakṛtasyācamati śirasy ānayate
24.d: यस्यां कृष्णम् इति वार्षकृतस्याचमति शिरस्य् आनयते

24.s: yaṃ tvā pṛṣatī rathe iti dyauḥ pṛṣaty ādityo rohitaḥ
24.d: यं त्वा पृषती रथे इति द्यौः पृषत्य् आदित्यो रोहितः

25.m:
[25].1) Now the medical rites.
[25].2) A disease having its characteristic symptom is to be treated medically.
[25].3) Otherwise when there is an explicit statement.
[25].4) With a water vessel containing the residue of oblations from the preceding rite, he anoints him.
[25].5) He wipes the folds of skin.
[25].6) With "We know the reed's…" [1.2.1] and "That which there…" [2.3.1 etc.], he binds the top part of muñja reed with a cord.
[25].7) Having drawn around a shaped clod and an ant-hill, he makes [him] drink [their dissolved earth].
[25].8) He anoints him with clarified butter.
[25].9) He blows upon him.
[25].10) With "We know the reed's…" [1.3.1], he binds the organ of urination.
[25].11) He makes [him] drink [a mixture of] earth thrown up by a rat, pūtīka, churned sour milk, old pramanda, and sap of trees.
[25].12) With the last two [verses], he causes [him] to stand firmly.
[25].13) He mounts a vehicle.
[25].14) He shoots an arrow.
[25].15) He loosens the bladder.
[25].16) He breaks the obstruction.
[25].17) Having brought twenty-one barley grains into a milk-pail with water, and having placed a wooden mallet at the buttocks, he pours it out from the front.
[25].18) He makes him drink a decoction of ālabisola.
[25].19) And for one suffering from upward movement of wind.
[25].20) And "The mothers go…" [1.4.1] and "Purified by the wind…" are pacifying verses.
[25].21) For the following one, they are combined with Soma.
[25].22) [The rite] of the expulsion hymns is explained by the driving away [of demons].
[25].23) He lays on [firewood sticks] of tin, a pestle, khadira, and tārṣṭāgha.
[25].24) With "Pierce both eyes!" [5.29.4], he drives an uneven number of khadira pegs into the ground level behind the fire.
[25].25) In the same manner, [pegs] of iron and copper.
[25].26) With heated gravel he scatters around the bed and the heaps of grain.
[25].27) On the new moon day, having scattered [grass] for sorcery, he puts into the kindling wood of tārṣṭāgha once-grasped barley grains, unbroken, not ground by turning back the pestle.
[25].28) If someone should approach, he should say to him: 'Wiping your tongue with a hemp cord, leap down from the hall!'
[25].29) While he does so, [the sorcerer] not partaking of food, when [the adversary] is subdued,
[25].30) he offers into a leaf-cone ingiḍa [oil] mixed with the down of vīriṇa reed.
[25].31) He hangs the kindling wood and the sacrificial grass in the hall.
[25].32) On the next day, if there is a change, it breaks from the Piśāca.
[25].33) The oblation has been explained.
[25].34) Having made anjali to Vaiśravaṇa, while murmuring [the mantra], he sips water and besprinkles [himself].
[25].35) At night he rubs together two firebrands.
[25].36) He performs the Svastyādya rite.
[25].37) With "This of the gods…" [1.10.1], together with twenty-one tufts of darbha grass and roof-slats, he pours [water] down upon his head.

25.s: vidmā śarasya ado yad iti muñjaśiro rajjvā badhnāti
25.d: विद्मा शरस्य अदो यद् इति मुञ्जशिरो रज्ज्वा बध्नाति

25.s: ekaviṃśatiṃ yavān dohanyām adbhir ānīya drughnīṃ jaghane saṃstabhya phalato avasiñcati
25.d: एकविंशतिं यवान् दोहन्याम् अद्भिर् आनीय द्रुघ्नीं जघने संस्तभ्य फलतो अवसिञ्चति

25.s: ambayo yanty vāyoḥ pūtaḥ iti ca śāntāḥ
25.d: अम्बयो यन्त्य् वायोः पूतः इति च शान्ताः

25.s: ayugmān khādirān śaṅkūn akṣyau ni vidhya iti paścād agneḥ samaṃbhūmi nihanti
25.d: अयुग्मान् खादिरान् शङ्कून् अक्ष्यौ नि विध्य इति पश्चाद् अग्नेः समंभूमि निहन्ति

25.s: amāvāsyāyāṃ sakṛdgṛhītān yavān anapahatān apratīhārapiṣṭān ābhicārikaṃ paristīrya tārṣṭāghedhma āvapati
25.d: अमावास्यायां सकृद्गृहीतान् यवान् अनपहतान् अप्रतीहारपिष्टान् आभिचारिकं परिस्तीर्य तार्ष्टाघेध्म आवपति

25.s: ya āgachet taṃ brūyāt śaṇaśulbena jihvāṃ nirmṛjānaḥ śālāyāḥ praskanda iti
25.d: य आगछेत् तं ब्रूयात् शणशुल्बेन जिह्वां निर्मृजानः शालायाः प्रस्कन्द इति

25.s: ayaṃ devānām iti ekaviṃśatyā darbhapiñjūlībhir valīkaiḥ sārdham adhiśiro avasiñcati
25.d: अयं देवानाम् इति एकविंशत्या दर्भपिञ्जूलीभिर् वलीकैः सार्धम् अधिशिरो अवसिञ्चति

26.s: jarāyujaḥ iti medo madhu sarpis tailaṃ pāyayati
26.d: जरायुजः इति मेदो मधु सर्पिस् तैलं पाययति
26.m:
[26].1) With "Born from the womb…" [1.12.1], he makes him drink fat, honey, clarified butter, and sesamum oil.
[26].2) Covered on his head with a braided muñja-plaited mat, holding husked grains in a sieve with his left hand, scattering them with his right, he walks away.
[26].3) With his left hand [he holds] the sieve and the plaited mat; with his right, the bowstring and the wooden mallet.
[26].4) The summoner walks in front.
[26].5) Where the disease seizes him, there he places the sieve and the plaited mat;
[26].6) and the bowstring;
[26].7) [and] the return [is performed].
[26].8) Ghee is poured into the nostrils.
[26].9) Having pressed the forehead with a five-jointed [reed], he murmurs "Those which…" [1.17.1].
[26].10) He scatters dust and sand around with a five-jointed [reed].
[26].11) He binds an armakapālikā [plant].
[26].12) He makes [him] drink [it].
[26].13) With four tips of dūrvā grass, he makes [him] drink curds and sesamum-cake.
[26].14) With "Following the sun…" [1.22.1], he causes him to sip [water] mixed with the hair of what is mentioned in the mantra.
[26].15) And having poured it over his back,
[26].16) he binds a peg-container with the residue of oblations upon milk for one seated upon a hide.
[26].17) He makes him drink [milk].
[26].18) Having fed him turmeric-rice, having smeared the left-overs [of the patient] with the left-over food down to his feet, having bound what is mentioned in the mantra below the bed to his left shanks with a yellow thread, he bathes him.
[26].19) He makes him go forth.
[26].20) As [a bird] chirps, he makes him attend.
[26].21) Having smeared hairs from the breast with lac, having covered it with gold,
[26].22) with "Born at night…" [1.23.1] and "The well-winged bird is born…" [1.24.1], having rubbed what is mentioned in the mantra with dung until it becomes reddish, he anoints [him].
[26].23) Having pulled out the gray hairs,
[26].24) covered with leaves of the māruta tree.
[26].25) With "Since Agni…" [1.25.1], murmuring, he heats an axe, boils [water with it], and pours it over [him].
[26].26) With "She has approached…" [1.28.1], for one trembling, he binds four stalks of vīriṇa reed with white flowers that have been singed at both ends;
[26].27) a reed-amulet singed in three ways.
[26].28) On a firebrand, [the rite] beginning with the Svastyātreya.
[26].29) Having offered powders of all fragrant substances mixed with the two Maternal Demon hymns, he anoints with the remainder.
[26].30) And at a crossroad, on the head, in a ring of darbha grass, on an earthen potsherd filled with burning coals, [the offerings] are smeared with the residue.
[26].31) Stepping against [the current], he winnows with a sieve; the other pours water from behind.
[26].32) Having thrown and poured it into an unbaked pot, he binds it to a three-legged stool of muñja grass at a bird's roosting-place.
[26].33) With "Hated by evil…" [2.7.1], "May the goddess bring us bliss…" [2.25.1], "The varaṇa…" [6.85.1], "The pippalī…" [6.109.1], "Of the abscess…" [6.127.1], and "Those which are brown…" [8.7.1];
[26].34) with the penultimate [hymn], he anoints with a four-finger-long palāśa piece;
[26].35) with the first, he binds what is mentioned in the mantra;
[26].36) with the second, he anoints with the residue of oblations of what is mentioned in the mantra;
[26].37) with the third, he binds what is mentioned in the mantra;
[26].38) with the fourth, he feeds [him];
[26].39) with the fifth, he brings the residue of oblations onto the head of one seized by Varuṇa;
[26].40) with the last, a splint [is bound].
[26].41) With "The two have arisen…" [2.8.1], he washes [him] outside.
[26].42) With "May it go away…" [2.8.2], at dawn.
[26].43) With "Of the brown…" [2.8.3], having drawn around what is mentioned in the mantra upon a shaped clod and an ant-hill, and having sewn it up into a live-skin pouch, he binds it.

26.s: mauñjapraśnena śirasi apihitaḥ savyena tita-uni pūlyāni dhārayamāṇo dakṣiṇenāvakiran vrajati
26.d: मौञ्जप्रश्नेन शिरसि अपिहितः सव्येन तित-उनि पूल्यानि धारयमाणो दक्षिणेनावकिरन् व्रजति

26.s: yatra enaṃ vyādhir gṛhṇāti tatra tita-upraśnau nidadhāti
26.d: यत्र एनं व्याधिर् गृह्णाति तत्र तित-उप्रश्नौ निदधाति

26.s: pañcaparvaṇā lalāṭaṃ saṃstabhya japati amūr yā iti
26.d: पञ्चपर्वणा ललाटं संस्तभ्य जपति अमूर् या इति

26.s: anu sūryam iti mantroktasya lomamiśram ācamayati
26.d: अनु सूर्यम् इति मन्त्रोक्तस्य लोममिश्रम् आचमयति

26.s: śaṅkudhānaṃ carmaṇi āsīnāya dugdhe saṃpātavantaṃ badhnāti
26.d: शङ्कुधानं चर्मणि आसीनाय दुग्धे संपातवन्तं बध्नाति

26.s: haridraudanabhuktam ucchiṣṭān ucchiṣṭenā prapadāt pralipya mantroktān adhastalpe haritasūtreṇa savyajaṅghāsu baddhvāvasnāpayati
26.d: हरिद्रौदनभुक्तम् उच्छिष्टान् उच्छिष्टेना प्रपदात् प्रलिप्य मन्त्रोक्तान् अधस्तल्पे हरितसूत्रेण सव्यजङ्घासु बद्ध्वावस्नापयति

26.s: naktaṃjātā suparṇo jātaḥ iti mantroktaṃ śakṛdā ālohitaṃ praghṛṣyālimpati
26.d: नक्तंजाता सुपर्णो जातः इति मन्त्रोक्तं शकृदा आलोहितं प्रघृष्यालिम्पति

26.s: yad agnir iti paraśuṃ japan tāpayati kvāthayati avasiñcati
26.d: यद् अग्निर् इति परशुं जपन् तापयति क्वाथयति अवसिञ्चति

26.s: upa prāgād iti udvijamānasya śuklaprasūnasya vīriṇasya catasṛṇām iṣīkāṇām ubhayataḥ pratyuṣṭaṃ badhnāti
26.d: उप प्रागाद् इति उद्विजमानस्य शुक्लप्रसूनस्य वीरिणस्य चतसृणाम् इषीकाणाम् उभयतः प्रत्युष्टं बध्नाति

26.s: mātṛnāmnoḥ sarvasurabhicūrṇāni anvaktāni hutvā śeṣeṇa pralimpati
26.d: मातृनाम्नोः सर्वसुरभिचूर्णानि अन्वक्तानि हुत्वा शेषेण प्रलिम्पति

26.s: catuṣpathe ca śirasi darbheṇḍve aṅgārakapāle anvaktāni
26.d: चतुष्पथे च शिरसि दर्भेण्ड्वे अङ्गारकपाले अन्वक्तानि

26.s: tita-uni pratīpaṃ gāhamāno vapatītaro avasiñcati paścāt
26.d: तित-उनि प्रतीपं गाहमानो वपतीतरो अवसिञ्चति पश्चात्

26.s: āmapātre opyāsicya mauñje tripāde vayoniveśane prabadhnāti
26.d: आमपात्रे ओप्यासिच्य मौञ्जे त्रिपादे वयोनिवेशने प्रबध्नाति

26.s: aghadviṣṭā śaṃ no devī varaṇo pippalī vidradhasya yā babhravo iti
26.d: अघद्विष्टा शं नो देवी वरणो पिप्पली विद्रधस्य या बभ्रवो इति

26.s: babhror iti mantroktam ākṛtiloṣṭavalmīkau parilikhya jīvakoṣaṇyām utsīvya badhnāti
26.d: बभ्रोर् इति मन्त्रोक्तम् आकृतिलोष्टवल्मीकौ परिलिख्य जीवकोषण्याम् उत्सीव्य बध्नाति

27.s: namas te lāṅgalebhyo iti sīrayogam adhiśiro avasiñcati
27.d: नमस् ते लाङ्गलेभ्यो इति सीरयोगम् अधिशिरो अवसिञ्चति
27.m:
[27].1) With "Homage to your plows..." (AV 2.8.4), he pours over the plow-harness placed over the head.
[27].2) With "Homage to the ones with drooping eyes..." (AV 2.8.5), he pours residues of oblations into water in an empty hut.
[27].3) The following [mantra] in an old ditch covered with hut-straw.
[27].4) In that [water] he makes [him] sip, and bathes [him].
[27].5) With "O ten-tree..." (AV 2.9.1), [an amulet] made of ten kinds of wood [is used].
[27].6) Ten friends touch [him] while reciting.
[27].7) With "From hereditary disease thee..." (AV 2.10.1), having bound [amulets] of kām-pīla splinters on his joints at a crossroads, he bathes [him] with bundles of grass.
[27].8) He sprinkles [him].
[27].9) With "Of the earthly..." (AV 2.29.1), he seats two persons back-to-back at sunrise.
[27].10) Having seated the sick person facing east and the healthy person facing west on branches, in a wicker cup, using two stirring sticks, having stirred up a mash on the head of the thirst-stricken one, he hands the mash to the one who is not thirsty.
[27].11) Into that [cup] he brings grass.
[27].12) He makes [him] drink drawn water.
[27].13) With "Living together..." (AV 2.29.6c), [he does] as stated in the mantra.
[27].14) With "That great [mill-stone] of Indra..." (AV 2.31.1), he offers sesame stalks, alāṇḍu worms, and killing-instruments mixed with ghee.
[27].15) Having wound hair around a spotted reed counter-clockwise, he splits it.
[27].16) He heats it.
[27].17) He puts it [on the fire].
[27].18) Facing south, having stirred up dust with the left hand, he scatters it around.
[27].19) He crushes [it].
[27].20) He puts it [on the fire].
[27].21) With "The sun rising..." (AV 2.32.1), as [the sun] rises, he says: "Cows' name... such-and-such a one!"
[27].22) At the end of the hymn, [he says]: "They are slain!"
[27].23) He throws [them into the fire] with darbha grass stalks.
[27].24) And at midday.
[27].25) In the afternoon, facing west.
[27].26) Having plucked a tuft of hair, [he offers it with] sesame seeds and the rest.
[27].27) With "From your eyes..." (AV 2.33.1), [he performs] the pulling-out rite.
[27].28) He pours over [him] with a water vessel containing residues of oblations.
[27].29) With "Of the antelope..." (AV 3.7.1), through binding [an amulet], making [him] drink, sipping water, and [heating] with the flame of roasted grain [on] pegs, he pours over [him] when the asterism has set.
[27].30) He throws in barley seized once from an unmeasured amount.
[27].31) He gives cooked food.
[27].32) With "I release thee..." (AV 3.11.1), [he offers] boiled rice with rotten carp in a village.
[27].33) In the forest, he pours over [him] with the flame of sesame, hemp, and dried cow-dung when the asterism has set.
[27].34) With the Mṛgāra hymns, saying "Release!", he bathes [him].

27.s: namaḥ sanisrasākṣebhyo iti śūnyaśālāyām apsu saṃpātān ānayati
27.d: नमः सनिस्रसाक्षेभ्यो इति शून्यशालायाम् अप्सु संपातान् आनयति

27.s: kṣetriyāt tvā iti catuṣpathe kāmpīlaśakalaiḥ parvasu baddhvā piñjūlībhir āplāvayati
27.d: क्षेत्रियात् त्वा इति चतुष्पथे काम्पीलशकलैः पर्वसु बद्ध्वा पिञ्जूलीभिर् आप्लावयति

27.s: prāṅmukhaṃ vyādhitam pratyaṅmukham avyādhitaṃ śākhāsūpaveśya vaitase camase upamanthanībhyāṃ tṛṣṇāgṛhītasya śirasi mantham upamathyātṛṣitāya prayachati
27.d: प्राङ्मुखं व्याधितम् प्रत्यङ्मुखम् अव्याधितं शाखासूपवेश्य वैतसे चमसे उपमन्थनीभ्यां तृष्णागृहीतस्य शिरसि मन्थम् उपमथ्यातृषिताय प्रयछति

27.s: indrasya yā mahī iti khalvaṅgān alāṇḍūn hananān ghṛtamiśrān juhoti
27.d: इन्द्रस्य या मही इति खल्वङ्गान् अलाण्डून् हननान् घृतमिश्रान् जुहोति

27.s: bālān kalmāṣe kāṇḍe savyaṃ pariveṣṭya saṃbhinatti
27.d: बालान् कल्माषे काण्डे सव्यं परिवेष्ट्य संभिनत्ति

27.s: udyann ādityaḥ iti udyati gonāma iti āhāsau iti
27.d: उद्यन्न् आदित्यः इति उद्यति गोनाम इति आहासौ इति

27.s: muñcāmi tvā iti grāmye pūtiśapharībhir odanam
27.d: मुञ्चामि त्वा इति ग्राम्ये पूतिशफरीभिर् ओदनम्

28.s: brāhmaṇo jajñe iti takṣakāyāñjaliṃ kṛtvā japann ācamayati abhyuks.ati
28.d: ब्राह्मणो जज्ञे इति तक्षकायाञ्जलिं कृत्वा जपन्न् आचमयति अभ्युक्स्।अति
28.m:
[28].1) With "The brāhmaṇa was born..." (AV 4.6.1), having made an añjali to Takṣaka, while muttering [the mantra] he makes [him] sip water and besprinkles [him].
[28].2) Having crushed a splinter of kṛmuka wood, by the flame of a coarse garment, old skin, and scrapings [he cures him].
[28].3) In a water vessel containing residues of oblations, having stirred up a mash with two smeared sticks whose fruit points upward, scattering rice-balls that preserve wealth stanza by stanza, he makes [him] vomit.
[28].4) He makes [him] drink turmeric in ghee.
[28].5) With "O healer..." (AV 4.12.1), he pours over [him] when the asterism has set.
[28].6) He makes [him] drink coagulated milk mixed with ghee, and anoints him.
[28].7) With "He sees..." (AV 4.20.1), he binds an amulet of sadaṃpuṣpā.
[28].8) With "O Bhava and Śarva..." (AV 4.28.1), having made seven kāmpīla leaf-cups filled with water containing residues of oblations, having poured them out to the south, he throws them away behind.
[28].9) With "Filled by thee..." (AV 4.37.1), [he puts] powder of śamī wood into the cooked food using a cup.
[28].10) [He puts it] into his ornament.
[28].11) He surrounds the hut [with it].
[28].12) With "And whose breath of life is immortal..." (AV 5.1.7), he gives cooked food to one possessed by folly.
[28].13) With the mantras mentioning kuṣṭha, he anoints [him] repeatedly without interruption with [kuṣṭha] mixed with fresh butter.
[28].14) With the mantras mentioning lākṣā, he makes [him] drink infusions in milk.
[28].15) With "The sacred knowledge born first..." (AV 5.6.1), he makes a woman in childbed and a damaged person step out.
[28].16) [There is] a mash, sipping water, and attendance on the sun.
[28].17) With "To heaven, svāhā!" (AV 5.9.1) and "This barley..." (AV 6.91.1), he pours four residues of oblations into a water vessel.
[28].18) Two upon the earth.
[28].19) Having brought those two back, he bathes [him].
[28].20) And with the subsequent [hymn] containing barley, he binds a barley [amulet].

28.s: saṃpātavati udapātre ūrdhvaphalābhyāṃ digdhābhyāṃ mantham upamathya rayidhāraṇapiṇḍān anvṛcaṃ prakīrya chardayate
28.d: संपातवति उदपात्रे ऊर्ध्वफलाभ्यां दिग्धाभ्यां मन्थम् उपमथ्य रयिधारणपिण्डान् अन्वृचं प्रकीर्य छर्दयते

28.s: bhavāśarvau iti sapta kāmpīlapuṭān apāṃ pūrṇān saṃpātavataḥ kṛtvā dakṣiṇenāvasicya paścād apavidhyati
28.d: भवाशर्वौ इति सप्त काम्पीलपुटान् अपां पूर्णान् संपातवतः कृत्वा दक्षिणेनावसिच्य पश्चाद् अपविध्यति

28.s: tvayā pūrṇam iti kośena śamīcūrṇāni bhakte
28.d: त्वया पूर्णम् इति कोशेन शमीचूर्णानि भक्ते

28.s: dive svāhā imaṃ yavam iti catura udapātre saṃpātān ānayati
28.d: दिवे स्वाहा इमं यवम् इति चतुर उदपात्रे संपातान् आनयति

29.s: dadir hi iti takṣakāya iti uktam
29.d: ददिर् हि इति तक्षकाय इति उक्तम्
29.m:
[29].1) With "For the giver..." (AV 5.13.1), it has been prescribed [in the rite] for Takṣaka.
[29].2) With the second [verse, a rite with] the catching [instrument is done].
[29].3) He walks around counter-clockwise.
[29].4) He ties clumps [of grass] in the fringe of his hair-tuft.
[29].5) With the third, [the rite with] the releasing [instrument is done].
[29].6) With the fourth, with the right hand, with "Go away!" (AV 7.88), having stroked the bite with blades of grass, he flings away towards the serpent,
[29].7) from where he was bitten.
[29].8) With the fifth, [he cures him] by the flame of straw and husks.
[29].9) With the sixth, with a loop of a bowstring from the notch of the bow.
[29].10) With two [verses], he makes [him] drink boils of madhūka.
[29].11) With the ninth, porcupine excrement [is used].
[29].12) With the [verse containing] three white words, he makes [him] eat meat.
[29].13) With the tenth, he makes [him] sip water from a bottle-gourd.
[29].14) With the eleventh, he binds his navel.
[29].15) With the verses mentioning madhula and the bull, having pounded bald-tailed leaf, he makes [him] drink it in honeyed mash.
[29].16) With the following [verses], he eats.
[29].17) He opens the door.
[29].18) With "Agni [driving away] the fever..." (AV 5.22.1), he makes [him] drink parched grain.
[29].19) During a forest fire, he pours residues of oblations upon his head using a red vessel.
[29].20) With "Woven for me..." (AV 5.23.1), [he takes] a piece of karīra root with a stalk,
[29].21) [and] dust from a village.
[29].22) Behind the fire, in the mother's lap, with the bottom of a pestle smeared with fresh butter, he heats his palate three times repeatedly.
[29].23) He smears [him] with śigru leaves mixed with fresh butter.
[29].24) Twenty-one uśīra roots, as stated in the mantra: "I split..." (AV 5.23.13c).
[29].25) He hands over the uśīra roots.
[29].26) He bathes [him] along with the twenty-one [roots].
[29].27) With "Whom they enter..." (AV 6.2.2), he eats milk-rice cooked at the roosting of birds.
[29].28) With "As around heaven..." (AV 6.12.1), he makes [him] drink mead-liquor,
[29].29) and mutters [the mantra].
[29].30) With "The loosening of the bones..." (AV 6.14.1), he pours over [him] into a reed-mat with a splinter, in water containing residues of oblations.

29.s: caturthyā dakṣiṇam apehy iti daṃśma tṛṇaiḥ prakarṣyāhim abhinirasyati
29.d: चतुर्थ्या दक्षिणम् अपेह्य् इति दंश्म तृणैः प्रकर्ष्याहिम् अभिनिरस्यति

29.s: ote me iti karīramūlaṃ kāṇḍena ekadeśam
29.d: ओते मे इति करीरमूलं काण्डेन एकदेशम्

29.s: paścād agner mātur upasthe musalabudhnena navanītānvaktena triḥ pratīhāraṃ tālūni tāpayati
29.d: पश्चाद् अग्नेर् मातुर् उपस्थे मुसलबुध्नेन नवनीतान्वक्तेन त्रिः प्रतीहारं तालूनि तापयति

29.s: ā yaṃ viśanti iti vayoniveśanaśṛtaṃ kṣīraudanam aśnāti
29.d: आ यं विशन्ति इति वयोनिवेशनशृतं क्षीरौदनम् अश्नाति

29.s: pari dyām iva iti madhuśībhaṃ pāyayati
29.d: परि द्याम् इव इति मधुशीभं पाययति

30.m: [30].1) With the verse 'ābayo...' (AVŚ 6.16.1), he binds [upon the patient] mustard oil containing the oblation residues, / [30].2) after smearing a stalk. / [30].3) He gives him mixed vegetable [food]. / [30].4) He gives him four vegetable fruits. / [30].5) He anoints himself with a milk linctus. / [30].6) He eats. / [30].7) With the verse 'agner iva...' (AVŚ 6.20.1), [the rite] has been stated in [the section on] forest fire. / [30].8) With the hymn 'imā yas tisraḥ...' (AVŚ 6.21.1), he sprinkles [him] with [the heat of] a flame produced on a tree-ground, / [30].9) along with head-infusions and akṣa [berries], / [30].10) [and] with two adjacent [items]. / [30].11) With the hymn 'kṛṣṇaṃ niyānaṃ...' (AVŚ 6.22.1), he causes [fluid] to drip upon [him] with an herb. / [30].12) [There is] the absorption of the Maruts. / [30].13) With the hymn 'himavataḥ...' (AVŚ 6.24.1), having fetched [water] along the stream from a flowing [river], [he sprinkles him] with roof-thatchings. / [30].14) With the hymn 'pañca ca yā...' (AVŚ 6.25.1), he sets fifty-five axe-leaves on fire with pieces of wood. / [30].15) He smears with a stick [the matter] cooked in an earthen vessel. / [30].16) He causes [him] to be bitten by a kiṃstya insect, horsefly, jāmbīla insect, water-fly, mosquito, and the like. / [30].17) At night, with the hymn 'ava mā pāpman...' (AVŚ 6.26.1), having poured empty grains into a sieve and discarded [them], / [30].18) on the next day, he offers tribute offerings to Sahasrākṣa in the waters; having thrown three rolled-up sacrificial cakes at a crossroad, he scatters them.

30.s: imā yas tisraḥ iti vṛkṣabhūmau jātājvālenāvasiñcati
30.d: इमा यस् तिस्रः इति वृक्षभूमौ जाताज्वालेनावसिञ्चति

30.s: himavataḥ iti syandamānā anvīpam āhārya valīkaiḥ
30.d: हिमवतः इति स्यन्दमाना अन्वीपम् आहार्य वलीकैः

30.s: pañca ca yā iti pañca pañcāśataṃ paraśuparṇān kāṣṭhair ādīpayati
30.d: पञ्च च या इति पञ्च पञ्चाशतं परशुपर्णान् काष्ठैर् आदीपयति

30.s: niśy ava mā pāpman iti tita-uni pūlyāni avasicyāpavidhya
30.d: निश्य् अव मा पाप्मन् इति तित-उनि पूल्यानि अवसिच्यापविध्य

30.s: aparedyuḥ sahasrākṣāyāpsu balīn trīn puroḍāśasaṃvartān catuṣpathe avakṣipyāvakirati
30.d: अपरेद्युः सहस्राक्षायाप्सु बलीन् त्रीन् पुरोडाशसंवर्तान् चतुष्पथे अवक्षिप्यावकिरति

31.s: yas te mado iti śamīlūnapāpalakṣaṇayoḥ śamīśamyākenābhyudya vāpayati
31.d: यस् ते मदो इति शमीलूनपापलक्षणयोः शमीशम्याकेनाभ्युद्य वापयति
31.m: [31].1) With the verse 'yas te mado...' (AVŚ 6.30.2), having sprinkled the two, [a head] shaven with śamī wood and [one] marked by bad omens, with śamī and samyāka [leaves], he causes [hair] to grow. / [31].2) Over the head. / [31].3) With the hymn 'antardāve...' (AVŚ 6.32.1), reciting all around the fire in a furrow filled with hot [water] and circumambulating thrice, he offers a sacrificial cake. / [31].4) With the hymns 'prāgnaye...' (AVŚ 6.34.1) and 'preto...' (AVŚ 7.114.2), he should place [them] on [the altar]. / [31].5) With the two [hymns] addressed to Vaiśvānara, [there are] potions. / [31].6) With the hymn 'asthād dyaur...' (AVŚ 6.44.1/6.77.1?), reciting with a cow-horn that fell off of its own accord from [a cow] cured of flatulence and contains oblation residues, / [31].7) with the hymn 'yāṃ te rudra...' (AVŚ 6.90.1), [he gives] a spear to one suffering from sharp pain (śūla). / [31].8) With the hymn 'ut sūryo...' (AVŚ 6.52.1), [he places] śamī, bimba, and śīrṇaparṇī [leaves] upon [the head]. / [31].9) With the hymn 'dyauś ca ma...' (AVŚ 6.53.1), having anointed, he wipes downwards. / [31].10) He rubs [it] against a post. / [31].11) With the hymn 'idam id vā...' (AVŚ 6.57.1), having moistened unhusked barley with urine-foam, / [31].12) he throws [it] on. / [31].13) He washes [it] off. / [31].14) He smears [it] over with tooth-powder. / [31].15) With dust from a clump of grass. / [31].16) With the hymns 'apacitaḥ...' (AVŚ 6.83.1) and 'ā susrasaḥ...' (AVŚ 7.76.1), [he applies] the kiṃstya insect and the like. / [31].17) Having crushed red salt, he spits upon [it]. / [31].18) With the hymn 'antarikṣeṇa...' (AVŚ 6.80.1), [he treats] a paralytic and whatever is mentioned in the mantra by causing [him] to walk about. / [31].19) He fumigates with an insect. / [31].20) With the quarter-verse 'glaur...' (AVŚ 6.83.3c), [he acts] with unhusked barley. / [31].21) With the verse 'vīhi svām...' (AVŚ 6.83.4), one who has an unknown sore, having besprinkled [it] with pacifying water, with his mind [he touches it] with oblation residues. / [31].22) With the hymn 'yā oṣadhayaḥ...' (AVŚ 6.96.1), he fumigates the [person] mentioned in the mantra with herbs. / [31].23) He makes him drink honey-buttermilk. / [31].24) Milk-buttermilk. / [31].25) And both. / [31].26) With the hymn 'devā aduḥ...' (AVŚ 6.100.1), [there are] tying on, drinking, sipping, and plastering with [earth from] an anthill, [mixed] with hot [water]. / [31].27) With the hymns 'yathā mano...' (AVŚ 6.105.1) and 'ava divas...' (AVŚ 7.107.1), [he acts] with an ariṣṭa [plant]. / [31].28) With the hymns 'devī devyām...' (AVŚ 6.136.1) and 'yāṃ jamadagnir...' (AVŚ 6.137.1), clothed in black, eating black food, before the flight of crows, when the asterism has set on the new moon day, he pours over [the head of the patient] the fruit mentioned in the mantra along with a jīvī and an alākā plant.

31.s: antardāve iti samantam agneḥ karṣvām uṣṇapūrṇāyāṃ japan triḥ parikramya puroḍāśaṃ juhoti
31.d: अन्तर्दावे इति समन्तम् अग्नेः कर्ष्वाम् उष्णपूर्णायां जपन् त्रिः परिक्रम्य पुरोडाशं जुहोति

31.s: asthād dyaur ity apavātāyāḥ svayaṃsrastena gośṛṅgeṇa saṃpātavatā japan
31.d: अस्थाद् द्यौर् इत्य् अपवातायाः स्वयंस्रस्तेन गोशृङ्गेण संपातवता जपन्

31.s: yāṃ te rudra iti śūline śūlam
31.d: यां ते रुद्र इति शूलिने शूलम्

31.s: idam id vā ity akṣataṃ mūtraphenenābhyudya
31.d: इदम् इद् वा इत्य् अक्षतं मूत्रफेनेनाभ्युद्य

31.s: vīhi svām ity ajñātāruḥ śāntyudakena saṃprokṣya manasā saṃpātavatā
31.d: वीहि स्वाम् इत्य् अज्ञातारुः शान्त्युदकेन संप्रोक्ष्य मनसा संपातवता

31.s: yā oṣadhayaḥ iti mantroktasya oṣadhībhir dhūpayati
31.d: या ओषधयः इति मन्त्रोक्तस्य ओषधीभिर् धूपयति

31.s: devā aduḥ iti valmīkena bandhanapāyanācamanapradehanam uṣṇeṇa
31.d: देवा अदुः इति वल्मीकेन बन्धनपायनाचमनप्रदेहनम् उष्णेण

31.s: yathā mano ava divas ity ariṣṭena
31.d: यथा मनो अव दिवस् इत्य् अरिष्टेन

31.s: devī devyām yāṃ jamadagnir iti mantroktāphalaṃ jīvyalākābhyām amāvāsyāyāṃ kṛṣṇavasanaḥ kṛṣṇabhakṣaḥ purā kākasaṃpātād avanakṣatre avasiñcati
31.d: देवी देव्याम् यां जमदग्निर् इति मन्त्रोक्ताफलं जीव्यलाकाभ्याम् अमावास्यायां कृष्णवसनः कृष्णभक्षः पुरा काकसंपाताद् अवनक्षत्रे अवसिञ्चति

32.s: yas te stanaḥ iti jambhagṛhītāya stanaṃ prayachati
32.d: यस् ते स्तनः इति जम्भगृहीताय स्तनं प्रयछति
32.m: [32].1) With the verse 'yas te stanaḥ...' (AVŚ 7.10.1), he gives the breast to [a child] seized by the Jambha demon. / [32].2) He makes [him] drink priyaṅgu grains over which [milk] has been freshly milked. / [32].3) With the hymns 'agnāviṣṇū...' (AVŚ 7.29.1), 'somārudrā...' (AVŚ 7.42.1), 'sinīvāli...' (AVŚ 7.46.1), 'vi te muñcāmi...' (AVŚ 7.78.1), and 'śumbhanī...' (AVŚ 7.112.1), having tied [amulets] of muñja grass on the joints, he drenches [him] with grass shoots. / [32].4) He pours [water] over [him]. / [32].5) With the hymn 'tiraścirājer...' (AVŚ 7.56.1), [he uses] what is mentioned in the mantra. / [32].6) Having drawn around a model, a clod of earth, and an anthill, / [32].7) [there are] potions. / [32].8) With the hymn 'apacitāṃ...' (AVŚ 7.74.1), [he applies] with a bamboo [stick], darbha grass sweepings, black wool, ghee, kālabunda [plants], and ends of tufts, as mentioned in the mantra. / [32].9) Applying [it] with the fourth [verse], he pierces [the swelling]. / [32].10) With the flame of a bowstring-tuft. / [32].11) With the verse 'yaḥ kīkasāḥ...' (AVŚ 7.76.3), he ties a string of a piśīla lute. / [32].12) With a cord [he ties] an earthworm. / [32].13) A strap of vīriṇa grass, withered of itself, having folded it thrice. / [32].14) With the hymn 'apsu te...' (AVŚ 7.83.1), inside a shed between two flowing [streams], he drenches [him] with grass shoots. / [32].15) He pours [water] over [him]: / [32].16) hot [waters], both containing oblation residues and not containing oblation residues. / [32].17) With the verse 'namo rūrāya...' (AVŚ 7.116.1), having bound a śakunī bird, a dung-beetle, and a spotted frog at the armpit with dark-blue and red threads, / [32].18) with the hymn 'śīrṣaktiṃ...' (AVŚ 9.8.1), he touches [the limbs]. / [32].19) With the last two [verses], he attends upon the sun. / [32].20) With the hymn 'indrasya prathamo...' (AVŚ 10.4.1), [the rite] has been stated for Takṣaka. / [32].21) Having dragged a Paidva [insect], [he inserts it] with the right thumb into the right nostril. / [32].22) In case of fear of snakes, he conceals it in the hem of the garment. / [32].23) With the verse 'aṅgādaṅgāt...' (AVŚ 10.4.25), [he rubs] down to the tip of the feet. / [32].24) Having heated the bite with the last [verse], he casts [the stick] at the snake / [32].25) from which he was bitten. / [32].26) Untransgressed and not forbidden [herbs] among herbs and trees [may be used] for medicines. / [32].27) [Rites are performed] with verses mentioning distress. / [32].28) For the previous one, for a woman desiring a son, and for one who has had a miscarriage, he pours pacified [waters] over the head at the water's edge. / [32].29) To a woman returning home, he gives sacrificial cakes, pramanda perfume, and ornaments containing oblation residues.

32.s: agnāviṣṇū somārudrā sinīvāli vi te muñcāmi śumbhanī iti mauñjaiḥ parvasu baddhvā piñjulībhir āplāvayati
32.d: अग्नाविष्णू सोमारुद्रा सिनीवालि वि ते मुञ्चामि शुम्भनी इति मौञ्जैः पर्वसु बद्ध्वा पिञ्जुलीभिर् आप्लावयति

32.s: apacitāṃ iti vaiṇavena dārbhyūṣeṇa kṛṣṇorṇājyena kālabundai stukāgrair iti mantroktam
32.d: अपचितां इति वैणवेन दार्भ्यूषेण कृष्णोर्णाज्येन कालबुन्दै स्तुकाग्रैर् इति मन्त्रोक्तम्

32.s: apsu te iti vahantyor madhye vimite piñjūlībhir āplāvayati
32.d: अप्सु ते इति वहन्त्योर् मध्ये विमिते पिञ्जूलीभिर् आप्लावयति

32.s: namo rūrāya iti śakunīniveṣīkāñjimaṇḍūkaṃ nīlalohitābhyāṃ sūtrābhyāṃ sakakṣaṃ baddhvā
32.d: नमो रूराय इति शकुनीनिवेषीकाञ्जिमण्डूकं नीललोहिताभ्यां सूत्राभ्यां सकक्षं बद्ध्वा

32.s: indrasya prathamo iti takṣakāya ity uktam
32.d: इन्द्रस्य प्रथमो इति तक्षकाय इत्य् उक्तम्

32.s: pūrvasya putrakāmāvatokayor udakānte śāntā adhiśiro avasiñcati
32.d: पूर्वस्य पुत्रकामावतोकयोर् उदकान्ते शान्ता अधिशिरो अवसिञ्चति

33.s: vaṣaṭ te pūṣann iti catura udapātre saṃpātān ānīya caturo muñjān mūrdhni vibṛhati prācaḥ
33.d: वषट् ते पूषन्न् इति चतुर उदपात्रे संपातान् आनीय चतुरो मुञ्जान् मूर्ध्नि विबृहति प्राचः
33.m: [33].1) With the verse 'Vaṣaṭ to thee, O Pūṣan!' (AV 1.11.1), having poured four residues of oblations into a water vessel, he pulls apart four reeds of muñja grass eastward upon [the woman's] head, / [33].2) [and] reeds [of it] westward. / [33].3) If they break, there is doubt. / [33].4) With warm [water] he washes her from the right tuft of hair. / [33].5) He loosens the house-knots. / [33].6) He binds a yoke-rope that has a loop at both ends [around her]. / [33].7) With the formula 'If thou art of King Soma, I buy thee back from King Soma; if thou art of King Varuṇa, I buy thee back from King Varuṇa', he scatters twenty-one barley grains around the wreath [plant]. / [33].8) With 'Let one of you protect the other...' (PS 1.65.4), he mixes [them]. / [33].9) With 'Let not thy digger come to harm...' (PS 1.65.3), 'Wreath is thy name', [and] 'Prajāpati dug thee for himself as a loosener of the dart; thee we dig, a loosener of the dart for so-and-so', after sunset, or having shaded it with an umbrella, he digs it up with a plowshare. / [33].10) With 'Here let it succeed for thee', he puts down the tip. / [33].11) With 'Here for me', he takes hold of the root. / [33].12) If it is a single-flowered plant [and] untouched [by insects], a male child [will be born]. / [33].13) Having wrapped it with darbha grass, he ties it into her hair. / [33].14) Thus indeed in the case of a vibṛha, a śāka, and a vṛṣa plant. / [33].15) When the afterbirth has fallen, they take [it] off. / [33].16) The digging of [other medicinal] herbs is explained by [that of] the wreath plant. / [33].17) He sprinkles four linseed seeds in her hand with water. / [33].18) If they roll around, a boy [will be born]. / [33].19) A descendant of a Brahmin touches her limbs. / [33].20) If [the thing touched] has a masculine name, a boy [will be born].

33.s: yadi somasyāsi rājñaḥ somāt tvā rājño 'dhikrīṇāmi yadi varuṇasyāsi rājño varuṇāt tvā rājño 'dhikrīṇāmi cf. ity ekaviṃśatyā yavaiḥ srajaṃ parikirati
33.d: यदि सोमस्यासि राज्ञः सोमात् त्वा राज्ञो ऽधिक्रीणामि यदि वरुणस्यासि राज्ञो वरुणात् त्वा राज्ञो ऽधिक्रीणामि च्f. इत्य् एकविंशत्या यवैः स्रजं परिकिरति

33.s: anyā vo anyām avatv anyānyasyā upāvata sadhrīcīḥ savratā bhūtvāsyā avata vīryam iti saṃnayati
33.d: अन्या वो अन्याम् अवत्व् अन्यान्यस्या उपावत सध्रीचीः सव्रता भूत्वास्या अवत वीर्यम् इति संनयति

33.s: mā te riṣan khanitā yasmai ca tvā khanāmasi | dvipāc catuṣpād asmākaṃ mā riṣad devy oṣadhe || srajo nāmāsi prajāpatiṣ ṭvām akhanad ātmane śalyasraṃsanam | tāṃ tvā vayaṃ khanāmasy amuṣmai tvā śalyasraṃsanam ity astamite chattreṇa vāntardhāya phālena khanati
33.d: मा ते रिषन् खनिता यस्मै च त्वा खनामसि । द्विपाच् चतुष्पाद् अस्माकं मा रिषद् देव्य् ओषधे ॥ स्रजो नामासि प्रजापतिष् ट्वाम् अखनद् आत्मने शल्यस्रंसनम् । तां त्वा वयं खनामस्य् अमुष्मै त्वा शल्यस्रंसनम् इत्य् अस्तमिते छत्त्रेण वान्तर्धाय फालेन खनति

33.s: atra tava rādhyatām ity agram avadadhāti
33.d: अत्र तव राध्यताम् इत्य् अग्रम् अवदधाति

34.s: idaṃ janāso ity asyai śiṃśapāśākhāsūdakānte śāntā adhiśiro avasiñcati
34.d: इदं जनासो इत्य् अस्यै शिंशपाशाखासूदकान्ते शान्ता अधिशिरो अवसिञ्चति
34.m: [34].1) With 'This, O people...' (AV 1.32.1), he pours pacified [waters] over her head at the edge of the water over branches of the śiṃśapā tree, / [34].2) for a woman who has departed [and returned]. / [34].3) With 'Away from the hall...' (AV 2.14.1), for one who has suffered a miscarriage, dressed in a black garment, he pours residues of oblations into water in three sheds having eastern doors and western doors; / [34].4) the subsequent ones on a palāśa leaf [and] pieces of lead. / [34].5) Making her stand upon the pieces of lead, he bathes her. / [34].6) Having laid down the black [garment], she departs. / [34].7) The Brahman priest, having kindled [it, departs]. / [34].8) Thus in the case of the previous two, with the ritual equipment collected separately. / [34].9) The Branch Hymn [is used]. / [34].10) Having placed two reeds [and] two stalks on both sides behind the fire, he causes [amulets] of udumbara wood to be fastened right over for the nursing woman. / [34].11) The last [verse is used] for one who has departed [and returned]. / [34].12) [Now] the husband-procuring rites. / [34].13) With 'To us, O Agni...' (AV 2.36.1), he feeds [her] a mixture of rice and peas that has been brought. / [34].14) On the altar, having taken the things mentioned in the mantra from the lair of a wild beast [and] treated with residues of oblations, he hands [them] over at the door. / [34].15) Having sacrificed rice and barley in a water beaker at night for an unmarried sister living at home, he steps out to the south. / [34].16) Having washed and cleaned [the beaker] behind the fire, [he does] what is stated in the mantra with the one treated with residues of oblations, with 'The boat of Bhaga...' (AV 2.36.5). / [34].17) Untying the calves tied to the ends on a seven-fold rope treated with residues of oblations, she leads [them]. / [34].18) With an unwashed garment treated with residues of oblations, he throws [it] over a bull. / [34].19) Whichever direction it drives toward, / [34].20) for an unmarried woman, with 'When indeed these...' (AV 5.1.4), [he feeds her] the mixture of rice and peas that has been brought. / [34].21) With 'These prayers...' (AV 5.2.8), [he acts] for his sister. / [34].22) With 'Here comes...' (AV 6.60.1), he sacrifices to Aryaman before the flight of crows. / [34].23) They present tribute offerings at the inner corners, / [34].24) from where [the crows] fly down.

34.s: nissālām ity avatokāyai kṛṣṇavasanāyai triṣu vimiteṣu prāgdvārapratyagdvāreṣu apsu saṃpātān ānayati
34.d: निस्सालाम् इत्य् अवतोकायै कृष्णवसनायै त्रिषु विमितेषु प्राग्द्वारप्रत्यग्द्वारेषु अप्सु संपातान् आनयति

34.s: paścād agner abhitaḥ kāṇḍe iṣīke nidhāyādhyadhi dhāyine audumbarīr ādhāpayati
34.d: पश्चाद् अग्नेर् अभितः काण्डे इषीके निधायाध्यधि धायिने औदुम्बरीर् आधापयति

34.s: ā no agne ity āgamakṛśaram āśayati
34.d: आ नो अग्ने इत्य् आगमकृशरम् आशयति

34.s: mṛgākharād vedyāṃ mantroktāni saṃpātavanti dvāre prayachati
34.d: मृगाखराद् वेद्यां मन्त्रोक्तानि संपातवन्ति द्वारे प्रयछति

34.s: udakaṃse vrīhiyavau jāmyai niśi hutvā dakṣiṇena prakrāmati
34.d: उदकंसे व्रीहियवौ जाम्यै निशि हुत्वा दक्षिणेन प्रक्रामति

34.s: paścād agneḥ prakṣālya saṃdhāvya saṃpātavatīṃ bhagasya nāvam iti mantroktam
34.d: पश्चाद् अग्नेः प्रक्षाल्य संधाव्य संपातवतीं भगस्य नावम् इति मन्त्रोक्तम्

34.s: saptadāmnyāṃ saṃpātavatyāṃ vatsān pratyantān pracṛtantī vahati
34.d: सप्तदाम्न्यां संपातवत्यां वत्सान् प्रत्यन्तान् प्रचृतन्ती वहति

34.s: jāmyai pra yad ete ity āgamakṛśaram
34.d: जाम्यै प्र यद् एते इत्य् आगमकृशरम्

34.s: ayam ā yāty iti purā kākasaṃpātād aryamṇe juhoti
34.d: अयम् आ यात्य् इति पुरा काकसंपाताद् अर्यम्णे जुहोति

35.m:
[35.1] Rites for producing a male child (puṃsavana).
[35.2] For [a woman] whose menstrual flow has ceased, under a masculine constellation,
[35.3] with the mantra, 'By which a barren cow' (AV 3.23.1), he parts [her hair] on her head with an arrow and binds [it].
[35.4] Having placed rice and barley grains into a wooden vessel of plough-share wood filled with milk from a cow that has a calf of identical colour, and having pounded them, having added two [berries of] adhyaṇḍā, bṛhatī, palāśa, or vidārī, just like the paidva ritual,
[35.5] with the hymn, 'From the mountain, from heaven' (AV 5.25.1), he feeds [her] boiled rice porridge (āgamakṛśara).
[35.6] Through a hole in the yoke, he makes her drink a second [portion] with the residue of oblations.
[35.7] Having rubbed palāśa handles split at the opening, when [the sun] has set, and having applied [them] to his penis, he enters the village.
[35.8] With the hymn, 'The aśvattha [mounted] upon the śamī' (AV 6.11.1), having churned fire in the manner stated in the mantra, in ghee from a cow that has borne a male calf, just like the paidva ritual,
[35.9] he makes her drink [it] in a honey-mash.
[35.10] Having wrapped it with black wool, he binds it [upon her].
[35.11] With the mantra, 'Thou art the restrainer' (AV 6.80.2), he binds what is stated in the mantra.
[35.12] The hymn 'Accomplishing the mantra' (AV 5.1.1) is one; 'As this earth' (AV 6.17.1–4) and 'Firm' are rites for securing the embryo.
[35.13] For one seized by a seizure-demon (jambha), having tied three knots in a bowstring, leaving out the first verse, he binds it [upon him].
[35.14] He makes him eat clods of earth verse by verse.
[35.15] He scatters dark sand around the bed.
[35.16] If he wishes a woman to give birth to a male hero, he addresses her belly with the hymns to Dhātṛ (dhātṛvyābhiḥ).
[35.17] With the verse, 'Prajāpati' (AV 6.11.3 / 7.19.1), he makes an offering into the lap of the woman who desires offspring.
[35.18] He makes her eat pieces of meat of a red she-goat,
[35.19] [and] drinks of all kinds.
[35.20] With the hymn, 'The two which thy mother' (AV 8.6.1), he binds the two [amulets] mentioned in the mantra.
[35.21] With the hymns, 'As from this earth' (AV 2.30.1), 'As the tree' (AV 6.8.1), 'Desire me' (AV 6.9.1), and 'As this draft animal' (AV 6.102.1), he rubs together chips of a tree and a climbing vine that are intertwined, hair from a pregnant cow, arrow-shaft wood, collyrium, costus, madugha, and grass whirled up by a tempest, combines them with ghee, and touches [the woman].
[35.22] With the hymn, 'May the disturber' (AV 3.25.1), he pushes her with his finger.
[35.23] He lays down twenty-one eastward-pointing, decorated, consecrated thorns.
[35.24] [And also] tips of kūdī with strings.
[35.25] Three times a day, for three nights, he heats costus smeared with butter over the fire.
[35.26] Taking hold of a long blue lotus, he lies down.
[35.27] Having tied hot water at his feet to a tripod, pressing it with both his big toes, he sleeps.
[35.28] He pierces the heart of an effigy made of comb-leavings with [a bow] of darbha grass having a string of hemp, and an arrow whose point is a thorn, whose feathers are owl feathers, and whose shaft is a black reed.

35.s: yena vehad iti bāṇaṃ mūrdhni vibṛhati badhnāti
35.d: येन वेहद् इति बाणं मूर्ध्नि विबृहति बध्नाति

35.s: phālacamase sarūpavatsāyā dudghe vrīhiyavau avadhāya mūrchayitvādhyaṇḍe bṛhatīpalāśavidaryau vā pratinīya paidvam iva
35.d: फालचमसे सरूपवत्साया दुद्घे व्रीहियवौ अवधाय मूर्छयित्वाध्यण्डे बृहतीपलाशविदर्यौ वा प्रतिनीय पैद्वम् इव

35.s: khe lūnān ca palāśatsarūn nivṛtte nighṛṣyādhāya śiśne grāmaṃ praviśati
35.d: खे लूनान् च पलाशत्सरून् निवृत्ते निघृष्याधाय शिश्ने ग्रामं प्रविशति

35.s: śamīm aśvattha iti mantrokte agniṃ mathitvā puṃsyāḥ sarpiṣi paidvam iva
35.d: शमीम् अश्वत्थ इति मन्त्रोक्ते अग्निं मथित्वा पुंस्याः सर्पिषि पैद्वम् इव

35.s: ṛdhaṅmantro ity ekā yatheyaṃ pṛthivī acyutā iti garbhadṛṃhaṇāni
35.d: ऋधङ्मन्त्रो इत्य् एका यथेयं पृथिवी अच्युता इति गर्भदृंहणानि

35.s: jambhagṛhītāya prathamāvarjaṃ jyāṃ trir udgrathya badhnāti
35.d: जम्भगृहीताय प्रथमावर्जं ज्यां त्रिर् उद्ग्रथ्य बध्नाति

35.s: yām iched vīraṃ janayed iti dhātṛvyābhir udaram abhimantrayate
35.d: याम् इछेद् वीरं जनयेद् इति धातृव्याभिर् उदरम् अभिमन्त्रयते

35.s: yau te mātā iti mantroktau badhnāti
35.d: यौ ते माता इति मन्त्रोक्तौ बध्नाति

35.s: yathedaṃ bhūmyā adhi yathā vṛkṣaṃ vāñcha me yathāyaṃ vāho iti saṃspṛṣṭayor vṛkṣalibujayoḥ śakalāvantareṣusthakarāñjanakuṣṭhamadughareṣmamathitatṛṇam ājyena saṃnīya saṃspṛśati
35.d: यथेदं भूम्या अधि यथा वृक्षं वाञ्छ मे यथायं वाहो इति संस्पृष्टयोर् वृक्षलिबुजयोः शकलावन्तरेषुस्थकराञ्जनकुष्ठमदुघरेष्ममथिततृणम् आज्येन संनीय संस्पृशति

35.s: navanītānvaktaṃ kuṣṭhaṃ trir ahnaḥ pratapati trirātre
35.d: नवनीतान्वक्तं कुष्ठं त्रिर् अह्नः प्रतपति त्रिरात्रे

35.s: uṣṇodakaṃ tripāde pattaḥ prabadhya prabaddhā p. n. aṅguṣṭhābhyām ardayan śete
35.d: उष्णोदकं त्रिपादे पत्तः प्रबध्य प्रबद्धा प्। न्। अङ्गुष्ठाभ्याम् अर्दयन् शेते

35.s: pratikṛtim āvalekhanīṃ dārbhyūṣeṇa bhāṅgajyena kaṇṭakaśalyayā ulūkapattrayāsitālakāṇḍayā hṛdaye vidhyati
35.d: प्रतिकृतिम् आवलेखनीं दार्भ्यूषेण भाङ्गज्येन कण्टकशल्यया उलूकपत्त्रयासितालकाण्डया हृदये विध्यति

36.m:
[36.1] The hymn, 'The thousand-horned' (AV 4.5.1), is a sleep-inducing charm.
[36.2] Having besprinkled the house with a water vessel containing the residue of oblations, he turns it upside down at the outer doorpost.
[36.3] Likewise [he does so] naked.
[36.4] He consecrates the mortar, the northern corner, the right bedpost, and the threads [of the bed].
[36.5] The hymn, 'Heaven hath stood firm' (AV 6.77.1 / 6.44.1), is a binding rite.
[36.6] Fastening the tip of a bamboo cane with a wrapper, he binds it to the middle post,
[36.7] and to the bedpost, and to a lotus,
[36.8] and to a dragged [branch].
[36.9] With a rake (ākarṣa), he offers sesame seeds.
[36.10] With the hymn, 'That which belongs to the beloved' (AV 6.89.1), he consecrates the corner of the head [of her bed].
[36.11] He holds the hairs.
[36.12] With the hymns, 'With fortune me' (AV 6.129.1), 'The clinging plant' (AV 6.139.1), and 'This I dig' (AV 7.38.1), having fastened a sauvarcala plant like an herb, with white flowers, onto his head, he enters the village.
[36.13] With the hymn, 'Of the charioteers' (AV 6.130.1), he scatters beans as love-charms.
[36.14] He flings flaming reed points in every direction towards an effigy made of comb-leavings.
[36.15] With the hymn, 'Her fortune and splendour' (AV 1.14.1), he buries her wreath, waste [hair], tooth-cleaning stick, hair, or the bag of a cow killed by lightning or used for an anustaraṇī offering, into a mortar-cleft or among three stones.
[36.16] Having crushed the wreath, he recites over it.
[36.17] Having tied three tufts of hair with a black thread, he places them alternately among three stones, with stones placed on top.
[36.18] Then he digs up her fortune with the mantra: 'What fortune of thine they buried among three stones, what among four stones, that do I dig up for thee, along with offspring and wealth.'
[36.19] With the hymn, 'This I dig' (AV 3.18.1), having mixed an arrow-shaped leaf with a drop of red goat's [milk or blood], he scatters it around the bed.
[36.20] With the verse-quarter, 'Over thee have I placed' (AV 3.18.6a), he fastens a palāśa leaf below.
[36.21] With the verse-quarter, 'Close to thee have I placed' (AV 3.18.6b), he casts [it] above.
[36.22] Wishing to dispel desire, scattering countless pebbles with an apāgha plant, he walks around.
[36.23] Trampling [the pebbles], he mutters [the mantra],
[36.24] or without trampling.
[36.25] With the hymns, 'The rush of jealousy' (AV 6.18.1), 'From the people of all nations' (AV 7.45.1), and 'I by Tvāṣṭra' (AV 7.74.3), there is repeating muttering, offerings, and touchings.
[36.26] With the first [hymn], [he touches] the regions mentioned in the mantra upon her thighs.
[36.27] With the verse, 'As of fire' (AV 7.45.2), [he uses] water heated by an axe.
[36.28] With the hymn, 'As [the arrow] from the bowstring' (AV 6.42.1), seeing [an enemy], he takes up a stone.
[36.29] With the second verse, he sets it down upon [the ground].
[36.30] With the third, he spits upon it.
[36.31] In the shade, he strings a bow.
[36.32] With the hymn, 'This darbha grass' (AV 6.43.1), [he acts] as with an herb.
[36.33] With the hymns, 'Those born from fire' (AV 7.34.1), [praying] that she may not give birth to a hero, and 'Others' (AV 7.35.1), [praying] that she may not bear at all, having rubbed mule's urine with two round stones, [he smears it] on her food or ornament.
[36.34] He inspects the parting of the hair.
[36.35] With the hymn, 'Hew down' (AV 7.90.1), he pronounces [a curse] on the paramour for the sake of the wife.
[36.36] In the footprint of an impotent person, he cuts down a bow of bādhaka wood.
[36.37] He strikes a stone into [the paramour's] resting-place.
[36.38] With the hymn, 'O harsh one' (AV 7.113.1), [he touches] an arrow-shaped leaf.
[36.39] With the hymn, 'I take to thee' (AV 7.114.1), he touches the items mentioned in the mantra.
[36.40] And he recites [the formula], and he recites [the formula].

36.s: udapātreṇa saṃpātavatā śālāṃ saṃprokṣyāparasmin dvārapakṣe nyubjati
36.d: उदपात्रेण संपातवता शालां संप्रोक्ष्यापरस्मिन् द्वारपक्षे न्युब्जति

36.s: ulūkhalam uttarāṃ sraktiṃ dakṣiṇaśayanapādaṃ tantūn abhimantrayate
36.d: उलूखलम् उत्तरां स्रक्तिं दक्षिणशयनपादं तन्तून् अभिमन्त्रयते

36.s: idaṃ yat preṇyaḥ iti śiraḥkarṇam abhimantrayate
36.d: इदं यत् प्रेण्यः इति शिरःकर्णम् अभिमन्त्रयते

36.s: bhagena mā nyastikā idaṃ khanāmi iti sauvarcalam oṣadhivat śuklaprasūnaṃ śirasi upacṛtya grāmaṃ praviśati
36.d: भगेन मा न्यस्तिका इदं खनामि इति सौवर्चलम् ओषधिवत् शुक्लप्रसूनं शिरसि उपचृत्य ग्रामं प्रविशति

36.s: śarabhṛṣṭīr ādīptāḥ pratidiśam abhyasyati arvācyā āvalekhanyāḥ
36.d: शरभृष्टीर् आदीप्ताः प्रतिदिशम् अभ्यस्यति अर्वाच्या आवलेखन्याः

36.s: bhagam asyā varca iti mālāniṣpramandadantadhāvanakeśamīśānahatāyā anustaraṇyā vā kośam ulūkhaladaraṇe triśile nikhanati
36.d: भगम् अस्या वर्च इति मालानिष्प्रमन्ददन्तधावनकेशमीशानहताया अनुस्तरण्या वा कोशम् उलूखलदरणे त्रिशिले निखनति

36.s: trīṇi keśamaṇḍalāni kṛṣṇasūtrena vigrathya triśile aśmottarāṇi vyatyāsam
36.d: त्रीणि केशमण्डलानि कृष्णसूत्रेन विग्रथ्य त्रिशिले अश्मोत्तराणि व्यत्यासम्

36.s: athāsyai bhagam utkhanati yaṃ te bhagaṃ nicakhnus triśile yaṃ catuḥśile | idaṃ tam utkhanāmi prajayā ca dhanena ca iti
36.d: अथास्यै भगम् उत्खनति यं ते भगं निचख्नुस् त्रिशिले यं चतुःशिले । इदं तम् उत्खनामि प्रजया च धनेन च इति

36.s: imāṃ khanāmy iti bāṇāparṇīṃ lohitājāyā drapsena saṃnīya śayanam anuparikirati
36.d: इमां खनाम्य् इति बाणापर्णीं लोहिताजाया द्रप्सेन संनीय शयनम् अनुपरिकिरति

36.s: abhi te 'dhāṃ ity adhastāt palāśam upacṛtati
36.d: अभि ते ऽधां इत्य् अधस्तात् पलाशम् उपचृतति
उप ते ऽधां इत्य् उपरि उपास्यति

36.s: kāmaṃ vineṣyamāṇo apāghenāsaṃkhyātāḥ śarkarāḥ parikiran vrajati
36.d: कामं विनेष्यमाणो अपाघेनासंख्याताः शर्कराः परिकिरन् व्रजति

36.s: īrṣyāyā dhrājiṃ janād viśvajanīnāt tvāṣṭreṇāhaṃ iti pratijāpaḥ pradānābhimarśanāni
36.d: ईर्ष्याया ध्राजिं जनाद् विश्वजनीनात् त्वाष्ट्रेणाहं इति प्रतिजापः प्रदानाभिमर्शनानि

36.s: ava jyām iva iti dṛṣṭvāśmānam ādatte
36.d: अव ज्याम् इव इति दृष्ट्वाश्मानम् आदत्ते

36.s: agne jātān iti na vīraṃ janayet prānyān iti na vijāyeta ity aśvatarīmūtram aśmamaṇḍalābhyāṃ saṃghṛṣya bhakte alaṃkāre
36.d: अग्ने जातान् इति न वीरं जनयेत् प्रान्यान् इति न विजायेत इत्य् अश्वतरीमूत्रम् अश्ममण्डलाभ्यां संघृष्य भक्ते अलंकारे

36.s: api vṛśca iti jāyāyai jāram anvāha
36.d: अपि वृश्च इति जायायै जारम् अन्वाह

36.s: ā te dade iti mantroktāni saṃspṛśati
36.d: आ ते ददे इति मन्त्रोक्तानि संस्पृशति

37.m:
[37].1) With "The mothers go..." [AV 1.4.1], there are divination omens through milk-rice, an utkuca plant, a clump of grass, and pāṭā.
[37].2) The divination of the sacrificial altar is related to battle.
[37].3) With "Vena beheld that..." [AV 2.1.1], he looks [for signs] on five-jointed arrows, a jar, a water pot, a clump of grass, a Kāmpīla branch, a yoke, firewood, axles, or on twenty-one pebbles in the two hands.
[37].4) Having wrapped a jar with an unwashed [cloth] and placed it upon an altered couch, he transfers the residues of oblations.
[37].5) Having covered [the jar] so it is not visible from outside, in whichever direction two girls who have not attained puberty carry it, in that direction lies the lost [item].
[37].6) In the same way with a plow and an axle.
[37].7) Regarding clods of earth, he says to a young maiden: "Take whichever you desire."
[37].8) [If she takes] a clod shaped [from a plowed field] or an ant-hill, [it portends] good fortune.
[37].9) From a crossroad, [it portends that she will be] one who goes after many men.
[37].10) From a cremation ground, she will not live long.
[37].11) He says: "Pour out a handful of water."
[37].12) When she throws it eastward, [it portends] good fortune.

37.s: venas tat iti pañcaparveṣukumbhakamaṇḍalustambakāmpīlaśākhāyuga idhmākṣeṣu pāṇyor ekaviṃśatyāṃ śarkarāsu īkṣate
37.d: वेनस् तत् इति पञ्चपर्वेषुकुम्भकमण्डलुस्तम्बकाम्पीलशाखायुग इध्माक्षेषु पाण्योर् एकविंशत्यां शर्करासु ईक्षते

37.s: kumbhamahatena pariveṣṭyādhāya śayane vikṛte saṃpātān atinayati
37.d: कुम्भमहतेन परिवेष्ट्याधाय शयने विकृते संपातान् अतिनयति

37.s: anatīkāśam avachādyārajovitte kumāryau yena haretāṃ tato naṣṭam
37.d: अनतीकाशम् अवछाद्यारजोवित्ते कुमार्यौ येन हरेतां ततो नष्टम्

37.s: loṣṭānāṃ kumārīm āha yam ichasi tam ādatsva iti
37.d: लोष्टानां कुमारीम् आह यम् इछसि तम् आदत्स्व इति

38.m:
[38].1) With "Born of the chorion..." [AV 1.12.1], when bad weather approaches, he stands up facing it,
[38].2) stanza by stanza with water-thunderbolts,
[38].3) taking a sword, a firebrand, and a stick measuring a cubit.
[38].4) Being naked and wiping his forehead,
[38].5) having set [the fire] outside on an ember potsherd, he offers horseradish tree [leaves] and pebbles.
[38].6) He lays down two kerārka plants.
[38].7) Surrounded by rain, having plowed counter-clockwise, having circumambulated three times, he quickly scatters Arka into a pit.
[38].8) Taking what is associated with the lightning-stroke, with "Homage be to you..." [AV 1.13.1] and "Whoever is your broad thunderer..." [AV 7.11.1],
[38].9) having wrapped the soma, darbha grass, keśānī, kuṣṭha, lac, madder, badara, and turmeric of the first [hymn] in a birch-bark fragment, he buries it at the head of a churning stick in the middle of a cultivated field.
[38].10) He eats curds with a new [vessel] until harvest.
[38].11) The [hymns] to the protectors of the quarters, except the third, are for firm establishment.
[38].12) The rites of a water bag are for the hymn to Earth [AV 12.1].
[38].13) He places sacrificial cakes topped with stones at the inner corners,
[38].14) both [kinds] possessing the residue of oblations,
[38].15) and in the compartments of the assembly hall.
[38].16) Without excessive heat, on one side of the place of fire while another is lying down, he mutters the hymn to Earth.
[38].17) With "This plant..." [AV 1.34.1], chewing madugha, he approaches the assembly from an undefeated [direction].
[38].18) With "Let not the enemy..." [AV 2.27.1], a root of pāṭā is fed [to him] beforehand;
[38].19) he recites [the hymn];
[38].20) he binds it on;
[38].21) he wears a garland of seven palāśa leaves.
[38].22) With "They who, eating..." [AV 2.35.1], he eats while gazing at a single meal in the assembly.
[38].23) With "The holy power first born..." [AV 4.1.1], when about to commence the study of the lessons, he causes [the students] to recite.
[38].24) When about to deliver a disputation,
[38].25) when about to speak a theological riddle,
[38].26) with "To me, Agni, splendour..." [AV 5.3.1], one desiring to enjoy pre-eminence binds a wild-hemp rope.
[38].27) With "May both the assembly and..." [AV 7.12.1], he consumes [food].
[38].28) He grasps the two posts and attends [upon them].
[38].29) With "What I speak..." [AV 12.1.58], as prescribed in the mantra.
[38].30) With "I am..." [AV 12.1.54], he approaches the assembly from an undefeated [direction].

38.s: varṣaparītaḥ pratilomakarṣitas triḥ parikramya khadāyām arkaṃ kṣipraṃ saṃvapati
38.d: वर्षपरीतः प्रतिलोमकर्षितस् त्रिः परिक्रम्य खदायाम् अर्कं क्षिप्रं संवपति

38.s: namas te astu yas te pṛthu stanayitnur ity aśaniyuktam apādāya
38.d: नमस् ते अस्तु यस् ते पृथु स्तनयित्नुर् इत्य् अशनियुक्तम् अपादाय

38.s: prathamasya somadarbhakeśānīkuṣṭhalākṣāmañjiṣṭhībadaraharidraṃ bhūrjaśakalena pariveṣṭya manthaśirasi urvarāmadhye nikhanati
