38.d: प्रथमस्य सोमदर्भकेशानीकुष्ठलाक्षामञ्जिष्ठीबदरहरिद्रं भूर्जशकलेन परिवेष्ट्य मन्थशिरसि उर्वरामध्ये निखनति

38.s: asaṃtāpe jyotirāyatanasya ekato anyaṃ śayāno bhaumaṃ japati
38.d: असंतापे ज्योतिरायतनस्य एकतो अन्यं शयानो भौमं जपति

38.s: iyaṃ vīrun iti madughaṃ khādann aparājitāt pariṣadam āvrajati
38.d: इयं वीरुन् इति मदुघं खादन्न् अपराजितात् परिषदम् आव्रजति

38.s: ye bhakṣayanto iti pariṣadi ekabhaktam anvīkṣamāṇo bhuṅkte
38.d: ये भक्षयन्तो इति परिषदि एकभक्तम् अन्वीक्षमाणो भुङ्क्ते

38.s: brahma jajñānaṃ ity adhyāyān upākariṣyann abhivyāhārayati
38.d: ब्रह्म जज्ञानं इत्य् अध्यायान् उपाकरिष्यन्न् अभिव्याहारयति

38.s: mamāgne varco iti vibhuṅkṣyamāṇaḥ pramattarajjuṃ badhnāti
38.d: ममाग्ने वर्चो इति विभुङ्क्ष्यमाणः प्रमत्तरज्जुं बध्नाति

38.s: aham asmi ity aparājitāt pariṣadam āvrajati
38.d: अहम् अस्मि इत्य् अपराजितात् परिषदम् आव्रजति

39.s: dūṣyā dūṣir asi iti srāktyaṃ badhnāti
39.d: दूष्या दूषिर् असि इति स्राक्त्यं बध्नाति
39.m:
[39].1) With "A damager of the damager are you..." [AV 2.11.1], he binds on an amulet of sraktya wood.
[39].2) In front of the fire, he causes a brown cow to be [brought];
[39].3) behind the fire, a red he-goat,
[39].4) for the sake of broth and meat.
[39].5) [The ingredients are] as stated in the mantra.
[39].6) Having put in vāśā, kāmpīla, sitīvāra, and sadaṃpuṣpā,
[39].7) with "A damager of the damager are you..." [AV 2.11.1], "They who from the east..." [AV 4.40.1], "The ruler over you..." [AV 4.17.1], "Equal splendour..." [AV 4.18.1], "And you are not making friends..." [AV 4.19.1], "The eagle you..." [AV 5.14.1], "What they made for you..." [AV 5.31.1], "This protective amulet..." [AV 8.5.1], and "What they fashion..." [AV 10.1.1], he performs the great pacification rite.
[39].8) Having removed it at night, wearing a turban, besprinkling ahead, he goes forth,
[39].9) [saying:] "To the restrained, to the restrained, to the pacified, to the peace-bringing, to the auspicious, to the fortunate, to the pleasant, to the potent, to the kindly, O well-omened one, O fruitful one, O calm one, I have not become adverse to you."
[39].10) Through absence, he throws it away.
[39].11) Looking at the sorcery doll with an unfriendly eye, with "O you pierced by deed..." [AV 5.14.9], he pierces what is smeared with sorcery.
[39].12) [He pierces] with the prescribed scraping implement.
[39].13) With "A damager of the damager are you..." [AV 2.11.1], three times with a wooden ladle he sprinkles around the ankles with churned [curds] without water, [derived] from a cow with a similar calf.
[39].14) Having poured [it] on with a wooden splinter, he feeds the broth and meat.
[39].15) Having bound the skin with sticks, the caller of prompts, having walked around, releases the bonds with a pair of tongs.
[39].16) He makes [it] lie down on the other side.
[39].17) As stated, with a wooden splinter.
[39].18) With "Anointed..." [AV 10.1.25], as stated in the mantra, with fresh butter.
[39].19) Having bound it with a rope of darbha grass, with "Stand up indeed..." [AV 10.1.20c], he makes it stand up.
[39].20) Taking a lamp with the left [hand] and a water-gourd with the right, with restrained speech,
[39].21) the caller of prompts in front,
[39].22) [to a place] not fenced in,
[39].23) [to a place] untrodden by cattle,
[39].24) [to a place] dug without water,
[39].25) he deposits [it] either on a southward slope, or in a natural cleft, or in a cleft made by oneself, or in a barren wasteland, or in another quarter.
[39].26) Having extinguished the lamp with the gourd, with "As the sun..." [AV 10.1.32], having turned around, he returns.
[39].27) Standing, he loudly recites the standing great pacification formula.
[39].28) They besprinkle the vital joints.
[39].29) He plows with a black plow.
[39].30) In addition to the plows, ten [cows are] the sacrificial fee.
[39].31) The regions of sorcery are known from the mantras: those are the vital joints.

39.s: dūṣyā duṣir asi ye purastāj īśānāṃ tvā samaṃ jyotiḥ uto asy abandhukṛd suparṇas tvā yāṃ te cakrur ayaṃ pratisaro yāṃ kalpayanti iti mahāśāntim āvapate
39.d: दूष्या दुषिर् असि ये पुरस्ताज् ईशानां त्वा समं ज्योतिः उतो अस्य् अबन्धुकृद् सुपर्णस् त्वा यां ते चक्रुर् अयं प्रतिसरो यां कल्पयन्ति इति महाशान्तिम् आवपते

39.s: niśi avamucya uṣṇīṣī agrataḥ prokṣan vrajati
39.d: निशि अवमुच्य उष्णीषी अग्रतः प्रोक्षन् व्रजति

39.s: yatāyai yatāyai śāntāyai śāntivāyai bhadrāyai bhadrāvati syonāyai śagmāyai śivāyai sumaṅgali prajāvati suśīme ahaṃ vāmābhūr iti
39.d: यतायै यतायै शान्तायै शान्तिवायै भद्रायै भद्रावति स्योनायै शग्मायै शिवायै सुमङ्गलि प्रजावति सुशीमे अहं वामाभूर् इति

39.s: kṛtyayāmitracakṣuṣā samīkṣan kṛtavyadhani ity avaliptaṃ kṛtyayā vidhyati
39.d: कृत्ययामित्रचक्षुषा समीक्षन् कृतव्यधनि इत्य् अवलिप्तं कृत्यया विध्यति

39.s: dūṣyā duṣir asi iti darvyā triḥ sārūpavatsenāpodakena mathitena gulphān pariṣiñcati
39.d: दूष्या दुषिर् असि इति दर्व्या त्रिः सारूपवत्सेनापोदकेन मथितेन गुल्फान् परिषिञ्चति

39.s: yaṣṭibhis carma pinahya praiṣakṛt parikramya bandhān muñcati saṃdaṃśena
39.d: यष्टिभिस् चर्म पिनह्य प्रैषकृत् परिक्रम्य बन्धान् मुञ्चति संदंशेन

39.s: savyena dīpaṃ dakṣiṇena udakālābu ādāya vāgyatāḥ
39.d: सव्येन दीपं दक्षिणेन उदकालाबु आदाय वाग्यताः

39.s: dakṣiṇāpravaṇe vā svayaṃdīrṇe vā svakṛte vā iriṇe anyāśāyāṃ vā nidadhāti
39.d: दक्षिणाप्रवणे वा स्वयंदीर्णे वा स्वकृते वा इरिणे अन्याशायां वा निदधाति

39.s: alābunā dīpam avasicya yathā sūryo ity āvṛtyāvrajati
39.d: अलाबुना दीपम् अवसिच्य यथा सूर्यो इत्य् आवृत्याव्रजति

40.s: yad adaḥ saṃprayatīr iti yena ichet nadī pratipadyeta iti prasiñcan vrajati
40.d: यद् अदः संप्रयतीर् इति येन इछेत् नदी प्रतिपद्येत इति प्रसिञ्चन् व्रजति
40.m:
[40].1) With the mantra 'When yonder, marching together...' (AV 3.13.1), he walks pouring out [water] along the path by which he wishes a river should go.
[40].2) He sets upright reed grass, dividhuvaka, and canes.
[40].3) With 'This to you, O waters...' (AV 3.13.7a), he places gold on [them].
[40].4) With 'This calf...' (AV 3.13.7b), having tied a frog painted with reed lines under its armpits with dark-blue and red thread,
[40].5) with 'Here, thus...' (AV 3.13.7c), he covers it with avakā plant.
[40].6) With 'Where this...' (AV 3.13.7d), he pours [water] out.
[40].7) He makes an offering to Varuṇa three times with milk-rice dedicated to the Maruts, cooked on a fire dedicated to the Maruts, having strewn around with [grass] dedicated to the Maruts, with a dipping spoon dedicated to the Maruts, and with ghee dedicated to the Maruts.
[40].8) The churning has been explained.
[40].9) Having carried out a tribute offering of curd-churn, he walks pouring out [water] with the two besprinkling waters.
[40].10) Having struck back with his hand or with a reed, he lies down upon [it].
[40].11) With 'This is your source...' (AV 3.20.1), he causes the fire to mount upon the two churning sticks,
[40].12) or into himself.
[40].13) With 'Descend again, O Jātavedas, a god to the gods, carry the oblation knowingly; joyful, rejoicing, with good sons, may we kindle you for a hundred autumns', he causes [the fire] to descend.
[40].14) With 'Which the gandharva dug for you...' (AV 4.4.1) and 'Bulls were your diggers, a bull are you, O plant; a bull are you, virile, for a bull we dig you' (PS 4.5.2), he digs up the ucchuṣmā and the parivyādha plants with an iron tool.
[40].15) Putting the two infusions into milk, placing [them] in his lap with bow drawn, he drinks.
[40].16) Sitting on a peg or on a mortar, with 'Just as the dark...' (AV 6.72.1), he binds an amulet made of one arka thread, originating from the arka plant.
[40].17) With 'Fitting the limbs...' (AV 6.72.3), [he binds an amulet] made of a black shoulder[-hair] with a black tail-hair.
[40].18) With 'Act the bull...' (AV 6.101.1), he approaches both.

40.s: idaṃ va āpo iti hiraṇyam adhidadhāti
40.d: इदं व आपो इति हिरण्यम् अधिदधाति

40.s: ayaṃ vatsa itīṣīkāñjimaṇḍūkaṃ nīlalohitābhyāṃ sakakṣaṃ baddhvā
40.d: अयं वत्स इतीषीकाञ्जिमण्डूकं नीललोहिताभ्यां सकक्षं बद्ध्वा

40.s: mārutaṃ kṣīraudanaṃ mārutaśṛtaṃ mārutaiḥ paristīrya mārutena sruveṇa mārutenājyena varuṇāya trir juhoti
40.d: मारुतं क्षीरौदनं मारुतशृतं मारुतैः परिस्तीर्य मारुतेन स्रुवेण मारुतेनाज्येन वरुणाय त्रिर् जुहोति

40.s: dadhimanthaṃ baliṃ hṛtvā saṃprokṣaṇībhyāṃ prasiñcan vrajati
40.d: दधिमन्थं बलिं हृत्वा संप्रोक्षणीभ्यां प्रसिञ्चन् व्रजति

40.s: pāṇinā vetreṇa vā pratyāhatya upari nipadyate
40.d: पाणिना वेत्रेण वा प्रत्याहत्य उपरि निपद्यते

40.s: ayaṃ te yonir ity araṇyor agniṃ samāropayati
40.d: अयं ते योनिर् इत्य् अरण्योर् अग्निं समारोपयति

40.s: upāvaroha jātavedaḥ punar devo devebhyo havyaṃ vaha prajānan | ānandino modamānāḥ suvīrā indhīmahi tvā śaradāṃ śatāni ity upāvarohayati
40.d: उपावरोह जातवेदः पुनर् देवो देवेभ्यो हव्यं वह प्रजानन् । आनन्दिनो मोदमानाः सुवीरा इन्धीमहि त्वा शरदां शतानि इत्य् उपावरोहयति

40.s: yāṃ tvā gandharvo akhanad vṛṣaṇas te khanitāro vṛṣā tvam asy oṣadhe | vṛṣāsi vṛṣṇyāvati vṛṣaṇe tvā khanāmasi ity ucchuṣmāparivyādhāv āyasena khanati
40.d: यां त्वा गन्धर्वो अखनद् वृषणस् ते खनितारो वृषा त्वम् अस्य् ओषधे । वृषासि वृष्ण्यावति वृषणे त्वा खनामसि इत्य् उच्छुष्मापरिव्याधाव् आयसेन खनति

40.s: dugdhe phāṇṭau adhijyam upastha ādhāya pibati
40.d: दुग्धे फाण्टौ अधिज्यम् उपस्थ आधाय पिबति

40.s: mayūkhe musale vāsīno yathāsitaḥ ity ekārkasūtram ārkaṃ badhnāti
40.d: मयूखे मुसले वासीनो यथासितः इत्य् एकार्कसूत्रम् आर्कं बध्नाति

41.s: samutpatantu pra nabhasva iti varṣakāmo dvādaśarātram anuśuṣyet
41.d: समुत्पतन्तु प्र नभस्व इति वर्षकामो द्वादशरात्रम् अनुशुष्येत्
41.m:
[41].1) With 'Let them fly up...' (AV 4.15.1) and 'Burst open...' (AV 7.18.1), one desiring rain should dry out for twelve nights.
[41].2) Having observed every vow, he performs austerities.
[41].3) He sacrifices to the Maruts just as he offers to Varuṇa.
[41].4) Having introduced plants possessing the residue of oblations, he turns [a vessel] upside down over [them].
[41].5) He should let it float away.
[41].6) Having tied the head of a dog, the head of a ram, hair, and an old sandal to the tip of a bamboo, he causes them to fight.
[41].7) Having besprinkled an unbaked vessel with a water vessel possessing the residue of oblations, and having placed a stone on a tripod, he deposits it in the water.
[41].8) When about to set out on a purpose, he should deposit [these] with 'This is your source...' (AV 3.20.1), 'Bring unto us...' (AV 5.7.1), and 'Or by thought...' (AV 7.1.1).
[41].9) He mutters [them].
[41].10) Under the constellation of Pūrvāṣāḍhā he digs a hole.
[41].11) Under Uttarāṣāḍhā he heaps it up.
[41].12) Having strewn the gambling ground,
[41].13) with 'Breaking forth, conquering...' (AV 4.38.1), 'As the thunderbolt a tree...' (AV 7.50.1), and 'This to the fierce...' (AV 7.109.1), he casts down the scented dice.
[41].14) [The mantras] 'The mothers go...' (AV 1.4.1), 'Beneficent, causing joy...' (AV 1.5, 1.6), 'Golden-colored...' (AV 1.33.1), 'When yonder...' (AV 3.13.1), 'May they purify me...' (AV 6.19.1), 'Having flowed...' (AV 6.23.1), 'From the snowy mountain they flow down...' (AV 6.24.1), 'Purified by the strainer of Vāyu...' (AV 6.51.1), 'And peace to us and joy to us...' (AV 6.57.3), 'For the draft oxen first you...' (AV 6.59.1), 'To me the waters...' (AV 6.61.1), and 'Vaiśvānara with his rays...' (AV 6.62.1) are for rites of causing rain to pour and of pouring upon.
[41].15) With the last [verse] having the characteristic mark of Vācaspati, he reveres the rising [sun].
[41].16) Having bathed and washed an unwashed garment, he puts on the unwashed [garment].
[41].17) He gives [a gift].
[41].18) 'As flesh...' (AV 6.70.1) is the recital.
[41].19) Having caused a calf to run together, having sprinkled it with cow urine, and having led it three times around, he attaches it.
[41].20) He addresses the mantra over its head and ear.
[41].21) With 'Swift as the wind...' (AV 6.92.1), when the horse has bathed, he pours the residue of oblations over it.
[41].22) He applies the subsequent [residues] upon palāśa powders.
[41].23) He makes [the horse] sip water.
[41].24) He bathes [the horse].
[41].25) He scatters it with powders.
[41].26) Three times with 'And with one...' (AV 7.4.1).

41.s: udapātreṇa saṃpātavatā saṃprokṣyāmapātraṃ tripāde aśmānam avadhāyāpsu nidadhāti
41.d: उदपात्रेण संपातवता संप्रोक्ष्यामपात्रं त्रिपादे अश्मानम् अवधायाप्सु निदधाति

41.s: ayaṃ te yonir ā no bhara dhītī vā ity artham utthāsyann upadadhīta
41.d: अयं ते योनिर् आ नो भर धीती वा इत्य् अर्थम् उत्थास्यन्न् उपदधीत

41.s: udbhindatīṃ saṃjayantīm yathā vṛkṣam aśanir idam ugrāya iti vāsitān akṣān nivapati
41.d: उद्भिन्दतीं संजयन्तीम् यथा वृक्षम् अशनिर् इदम् उग्राय इति वासितान् अक्षान् निवपति

41.s: ambayo yanty śaṃbhumayobhū hiraṇyavarṇāḥ yad adaḥ punantu mā sasruṣīs himavataḥ pra sravanti vāyoḥ pūtaḥ pavitreṇa śaṃ ca no mayaś ca no anaḍudbhyas tvaṃ prathamaṃ mahyam āpo vaiśvānaro raśmibhir ity abhivarṣaṇāvasecanānām
41.d: अम्बयो यन्त्य् शंभुमयोभू हिरण्यवर्णाः यद् अदः पुनन्तु मा सस्रुषीस् हिमवतः प्र स्रवन्ति वायोः पूतः पवित्रेण शं च नो मयश् च नो अनडुद्भ्यस् त्वं प्रथमं मह्यम् आपो वैश्वानरो रश्मिभिर् इत्य् अभिवर्षणावसेचनानाम्

41.s: vatsaṃ saṃdhāvya gomūtreṇāvasicya triḥ pariṇīya upacṛtati
41.d: वत्सं संधाव्य गोमूत्रेणावसिच्य त्रिः परिणीय उपचृतति

41.s: vātaraṃhā iti snāte aśve saṃpātān abhyatinayati
41.d: वातरंहा इति स्नाते अश्वे संपातान् अभ्यतिनयति

42.m:
[42].1) With 'From good [to better]' (AVŚ 7.8.1), one about to set out on a journey should place [the ritual sticks].
[42].2) He murmurs [the hymn].
[42].3) Having besprinkled the vehicle, he unyokes it.
[42].4) He lifts up the property with the residue of oblations.
[42].5) Having wiped it off, he holds it.
[42].6) With 'Both of you conquered' (AVŚ 7.44.1), [he performs the rite of] concord with both having wet feet.
[42].7) Having brought the two [parties] to settle facing west from the settlements by means of a vehicle, he hands it over.
[42].8) Having returned and taken firewood sticks, coming with 'Bearing nourishment' (AVŚ 7.60.1) without forming a mental intention, he places them once.
[42].9) With 'The Ṛc, the Sāman' (AVŚ 7.54.1), he makes an offering of the after-recitation rite.
[42].10) With the two 'joined' verses, [he makes] the third [offering].
[42].11) The fourth [offering] is to Anumati.
[42].12) And this is the sacrifice of both the rite of return and the rite of completion.
[42].13) With 'Divine waters' (AVŚ 7.89.1 / 10.5.46), one whose vow has expired consecrates pacifying water at the edge of the water.
[42].14) At sunset, approaching with firewood in hand, he places the firewood sticks, except for the third.
[42].15) With 'To the Idāvatsara' (PS 19.51.1–4), he should sacrifice ghee as the release from the vow.
[42].16) He should put the firewood sticks on [the fire].
[42].17) With 'To Idāvatsara, to Parivatsara, to Saṃvatsara we announce this; what offense we committed during our vows, with that defilement we smear our enemy. What vow of mine was corrupted, O lord of vows, may day and night make that whole for me; may the moon rising in the east be the healer, may the sun with its rays commend this. What vow was transgressed intentionally, with the mind, with the heart, may the Ādityas, the Rudras, and the Vasus kindle that in me. I undertake vows to Agni, the lord of vows; may he grant me splendor, high fame, and long life' (PS 19.51.1–4), he places the vow-completing [sticks].
[42].18) For three nights, eating without salt and pungent food, he observes the vow of one who has bathed.
[42].19) With 'Drive away the sign of misfortune' (AVŚ 1.18.1), verse by verse, he sprinkles the face of a woman having signs of ill-luck from the tuft of hair on the right.
[42].20) Having offered the chaff with a palāśa leaf, he brings back the remainder.
[42].21) He places the chaff, husks, chaff-dust, and shavings under her left heel.
[42].22) With the two hymns of expulsion and repelling, looking at her, he mutters in response.
[42].23) With 'For long life' (AVŚ 2.4.1), he binds [an amulet] as specified in the mantra.

42.s: āyātaḥ samidha ādāya ūrjaṃ bibhrad ity asaṃkalpayann etya sakṛd ādadhāti
42.d: आयातः समिध आदाय ऊर्जं बिभ्रद् इत्य् असंकल्पयन्न् एत्य सकृद् आदधाति

42.s: āpo divyā iti paryavetavrata udakānte śāntyudakam abhimantrayate
42.d: आपो दिव्या इति पर्यवेतव्रत उदकान्ते शान्त्युदकम् अभिमन्त्रयते

42.s: astamite samitpāṇir etya tṛtīyavarjaṃ samidha ādadhāti
42.d: अस्तमिते समित्पाणिर् एत्य तृतीयवर्जं समिध आदधाति

42.s: idāvatsarāya parivatsarāya saṃvatsarāya prati vedayāma enat | yad vrateṣu duritaṃ nijagmimo durhārdaṃ tena śamalenāñjmaḥ || yan me vrataṃ vratapate lulobhāhorātre sam adhātāṃ ma enat | udyan purastād bhiṣag astu candramāḥ sūryo raśmibhir abhi gṛṇātv enat || yad vratam atipede cittyā manasā hṛdā | ādityā rudrās tan mayi vasavaś ca sam indhatām || vratāni vratapataya upā karomy agnaye | sa me dyumnaṃ bṛhad yaśo dīrgham āyuḥ kṛṇotu me || iti vratasamāpanīr ādadhāti
42.d: इदावत्सराय परिवत्सराय संवत्सराय प्रति वेदयाम एनत् । यद् व्रतेषु दुरितं निजग्मिमो दुर्हार्दं तेन शमलेनाञ्ज्मः ॥ यन् मे व्रतं व्रतपते लुलोभाहोरात्रे सम् अधातां म एनत् । उद्यन् पुरस्ताद् भिषग् अस्तु चन्द्रमाः सूर्यो रश्मिभिर् अभि गृणात्व् एनत् ॥ यद् व्रतम् अतिपेदे चित्त्या मनसा हृदा । आदित्या रुद्रास् तन् मयि वसवश् च सम् इन्धताम् ॥ व्रतानि व्रतपतय उपा करोम्य् अग्नये । स मे द्युम्नं बृहद् यशो दीर्घम् आयुः कृणोतु मे ॥ इति व्रतसमापनीर् आदधाति

42.s: nir lakṣmyaṃ iti pāpalakṣaṇāyā mukham ukṣati anvṛcaṃ dakṣiṇāt keśastukāt
42.d: निर् लक्ष्म्यं इति पापलक्षणाया मुखम् उक्षति अन्वृचं दक्षिणात् केशस्तुकात्

43.s: karśaphasya iti piśaṅgasūtram araludaṇḍaṃ yad āyudham
43.d: कर्शफस्य इति पिशङ्गसूत्रम् अरलुदण्डं यद् आयुधम्
43.m:
[43].1) With 'Of Karśapha' (AVŚ 3.9.1), [he uses] a reddish-brown thread, a staff of aralu wood, and whatever weapon [is prescribed].
[43].2) He fumigates [the patient] with grain chaff.
[43].3) With 'Across the deserts' (AVŚ 7.41.1), [is performed] the sacrifice for settling, dwelling, attending, and moving beyond.
[43].4) With verses relating to the lord of the homestead, he brings the ritual equipment to the south of the fire on ground plowed with a kulija.
[43].5) He adds [the verses] relating to the lord of the homestead, etc., into the Great Pacification.
[43].6) In the central pit, he scatters rice and barley upon darbha grass.
[43].7) In the others, pacifying water, young sprouts of grass, and gravel.
[43].8) With 'Right here, steadfast' (AVŚ 3.12.1), he recites over [the house] being measured and being erected.
[43].9) Having anointed [the pillar], with 'By cosmic order' (AVŚ 3.12.6), [he performs] what is stated in the mantra.
[43].10) With 'Full, O woman' (AVŚ 3.12.8), taking a water jar and the fire, they enter.
[43].11) With the two 'firm' verses, he firms [the dwelling].
[43].12) With the two 'beneficent' verses, he sprinkles it around.
[43].13) With 'O Lord of the homestead, recognize us; be an easy entrance for us, free from disease. What we ask of you, favor that for us; introduce our four-footed and two-footed [beings] here' (PS 7.6.10), and 'Free from disease, O Lord of the homestead, entering all forms, be our very kind friend' (PS 20.23.2), he offers boiled rice with milk to the Lord of the homestead.
[43].14) He feeds the Brahmins all kinds of food,
[43].15) [and provides] auspicious items.
[43].16) With 'Which fires' (AVŚ 3.21.1–7), with the formula 'unharmed by flesh-eating fire', he binds on a palāśa [amulet].
[43].17) He offers an oblation.
[43].18) He lays on [firewood sticks].
[43].19) Having fetched barley with water into a water pot by means of a ladle, [he takes] a handful.
[43].20) With 'Which fires' (AVŚ 3.21.1), having stirred the porridge with a ladle made of palāśa wood by means of two stirring sticks made of kāmpīla wood,
[43].21) and [he performs] the pacification.

43.s: vāstoṣpatīyaiḥ kulijakṛṣṭe dakṣiṇato agneḥ saṃbhāram āharati
43.d: वास्तोष्पतीयैः कुलिजकृष्टे दक्षिणतो अग्नेः संभारम् आहरति

43.s: ihaiva dhruvāṃ ity mīyamānām ucchrīyamāṇām anumantrayate
43.d: इहैव ध्रुवां इत्य् मीयमानाम् उच्छ्रीयमाणाम् अनुमन्त्रयते

43.s: pūrṇaṃ nāri ity udakumbham agnim ādāya prapadyante
43.d: पूर्णं नारि इत्य् उदकुम्भम् अग्निम् आदाय प्रपद्यन्ते

43.s: vāstoṣ pate prati jānīhy asmān svāveśo anamīvo na edhi | yat tvemahe prati nas taj juṣasva catuṣpado dvipada ā veśayeha || anamīvo vāstoṣ pate viśvā rūpāṇy āviśan | sakhā suśeva edhi naḥ || iti vāstoṣpataye kṣīraudanasya juhoti
43.d: वास्तोष् पते प्रति जानीह्य् अस्मान् स्वावेशो अनमीवो न एधि । यत् त्वेमहे प्रति नस् तज् जुषस्व चतुष्पदो द्विपद आ वेशयेह ॥ अनमीवो वास्तोष् पते विश्वा रूपाण्य् आविशन् । सखा सुशेव एधि नः ॥ इति वास्तोष्पतये क्षीरौदनस्य जुहोति

43.s: ye agnayo iti kravyādanupahata iti palāśaṃ badhnāti
43.d: ये अग्नयो इति क्रव्यादनुपहत इति पलाशं बध्नाति

43.s: udañcanena udapātryāṃ yavān adbhir ānīya ullopam
43.d: उदञ्चनेन उदपात्र्यां यवान् अद्भिर् आनीय उल्लोपम्

43.s: ye agnayo iti pālāśyā darvyā mantham upamathya kāmpīlībhyām upamanthanībhyām
43.d: ये अग्नयो इति पालाश्या दर्व्या मन्थम् उपमथ्य काम्पीलीभ्याम् उपमन्थनीभ्याम्

44.m:
[44].1) With "He who gives breath" [AV 4.2.1] [is performed] the pacification of a barren cow.
[44].2) He holds [her] west of the fire, facing west.
[44].3) Having sat down to the west of the fire, facing east, he prepares pacifying water for her while she is held in touch.
[44].4) In that [procedure] he applies this hymn.
[44].5) With it, he makes her sip water and besprinkles her.
[44].6) Standing, he recites the Great Pacification loudly over her as she stands.
[44].7) Having made an oblation with "He who rules as lord of beasts over beasts" [AV 2.34.1], he anoints the barren cow on the head, the hump, and the rump region.
[44].8) He anoints one of the two edges of the knife.
[44].9) With the anointed [edge] he digs out the omentum.
[44].10) On her right flank, he lays down [the knife] with two blades of darbha grass, with "Pleasing to such-and-such [deity] art thou," according to the deity.
[44].11) With "Out from the dwelling" [AV 2.14.1], he carries a firebrand counter-clockwise three times around [her], not carrying it around himself.
[44].12) He takes hold of her with two blades of darbha grass.
[44].13) West of the fire, to the north, he pins her down with her head to the west and feet to the north.
[44].14) With "Be united with this one's body," he casts down one of the two darbha blades.
[44].15) Then he settles the vital breaths with "Knowing" [AV 2.34.5].
[44].16) Standing to the south, he murmurs the demon-slaying [mantra].
[44].17) When she is suffocated, he offers an oblation with "If the barren cow made a cry, or struck her breast with her feet, may Agni release me from that sin, from every distress!"
[44].18) Approaching with a water vessel, the sacrificer's wife washes the limbs, beginning with the mouth:
[44].19) With "Cleanse thy mouth, [the portion] of the deity's sacrifice;"
[44].20) the two nostrils with "[Cleanse thy] breaths;"
[44].21) the two eyes with "[Cleanse thy] sight;"
[44].22) the two ears with "[Cleanse thy] hearing;"
[44].23) with "Whatsoever of thee is raw, whatsoever is stationary," [she washes] all around the place of the halter;
[44].24) with "[Cleanse thy] feet," collecting [water] from the foot;
[44].25) the navel with "[Cleanse thy] navel;"
[44].26) the penis [or vulva] with "[Cleanse thy] generative organ;"
[44].27) the anus with "[Cleanse thy] anus."
[44].28) With "Whatsoever of thee is raw, whatsoever is stationary, cleanse that," having poured out the remaining [water] on the side region, she goes away according to her purpose.
[44].29) Taking the two omentum-spits, ghee, the dipping spoon, the knife, and a blade of darbha grass, and approaching, having turned [the cow] on her back, he spreads darbha grass with the grain on the navel region.
[44].30) With "O plant, protect him; o knife, do not harm him," he hands over the slaughtering knife.
[44].31) Having severed [it] with "Here I cut off the in-breath and out-breath of descendant-of-so-and-so, son-of-so-and-so,"
[44].32) having struck away the lower incision of blood,
[44].33) he buries [it] in the mouth with "Here I bury the in-breath and out-breath of descendant-of-so-and-so, son-of-so-and-so."
[44].34) Having covered the two omentum-spits with the omentum with "Cover, O Heaven and Earth, with the omentum,"
[44].35) cutting around and extracting [it] with the knife,
[44].36) having basted the cut with ghee,
[44].37) he casts the tip of the darbha grass [into the fire] with "O Vāyu, partake of the drops!"
[44].38) With "Scorched is the demon," he sets the boiled oblation down on the charcoal.
[44].39) With "May divine Savitṛ cook thee," he cooks it.
[44].40) He makes it well-cooked.

44.s: paścād agneḥ prāṅmukha upaviśyānvārabdhāyai śāntyudakaṃ karoti
44.d: पश्चाद् अग्नेः प्राङ्मुख उपविश्यान्वारब्धायै शान्त्युदकं करोति

44.s: tena enām ācāmayati ca saṃprokṣati ca
44.d: तेन एनाम् आचामयति च संप्रोक्षति च

44.s: ya īśe paśupatiḥ paśūnām iti hutvā vaśām anakti śirasi kakude jaghanadeśe
44.d: य ईशे पशुपतिः पशूनाम् इति हुत्वा वशाम् अनक्ति शिरसि ककुदे जघनदेशे

44.s: dakṣiṇe pārśve darbhābhyām adhikṣipati amuṣmai tvā juṣṭam iti yathādevatam
44.d: दक्षिणे पार्श्वे दर्भाभ्याम् अधिक्षिपति अमुष्मै त्वा जुष्टम् इति यथादेवतम्

44.s: nissālām ity ulmukena triḥ prasavyaṃ pariharati anabhipariharan ātmānam
44.d: निस्सालाम् इत्य् उल्मुकेन त्रिः प्रसव्यं परिहरति अनभिपरिहरन् आत्मानम्

44.s: paścād uttarato agneḥ pratyakśīrṣīm udakpādīṃ nividhyati
44.d: पश्चाद् उत्तरतो अग्नेः प्रत्यक्शीर्षीम् उदक्पादीं निविध्यति

44.s: sam asyai tanvā bhava ity anyataraṃ darbham avāsyati
44.d: सम् अस्यै तन्वा भव इत्य् अन्यतरं दर्भम् अवास्यति

44.s: saṃjñaptāyāṃ juhoti yad vaśā māyum akratoro vā paḍbhir āhata | agnir mā tasmād enaso viśvān muñcatv aṃhasaḥ iti
44.d: संज्ञप्तायां जुहोति यद् वशा मायुम् अक्रतोरो वा पड्भिर् आहत । अग्निर् मा तस्माद् एनसो विश्वान् मुञ्चत्व् अंहसः इति

44.s: udapātreṇa patnī abhivrajya mukhādīni gātrāṇi prakṣālayate
44.d: उदपात्रेण पत्नी अभिव्रज्य मुखादीनि गात्राणि प्रक्षालयते

44.s: yat te krūraṃ yad āsthitaṃ iti samantaṃ rajjudhānam
44.d: यत् ते क्रूरं यद् आस्थितं इति समन्तं रज्जुधानम्

44.s: yat te krūraṃ yad āsthitaṃ tac chundhasva iti avaśiṣṭāḥ pārśvadeśe avasicya yathārthaṃ vrajati
44.d: यत् ते क्रूरं यद् आस्थितं तच् छुन्धस्व इति अवशिष्टाः पार्श्वदेशे अवसिच्य यथार्थं व्रजति

44.s: vapāśrapaṇyau ājyaṃ sruvaṃ svadhitiṃ darbham ādāyābhivrajya uttānāṃ parivartyānulomaṃ nābhideśe darbham āstṛṇāti
44.d: वपाश्रपण्यौ आज्यं स्रुवं स्वधितिं दर्भम् आदायाभिव्रज्य उत्तानां परिवर्त्यानुलोमं नाभिदेशे दर्भम् आस्तृणाति

44.s: oṣadhe trāyasvainaṃ svadhite mainaṃ hiṃsīḥ iti śastraṃ prayachati
44.d: ओषधे त्रायस्वैनं स्वधिते मैनं हिंसीः इति शस्त्रं प्रयछति

44.s: idam aham āmuṣyāyaṇasyāmuṣyāḥ putrasya prāṇāpānāv apakṛntāmīty apakṛtya
44.d: इदम् अहम् आमुष्यायणस्यामुष्याः पुत्रस्य प्राणापानाव् अपकृन्तामीत्य् अपकृत्य

44.s: idam aham āmuṣyāyaṇasyāmuṣyāḥ putrasya prāṇāpānau nikhanāmīty āsye nikhanati
44.d: इदम् अहम् आमुष्यायणस्यामुष्याः पुत्रस्य प्राणापानौ निखनामीत्य् आस्ये निखनति

44.s: vapayā dyāvāpṛthivī prorṇuvāthām iti vapāśrapaṇyau vapayā prachādya
44.d: वपया द्यावापृथिवी प्रोर्णुवाथाम् इति वपाश्रपण्यौ वपया प्रछाद्य

44.s: vāyo ve stokānām iti darbhāgraṃ prāsyati
44.d: वायो वे स्तोकानाम् इति दर्भाग्रं प्रास्यति

44.s: pratyuṣṭaṃ rakṣaḥ iti carum aṅgāre nidadhāti
44.d: प्रत्युष्टं रक्षः इति चरुम् अङ्गारे निदधाति

44.s: devas tvā savitā śrapayatu iti śrapayati
44.d: देवस् त्वा सविता श्रपयतु इति श्रपयति

45.s: yadi aṣṭāpadī syād garbhamañjalau sahiraṇyaṃ sayavaṃ vā ya ātmadā iti khadāyāṃ tryaratnau agnau sakṛt juhoti
45.d: यदि अष्टापदी स्याद् गर्भमञ्जलौ सहिरण्यं सयवं वा य आत्मदा इति खदायां त्र्यरत्नौ अग्नौ सकृत् जुहोति
45.m:
[45].1) If she should have eight feet [i.e., be pregnant], taking the embryo in his folded hands with gold or with barley, with "He who gives breath" [AV 4.2.1], he offers it once into the fire in a pit measuring three cubits.
[45].2) Having butchered [the animal], he should cut off the portions cut from all parts.
[45].3) "The heart, tongue, and breast, the two forelegs, and the two flanks: these are six. The liver, two kidneys, rectum, and two haunches: these are the eleven portions belonging to the deities."
[45].4) "The right side of the head, the left haunch, and the rectum: these three are the triple limb, the share for Agni Sviṣṭakṛt alone."
[45].5) Having cut that off, he should cook the designated portions.
[45].6) When about to offer, he should cut twice each for the deities;
[45].7) once each for the portions belonging to Sviṣṭakṛt.
[45].8) From the omentum, he offers oblations with "Kindled" [AV 5.12.1] and "Upright are his [rays]" [AV 5.27.1].
[45].9) With the two yoked [verses], the third [oblation].
[45].10) With [a verse] addressed to Anumati, the fourth.
[45].11) [With] "O Jātavedas, go to the gods with the omentum, for thou becamest the first Hotṛ priest! O Agni, be united with the body of ghee; may the desires of the sacrificer be true, svāhā!"
[45].12) With "Go to the loftiest vault of heaven," he throws the two omentum-spits [into the fire]:
[45].13) the single-pronged one toward the east, the double-pronged one toward the west.
[45].14) With "Carry the omentum, O Jātavedas, to the ancestors where thou knowest them deposited in the distance; let streams of fat flow to them; may their blessings and desires be true, svāhā svadhā!", he offers three times from the omentum;
[45].15) [then oblations] from the portions cut from all parts;
[45].16) from the cooked pot-oblation, he offers with "A sovereign art thou, whose name is cooking; may I master all quarters among my friends! Desire art thou; for desire I offer thee, for one having all heroes, all men, all troops, all desires! May Anumati favour us today, Pūṣan, and great Sarasvatī! What I perform, may that prosper; to Anumati svāhā!"
[45].17) With "Who gave this to whom?" [AV 3.29.7-8], "Desire in the beginning" [AV 19.52.1], "Whatever food" [AV 6.71.1], and "May my power return to me" [AV 7.67.1], he accepts [the gift].
[45].18) The last [verse fulfills] all desires.
[45].19) By means of the barren cow, the cooked sacrifices are explained.

45.s: hṛdayaṃ jihvā śyenaś ca doṣī pārśve ca tāni ṣaṭ | yakṛdvṛkkau gudaśroṇī tāny ekādaśa daivatāni |
45.d: हृदयं जिह्वा श्येनश् च दोषी पार्श्वे च तानि षट् । यकृद्वृक्कौ गुदश्रोणी तान्य् एकादश दैवतानि ।

45.s: dakṣiṇaḥ kapilalāṭaḥ savyā śroṇir gudaś ca yaḥ | etāni trīṇi tryaṅgāni sviṣṭakṛdbhāga eva |
45.d: दक्षिणः कपिललाटः सव्या श्रोणिर् गुदश् च यः । एतानि त्रीणि त्र्यङ्गानि स्विष्टकृद्भाग एव ।

45.s: vapāyāḥ samiddho ūrdhvā asya iti juhoti
45.d: वपायाः समिद्धो ऊर्ध्वा अस्य इति जुहोति

45.s: jātavedo vapayā gacha devāṃs tvaṃ hi hotā prathamo babhūtha | ghṛtasyāgne tanvā saṃ bhava satyāḥ santu yajamānasya kāmāḥ svāhā |
45.d: जातवेदो वपया गछ देवांस् त्वं हि होता प्रथमो बभूथ । घृतस्याग्ने तन्वा सं भव सत्याः सन्तु यजमानस्य कामाः स्वाहा ।

45.s: vaha vapāṃ jātavedaḥ pitṛbhyo yatraitān vettha nihitān parāke | medasaḥ kulyā upa tān sravantu satyā eṣām āśiṣaḥ santu kāmāḥ svāhā svadhā iti vapāyās trir juhoti
45.d: वह वपां जातवेदः पितृभ्यो यत्रैतान् वेत्थ निहितान् पराके । मेदसः कुल्या उप तान् स्रवन्तु सत्या एषाम् आशिषः सन्तु कामाः स्वाहा स्वधा इति वपायास् त्रिर् जुहोति

45.s: sthālīpākasya samrāḍ asy adhiśrayaṇaṃ nāma sakhīnām abhy ahaṃ viśvā āśāḥ sākṣīya | kāmo 'si kāmāya tvā sarvavīrāya sarvapuruṣāya sarvagaṇāya sarvakāmāya juhomi | anv adya no 'numatiḥ pūṣā sarasvatī mahī | yat karomi tad ṛdhyatām anumataye svāhā iti juhoti
45.d: स्थालीपाकस्य सम्राड् अस्य् अधिश्रयणं नाम सखीनाम् अभ्य् अहं विश्वा आशाः साक्षीय । कामो ऽसि कामाय त्वा सर्ववीराय सर्वपुरुषाय सर्वगणाय सर्वकामाय जुहोमि । अन्व् अद्य नो ऽनुमतिः पूषा सरस्वती मही । यत् करोमि तद् ऋध्यताम् अनुमतये स्वाहा इति जुहोति

45.s: ka idaṃ kasmā adāt kāmas tad agre yad annam punar maitv indriyaṃ iti pratigṛhṇāti
45.d: क इदं कस्मा अदात् कामस् तद् अग्रे यद् अन्नम् पुनर् मैत्व् इन्द्रियं इति प्रतिगृह्णाति

46.s: utāmṛtāsur śivās ta ity abhyākhyātāya prayachati
46.d: उतामृतासुर् शिवास् त इत्य् अभ्याख्याताय प्रयछति
46.m:
[46].1) With the mantras, "Even though his life is immortal..." [AV 5.1.7] and "Auspicious to you..." [AV 7.43.1], he hands [the oblation] over to the accused.
[46].2) He ties the head of a wooden mallet with a rope.
[46].3) [An effigy] corresponding [to the body] made of palāśa wood, iron, copper, and gold [is prepared].
[46].4) With the mantra, "By which Soma..." [AV 6.7.1], one who intends to perform a sacrifice for someone eats [the milk of] a cow with a calf of identical appearance.
[46].5) At the conclusion, he offers sacrifice.
[46].6) With the mantras, "Whom I ask..." [AV 5.7.5] and "What by wish..." [AV 7.57.1], [one performs the rite] when intending to solicit [gifts].
[46].7) For the birds that have fallen [or perched], he performs the Mahāśānti rite with the mantras mentioned, "O gods, the pigeon..." [AV 6.27.1], "With the verse, the pigeon..." [AV 6.28.1], and "Their missile..." [AV 6.29.1].
[46].8) With the verse, "Around this fire..." [AV 6.28.2], taking fire and a cow, the patron having it performed leads them three times around the dwelling at night.
[46].9) Having seen a bad dream, he wipes his face with the mantras, "Go far away..." [AV 6.45.1] and "He who is not living..." [AV 6.46.1].
[46].10) Having seen an exceedingly terrible [dream], he deposits a sacrificial cake of mixed grain in another direction.
[46].11) With the mantra, "I turn around..." [AV 7.100.1], he turns around [in bed].
[46].12) Having eaten, he looks around with the mantra, "What in a dream..." [AV 7.101.1].
[46].13) The mantra, "We know you, O dream..." [AV 6.46.2], is the concluding formula for all [bad dream rites].
[46].14) With the mantra, "Indeed not your bodies, O Agni..." [AV 6.49.1], a vedic student, having built up a fire at the teacher's cremation ground, having circumambulated it three times, offers a sacrificial cake.
[46].15) He should lie down for three nights without turning around.
[46].16) He should not lie down close [to the fire], so says Kauśika.
[46].17) He should bathe with the bathing [verses].
[46].18) One whose vow is uninfringed should re-enter [the student's duties].
[46].19) Fastening a rope of darbha grass on a student who has broken his vow of chastity, he scatters [grains into the fire] with the mantra, "What to you, O divine..." [AV 6.63.1].
[46].20) Likewise, having poured [water] over him with a water vessel containing the residue of oblations,
[46].21) having besprinkled with pacifying water the [items] mentioned in the mantra,
[46].22) [he makes an offering] on a fire that has ignited on its own with the mantra, "Kindled together..." [AV 6.63.4].
[46].23) With the mantra, "Agni wards off the demons..." [AV 8.3.26], [he addresses Agni] warding off.
[46].24) Failing to deliver a commission, [he recites] with the mantra, "What through forgetfulness..." [AV 7.106.1].
[46].25) For one born under an inauspicious lunar mansion, [he performs a rite] with the Mūla plant, with the mantra, "Ancient indeed..." [AV 6.110.1].
[46].26) For the elder brother who remains unmarried while the younger has married and for the younger brother who marries before the elder, having bound them at the joints with muñja cords at the water's edge, he bathes them with bunches of grass with the mantras, "Do not the eldest..." [AV 6.112.1] and "In Trita, the gods..." [AV 6.113.1].
[46].27) He pours water down [upon them].
[46].28) Placing the upper bonds onto the foam [of the water], he sets them afloat with the mantra, "The foams of the rivers..." [AV 6.113.2c].
[46].29) And entering [the water], [he recites] with all the waters-hymns.
[46].30) With the hymn on the anger of the gods [AV 6.114], [he offers] what is mentioned in the mantra.
[46].31) [He gives a fee] to the teacher.
[46].32) He should place [the offering upon the bed].
[46].33) He scatters [offerings] for one lying in a ditch.
[46].34) He sacrifices to Yama, son of Vivasvat.
[46].35) He gives a four-cup portion [of food].
[46].36) If a creditor has died, he gives [the debt-payment] to his offspring.
[46].37) [Or] to one of the same gotra.
[46].38) He scatters it at the cremation ground.
[46].39) And at a crossroads.
[46].40) He kindles brushwood.
[46].41) With the mantra, "From the sky now to me..." [AV 6.124.1], he washes off drops from a clear sky.
[46].42) He touches the [body parts] mentioned in the mantra.
[46].43) For a child whose upper teeth appear first, he scatters [grains into the fire] with the mantra, "Which two tigers..." [AV 6.140.1].
[46].44) He causes him to bite the [substances] mentioned in the mantra.
[46].45) He feeds the designated [foods] boiled in pacifying water.
[46].46) And the two parents [eat as well].
[46].47) What has been soiled by a black bird he washes with the mantra, "This which the black..." [AV 7.64.1].
[46].48) What has been wiped he carries fire around.
[46].49) With the mantra, "Having backward-turned fruit..." [AV 7.65.1], he places apāmārga plants onto apāmārga kindling wood.
[46].50) With the mantra, "Whatever is downward..." [AV 10.5.22], he sips water.
[46].51) With the mantra, "What of you, O Earth..." [AV 12.1.35], he digs out [earth].
[46].52) With the mantra, "What of you is deficient..." [AV 12.1.61c], he fills it back up.
[46].53) With the verses, "Go forth, strike out..." [PS 20.50.5–7 etc.], the auspicious chants concerning the francolin partridge take place.
[46].54) "Go forth, strike out or... the forest fires for the well-being of our houses; / O hundred-feathered francolin, call out to us auspiciously on the right. // Speak auspiciously from the right, speak auspiciously from the north; / speak auspiciously from the front to us, auspiciously from behind, O francolin. // Call fortune from the right, call fortune from the north; / call fortune from the front to us, fortune from behind, O francolin. // Call fortune with sons, call fortune in the homes; / call fortune for us, call us security. // Calling out, O bird, call out good fortune; sitting quietly, observe our good intention; / when flying up you call like a lute, may we speak aloud in the assembly, blessed with heroic men. // You magnify youthful strengths like a drum of the victors; / O hundred-feathered francolin, call out to us auspiciously on the right." — these are the auspicious chants concerning the francolin partridge.
[46].55) With the mantra, "You who, turning brownish, eat the sleeping man lying down, moving without feet: / may Varuṇa encircle us with an iron sacred formulation, with a stony coat of mail" [PS 20.9.4], he lies down in the open air, he lies down in the open air.

46.s: yena soma iti yājayiṣyan sārūpavatsam aśnāti
46.d: येन सोम इति याजयिष्यन् सारूपवत्सम् अश्नाति

46.s: yaṃ yācāmy yad āśasā iti yāciṣyan
46.d: यं याचाम्य् यद् आशसा इति याचिष्यन्

46.s: mantroktāni patitebhyo devāḥ kapota ṛcā kapotaṃ amūn hetiḥ iti mahāśāntim āvapate
46.d: मन्त्रोक्तानि पतितेभ्यो देवाः कपोत ऋचा कपोतं अमून् हेतिः इति महाशान्तिम् आवपते

46.s: parīme 'gnim ity agniṃ gām ādāya niśi kārayamāṇas triḥ śālāṃ pariṇayati
46.d: परीमे ऽग्निम् इत्य् अग्निं गाम् आदाय निशि कारयमाणस् त्रिः शालां परिणयति

46.s: paro 'pehi yo na jīvo iti svapnaṃ dṛṣṭvā mukhaṃ vimārṣṭi
46.d: परो ऽपेहि यो न जीवो इति स्वप्नं दृष्ट्वा मुखं विमार्ष्टि

46.s: atighoraṃ dṛṣṭvā maiśradhānyaṃ puroḍāśam anyāśāyāṃ vā nidadhāti
46.d: अतिघोरं दृष्ट्वा मैश्रधान्यं पुरोडाशम् अन्याशायां वा निदधाति

46.s: vidma te svapna iti sarveṣām apyayaḥ
46.d: विद्म ते स्वप्न इति सर्वेषाम् अप्ययः

46.s: nahi te agne tanvaḥ iti brahmacārī ācāryasyādahana upasamādhāya triḥ parikramya puroḍāśaṃ juhoti
46.d: नहि ते अग्ने तन्वः इति ब्रह्मचारी आचार्यस्यादहन उपसमाधाय त्रिः परिक्रम्य पुरोडाशं जुहोति

46.s: avakīrṇine darbhaśulbam āsajya yat te devī iti āvapati
46.d: अवकीर्णिने दर्भशुल्बम् आसज्य यत् ते देवी इति आवपति

46.s: pratno hi iti pāpanakṣatre jātāya mūlena
46.d: प्रत्नो हि इति पापनक्षत्रे जाताय मूलेन

46.s: mā jyeṣṭhaṃ tṛte devā iti parivittiparivividānau udakānte mauñjaiḥ parvasu baddhvā piñjūlībhir āplāvayati
46.d: मा ज्येष्ठं तृते देवा इति परिवित्तिपरिविविदानौ उदकान्ते मौञ्जैः पर्वसु बद्ध्वा पिञ्जूलीभिर् आप्लावयति

46.s: pheneṣūttarān pāśān ādhāya nadīnāṃ phenān iti praplāvayati
46.d: फेनेषूत्तरान् पाशान् आधाय नदीनां फेनान् इति प्रप्लावयति

46.s: divo nu mām iti vīdhrabindūn prakṣālayati
46.d: दिवो नु माम् इति वीध्रबिन्दून् प्रक्षालयति

46.s: yasya uttamadantau pūrvau jāyete yau vyāghrāv ity āvapati
46.d: यस्य उत्तमदन्तौ पूर्वौ जायेते यौ व्याघ्राव् इत्य् आवपति

46.s: idaṃ yat kṛṣṇaḥ iti kṛṣṇaśakuninādhikṣiptaṃ prakṣālayati
46.d: इदं यत् कृष्णः इति कृष्णशकुनिनाधिक्षिप्तं प्रक्षालयति

46.s: prehi pra hara iti kāpiñjalāni svastyayanāni bhavanti
46.d: प्रेहि प्र हर इति कापिञ्जलानि स्वस्त्ययनानि भवन्ति

46.s: prehi pra hara vā dāvān gṛhebhyaḥ svastaye | kapiñjala pradakṣiṇaṃ śatapattrābhi no vada || bhadraṃ vada dakṣiṇato bhadram uttarato vada | bhadraṃ purastān no vada bhadraṃ paścāt kapiñjala || śunaṃ vada dakṣiṇataḥ śunam uttarato vada | śunaṃ purastān no vada śunaṃ paścāt kapiñjala || bhadraṃ vada putrair bhadraṃ vada gṛheṣu ca | bhadram asmākaṃ vada bhadraṃ no abhayaṃ vada || āvadaṃs tvaṃ śakune bhadram ā vada tūṣṇīm āsīnaḥ sumatiṃ cikiddhi naḥ | yad utpatan vadasi karkarir yathā bṛhad vadema vidathe suvīrāḥ || yauvanāni mahayasi jigyuṣām iva dundubhiḥ | kapiñjala pradakṣiṇaṃ śatapattrābhi no vada || iti kāpiñjalāni svastyayanāni bhavanti
46.d: प्रेहि प्र हर वा दावान् गृहेभ्यः स्वस्तये । कपिञ्जल प्रदक्षिणं शतपत्त्राभि नो वद ॥ भद्रं वद दक्षिणतो भद्रम् उत्तरतो वद । भद्रं पुरस्तान् नो वद भद्रं पश्चात् कपिञ्जल ॥ शुनं वद दक्षिणतः शुनम् उत्तरतो वद । शुनं पुरस्तान् नो वद शुनं पश्चात् कपिञ्जल ॥ भद्रं वद पुत्रैर् भद्रं वद गृहेषु च । भद्रम् अस्माकं वद भद्रं नो अभयं वद ॥ आवदंस् त्वं शकुने भद्रम् आ वद तूष्णीम् आसीनः सुमतिं चिकिद्धि नः । यद् उत्पतन् वदसि कर्करिर् यथा बृहद् वदेम विदथे सुवीराः ॥ यौवनानि महयसि जिग्युषाम् इव दुन्दुभिः । कपिञ्जल प्रदक्षिणं शतपत्त्राभि नो वद ॥ इति कापिञ्जलानि स्वस्त्ययनानि भवन्ति

46.s: yo abhy u babhruṇāyasi svapantam atsi puruṣaṃ śayānam agatsvalam | ayasmayena brahmaṇāśmamayena varmaṇā pary asmān varuṇo dadhat ity abhyavakāśe saṃviśati abhyavakāśe saṃviśati
46.d: यो अभ्य् उ बभ्रुणायसि स्वपन्तम् अत्सि पुरुषं शयानम् अगत्स्वलम् । अयस्मयेन ब्रह्मणाश्ममयेन वर्मणा पर्य् अस्मान् वरुणो दधत् इत्य् अभ्यवकाशे संविशति अभ्यवकाशे संविशति
